en.anleitungen/zwei-faktor.md:
---
key: guide.two_factor
titel: Set up two-factor authentication
routen: [/mein-konto/anmeldung]
reihe: 20
stichworte: [2FA, authenticator, phone, code, TOTP, security]
---

You need an authenticator app on your phone, for example FreeOTP, Aegis or Google Authenticator.

1. Open [Sign-in & security](/mein-konto/anmeldung) under **My account**.
2. In the **Two-factor authentication** section, scan the QR code with the app.
3. Enter the **Code from the app** and **Your password for confirmation**.
4. Click **Activate**.
5. Keep the **Recovery codes** that appear in a safe place, for example printed. Each code
   works once if you don't have your phone.

![The “Two-factor authentication” section with the QR code](bild:konto-zwei-faktor)

Club logo in the app: The QR code contains your club's logo. Some apps such as FreeOTP show it
as the icon. Others, for example Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 2FAS or Aegis, show
the initials instead. In Aegis you can choose your own image for the entry, in 2FAS you can change
the letters and colour. An entry
you already set up only changes when you set up two-factor authentication again.

## Confirming sensitive actions

For some actions HUBIplan asks again for a current code from the app if your last code is
older than 10 minutes: full exports and spin-offs, assigning roles or extending their rights,
resetting another person's two-factor authentication, creating the QR code for the HUBIplan app
and permanent deletion (club, former member, name in the chronicle). A recovery code works too,
and with a passkey set up, the passkey (see “Sign in with a passkey”).
If you have not set up two-factor authentication yet, you confirm with your password during the
transition period.

Platform administration has no transition period: without two-factor authentication its
rights are paused until you set it up here. Anyone else with a permission in a club or
department has 3 days; the deadline is shown at the top of every page. During that time,
circulars, exports and posting in the treasury are already paused, afterwards all permissions.
Your own member area does not need a second factor.
en.seiten/abteilung.md:
---
key: page.department
titel: Sub-unit area
routen: [/abteilung]
stichworte: [platoon, department, area, leader]
---

This is the work area of the sub-unit where you have a role. You see its members, events, documents and invoices as far as your role allows. You switch the area at the top right. Its sub-items (members, development, invoices, offices, entries, export) are in the sidebar, as for every other area.

Under **Offices** you see today’s **Office holders** at the top, and below under “Roles and permissions” what each role of the sub-unit may do: per area _no access_, _read_ or _edit_. If your role may only read roles, you see the rights and who holds which role, but cannot change anything. The same applies to members’ logins: with _read_ you see in the record whether someone has a login, with _edit_ you send login links.

With role “edit” you assign any role under **Office holders** with **Assign**. The dialog can end the predecessor’s term; your own role with role management stays in place.
en.seiten/aufgaben.md:
---
key: page.aufgaben
titel: Tasks
rechte: [todos.view]
routen: [/aufgaben]
stichworte: [Todo, Tasks]
---

In the overview, tasks appear directly below the status controls and filter. “New task” sits beside the heading. Below the list, notices for tasks without a responsible account and incoming tasks from other installations appear only when there are entries, with a count. Loading errors remain visible with a retry action. Adopting the last entry removes its notice. The export action is below the list. Authorised role managers can also open “Administration” there to configure retention of shared tasks. This section is initially collapsed.

Create personal tasks with a title and an optional description and due date. Personal tasks are private. After creation, edits are saved automatically. Completed tasks appear under Done. Deleted tasks can be restored from the trash for 30 days. Export personal tasks downloads your private tasks.

Shared tasks are also visible to selected people or current role holders. View permission allows reading; edit permission also allows changes and completion. Only the responsible account can delete or transfer responsibility. Under My account › Notifications, disable email and push notices when tasks are shared. Authorised role managers can take over orphaned shared tasks when the responsible account permanently loses access; personal tasks remain hidden. The outbox stores only a neutral delivery record for task notices.

Configure email and push under My account › Notifications. For each task with a due date, choose reminder times and channels or disable notices. Responsible participants are reminded; without an assignment, all participants with edit permission are reminded. Date-only deadlines last until the end of the day and reminders arrive at 8 am; timed deadlines use their exact time. Overdue tasks receive exactly one additional notice at 8 am the next day. Highlighting in HUBIplan remains active independently of email and push. Optionally move completed one-off tasks to the trash after twelve months; this is off by default. Recurring task history is excluded. In your profile, personal tasks can still be exported or permanently deleted after a role ends.

Under Attachments, upload multiple files by selecting them or dropping them in the upload area. Each file may be up to 20 MB; the document repository’s file types and safety checks apply. Restore removed attachments from the attachment trash for 30 days. Document links grant no additional repository permissions: without access, only a placeholder appears. The personal export downloads a ZIP file with tasks, settings and authorised files, including your private tasks after a role ends.

Under Repeat, choose daily, weekly, monthly or yearly occurrences with an interval and an optional end date or total count. Completing a task creates exactly one next occurrence. Month-end dates and 29 February retain their original anchor; late completion skips past due dates. Choose whether the interval starts from the previous due date or from completion. Content changes can apply only to this occurrence or to all following ones. Document links and personal reminder rules are inherited; uploaded files are not. Reopening or undoing an occurrence may retract its successor only while it is untouched. End series keeps an existing open occurrence; the series trash deletes and restores the entire history without creating an extra occurrence.

For recurring tasks, Transfer responsibility applies to the entire shared history and future continuation. If earlier private occurrences remain, the transfer is rejected to protect their contents; review their sharing permissions explicitly first.

Use Target unit to share with allowed neighbouring levels on the same instance. Add same-named roles explicitly for the displayed units; units added later are not included automatically. A shared task is completed once for everyone. With a separate occurrence for each unit, each target unit owns its own copy and, for recurring tasks, an independent sequence. The distribution mode is fixed after sharing. Local editors manage notes, attachments and participants within their unit. Titles, descriptions and due dates remain controlled centrally. The source receives only progress, including the local occurrence number, due date, completion time and account. Central updates affect open copies while preserving local additions and completed history. Removing a target unit or deleting the source stops future occurrences and access to source attachments; the target unit retains its local data. When it revokes a local share, current permissions also apply to files, undo and reminders. For shared tasks, undo uses the authorised target context.

## Tasks linked to events

Link a task to an event in your own calendar. The event offers links to its tasks and to creating a linked task. The task owner can change or remove the link under “Linked event”. Calendar and task permissions remain independent: linking does not share either object. Without calendar permission, only “Event unavailable” appears. Deleting the event keeps the task and removes its link. Due dates do not move automatically with the event. A recurring event is linked as a whole series, rather than an individual occurrence.

## Member tasks

The responsible account can explicitly select current members under “Share in the member portal” (view only or allowed to complete) or publish an open offer. Current unit members can view an offer; department offers are limited to their members. Exactly one person can claim it, complete it or release an open claim. Every read, change and file download checks current membership, portal access and task publication. Members receive no administration rights and cannot change titles, due dates or participants. Document references grant no additional repository access.

Publication initially applies only to the selected occurrence. Explicitly enabling “Also share following occurrences in the member portal” copies it into future occurrences; offers become available to claim again. Completing and reopening preserve the existing protections for subsequent occurrences. Assigned members allowed to complete, or the member who claimed an offer, receive reminders according to their notification preferences.

Use “My area › Tasks” to view open and completed tasks. Mail and push links select the matching portal access. Revoked access, ended membership or a disabled portal prevents further access.

## Creating tasks

“New task” opens a dialog. “Close” is in a separate dialog header. Enter the title, description, due date and sharing before creating the task. After “Create”, the same dialog stays open for attachments, reminders, recurrence and member access; “Done” closes it. Existing tasks save as usual and unsaved access settings are checked before closing. The description uses a wide, resizable text field. Status and filters share one row on larger screens and wrap on smaller screens.

## Tasks across separate installations

In the task dialog, **Share with another installation** selects a confirmed connection. Enable the task packet in the connection and have the receiving side accept it first. Each task also needs its own explicit grant. New offers appear under **Tasks from other installations** and must be adopted by a responsible local account.

- **Separate copy with independent completion**: Each receiving unit completes independently. The source only sees occurrence, deadline and progress; local notes, additional attachments and account names are not returned. Open copies receive central content changes. Completed copies retain their content. Revocation stops further updates and future occurrences; adopted content stays local. Source attachments still require a current grant.
- **One jointly completed task**: Reading and completion are checked at the source. Completion applies across installations; reload after a version conflict. An unreachable source cannot confirm a new completion state. Revocation, a paused connection or an unconfirmed key change removes access.

After adoption, local task permissions apply. Another board member does not automatically gain access. The source controls whether the receiving side may complete a task. The distribution mode cannot be changed after the first grant. Future occurrences require **Also share future occurrences**. Separate copies then have independent local sequences; jointly completed tasks create successors at the source.

The task list uses table rows for title, deadline and actions. The title is a link; clicking the free area of a row also opens the task. The checkbox only changes completion. The trash icon on the right moves a task to trash; the restore icon returns it from trash. On narrow screens, the deadline appears below the title.

If the music module is switched on, **Personal music reminders** at the top right leads to your reminders for sheet music returns and equipment returns and maintenance. They appear as private tasks.
en.seiten/belegung.md:
---
key: page.bookings
titel: Bookings and booking calendars
rechte: [bookings.view, bookings.edit, infrastructure.view, material.view]
routen: [/belegung]
stichworte: [Booking, Booking calendar, Reservation, Request, Approval, Set-up time, Hall]
---

Equipment & rooms › **Bookings** shows when facilities and material with a booking calendar are in use. The week
view has one row per item; use **Previous week** and **Next week** to move through the weeks.

Switch on a booking calendar: On the detail page of a facility or a material item, the
managers switch on booking under **Booking calendar**. There you also decide whether bookings
need approval, how much set-up time stays free before and after, and how far ahead
people may book.

Book: Choose **Book**, then the item, the purpose and the time. A booking can repeat
weekly, monthly or yearly. Instead of a time you can choose an event or a competition;
the booking then follows it when it is moved or cancelled. Booking a whole building also books
all of its areas.

Overlaps: If the item, including set-up time, is already booked, HUBIplan refuses the
booking and shows the booked time. If a linked event later moves onto a booked time, the
booking is marked **check**.

Requests and approval: If an item needs approval, your booking starts as a request and does
not block anything yet. People with the permission “Book for others and approve bookings”, or with edit permission
on the item, see **Open requests** and approve or reject them. You can cancel your own request
or booking yourself.

Visibility: With **Only the managers see the purpose**, other members only see "Booked".
Cancel a single date of a series with **Cancel this date only**.

Lending material: For one-off bookings of material, the managers use **Confirm hand-out** in
the booking and later **Confirm return**. Only if you tick
**Record the item's condition on return** does HUBIplan change the item's condition and note; the change then appears in the
item's history.

Booking from a demand: If a material item with a booking calendar is assigned to an event, its
detail page shows **Book firmly**. This opens a booking for that event; for "This occurrence only"
exactly that date is booked.

On the website: Under **Booking calendar** you choose per item whether the “Bookings” section of the website shows nothing, only booked times or, for public bookings, also the purpose. Switch the section on under Website › Menu and sections.

Requests from the members' area: With **Members may send requests from the members' area** an
item appears in My area on the Bookings tile. Such requests always need approval. Whoever made a
request or booking receives an email when someone else confirms, rejects or cancels it.
en.seiten/chronik.md:
---
key: page.chronicle
titel: Chronicle
modul: chronicle
rechte: [chronicle.view, chronicle.edit]
routen: [/chronik]
stichworte: [chronicle, history, timeline, anniversary book, anniversary, chapter]
---

Under **Chronicle** you maintain the history of the club as a timeline: short entries with a
year or period, optionally with pictures, and chapters as subheadings. A short introduction sits
above it.

The chronicle is a module of its own and useful even without a website, for example for an
anniversary book. If the **Website** module is switched on, the published version appears there
under “Chronicle”. It is maintained only here; under Website › Texts the chronicle only shows
its address and menu setting.

HUBIplan saves changes as a draft. **Publish** makes the draft the valid version; earlier
versions can be brought back into the draft below. You can take over many entries at once from
an Excel file.

Anyone with the “Maintain chronicle” right may edit it; anyone with “Read chronicle” may read
it. Roles that edit website content already have both.
en.seiten/dokumente.md:
---
key: page.documents
titel: Documents
modul: docs
routen: [/dokumente]
stichworte: [file, storage, folder, statutes, minutes]
---

Document storage keeps the unit's statutes, minutes, forms and other files in folders. For each folder you decide who sees it, for example only the board or all members. Deleted items go to the bin first; the “Bin” link is at the top of the library.

Storage opens in **Tile view** with folder and file type icons. Switch to **List view** for a compact layout. Click a folder to open it, then **Documents** in the folder path to return to the overview.

**Search (folders, title and note)** searches all your visible own and shared folders, even while a folder is open. Results include matching folder names and documents with matching titles or notes. **Clear search** returns to the previous folder.

Statutes, fee rules and the founding deed are at the top under “Club documents” as fixed folders with their existing versions and sharing settings. A lock marks board folders. Folders shared by other units are read only. Users with management rights can create folders, change visibility and sharing, upload, edit, move, add versions or delete files. The storage display shows usage and, where available, the club's budget.

If virus scanning is set up on the server, HUBIplan scans newly uploaded files. If the scanner is unreachable right now, the document shows “Being scanned for viruses”: it can only be opened after the scan, usually within a few minutes. “Locked: malware found” means the file stays locked for good; upload a clean version instead.

HUBIplan uses these words everywhere in the menu, lists and texts; with several levels it counts per level, for example “7 corps · 15 platoons”. Whether sub-units keep their own members and have their own access is also set here. HUBIplan saves changes automatically.

---
key: page.settings_privacy
titel: Settings › Privacy
rechte: [org.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/datenschutz]
stichworte: [privacy, GDPR, privacy notice, retention periods]

Here you maintain the privacy notices of your unit and website. A draft only becomes public with “publish”. The notices explain to members which data you store and why.
en.seiten/einstellungen-datenuebernahme.md:
---
key: page.settings_data_transfer
titel: Settings › Data transfer
rechte: [data.export, export.run]
routen: [/einstellungen/datenuebernahme]
stichworte: [export, backup, move, JSON]
---

With the full export you take all of the unit's data as a file, for example to move to another HUBIplan instance or as your own backup. The import loads such a file. Keep the file safe; it contains personal data.

New exports explicitly identify their permission schema. Files without a schema and with ambiguous codes require an explicit selection
of the original meaning. **Check again** shows the resulting effective role
permissions, which must be explicitly confirmed before import. The historical
schema includes former photo/card/login data access. Newly
exported narrow read permissions remain narrow. Unknown schemas are rejected. URLs
must use HTTP(S). If scanning is enabled, every inner file actually reused is scanned
individually, even when the outer archive exceeded the upload scan limit. Required
scanning rejects missing scanners and oversized inner files; an error aborts import.
en.seiten/einstellungen-einrichtung.md:
---
key: page.settings_setup
titel: Settings › Setup (overview)
rechte: [settings.view]
routen: [/einstellungen/einrichtung, /einstellungen]
stichworte: [initial setup, set up, progress, required details, reminder levels]
---

The overview shows all setup pages of the enabled modules in one place, grouped by area: club, members, events, finance and, if enabled, competitions and music. The pages themselves stay in their area; each row leads there.

On the right of each row you see the status: “4 created”, “filled in”, “Details missing” or “optional”. Required items that are still missing are marked in red, such as the address under Organisation, membership types, fee rates or reminder levels. At the top you see how many required items are done. While one is missing, the home page shows an entry under **To do** that leads here; missing details in the legal notice appear there under **Notices**.

Use **Search setup** to find an item without knowing which area it belongs to.

You only see items whose page you may open. The overview itself needs “View settings”.

![Setup overview with the status of each item](bild:einrichtung-uebersicht)
en.seiten/einstellungen-erscheinungsbild.md:
---
key: page.settings_theme
titel: Settings › Appearance
rechte: [theme.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/erscheinungsbild, /einstellungen/erscheinungsbild/farbblatt]
stichworte: [colour, logo, coat of arms, look, dark mode, gradient, colour sheet, corporate design]
---

Here you set the club colours and logo. They appear in HUBIplan, on cards, letters and the website. Sub-units inherit them unless they set their own.

Besides the main and second colour there are up to four further colours under **Further colours**, six in total. Each colour gets a name and, if you like, a use, such as “lead colour”, “body text” or “surfaces, table rows”. This lets you take over the colour sheet of a corporate design. Under **Gradients** you create up to two named gradients from two palette colours, for example a blue gradient from blue to dark blue, from left to right or from top to bottom. The website uses them for the header, footer, colour bands, decorative lines and sections; where exactly is set under Website › Design. Next to each gradient you see how readable text on it is. Further colours and gradients only apply together with an own main colour.

Below each colour you tick under **Used for** what it is for: **Body text**, **Secondary text**, **Surfaces and table rows** or **Background**. Each role has at most one colour; ticking it for another colour moves it there. The website takes these colours as its default (under Website › Design each role can still be changed per design), and table rows on the website alternate with the surface colour. With **Also use colour roles in HUBIplan** the roles also colour HUBIplan itself, but only in the light view; dark mode keeps its colours. If text on a surface or the background would be less readable than 4.5 : 1, HUBIplan uses its own colour there and the page names the affected role. Sub-units take over the roles together with the main colour. Without ticked roles everything stays as it is.

**View colour sheet** shows all colours with name, hex and RGB value and use, plus the gradients, on one page to pass on or to save as PDF with **Print**.

Below the logo you can upload a second **Logo / coat of arms for dark mode**, for example a version with light lettering or a light outline. It appears when someone uses the dark appearance (sign-in, home page, events, My account and My area). The preview shows it on a dark background. Without a separate dark mode logo, the normal logo is used in the dark as well. Cards, letters and PDFs always use the normal logo. Sub-units upload their dark coat of arms under Sub-units, with the sub-unit itself.

Links are never underlined. So that they are still easy to recognise, HUBIplan uses a shade of your club colour for links that stands out clearly from the background and from the surrounding text. For very dark colours this shade is a little lighter, for very light colours a little darker. The preview shows the shade used and both values. In headings and bold text, a link also has a “›” after it.

At platform level you set the appearance of the whole instance: its colours and logo then apply to the sign-in page, the public pages and all units without their own colours or logo. This lets every HUBIplan installation have its own look. Club colours always take precedence. For the platform, too, HUBIplan checks that text on the colours is easy to read.

Below that, the platform administration sets the **Instance icon**. It appears in the browser tab and on the phone home screen when someone adds HUBIplan there. A square image without text of at least 512 × 512 pixels works best; HUBIplan creates all required sizes from it. Without a custom icon, the HUBIplan H mark remains. Phones only show a new icon once they fetch it again; on an iPhone the page has to be added to the home screen again.
en.seiten/einstellungen-impressum.md:
---
key: page.settings_imprint
titel: Settings › Legal notice
rechte: [org.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/impressum]
stichworte: [legal notice, imprint, responsible person]
---

The legal notice states who is responsible for your pages. It applies to HUBIplan and the website. If required details are missing, HUBIplan shows this on the home page.
en.seiten/einstellungen-konten.md:
---
key: page.settings_accounts
titel: Settings › Accounts
rechte: [roles.view, logins.view]
routen: [/einstellungen/konten]
stichworte: [account, sign-in, invitation, sign-in link, two-factor, access, user]
---

An account is a person’s sign-in. This page lists all accounts with a role in your unit and everyone allowed to use the member area, with roles, last sign-in and two-factor.

Under **Show** you pick a filter: **with permissions**, **never signed in**, **invitation expired** or **no two-factor although required**. Tick accounts and click “Resend sign-in link”. Accounts with a role get a new invitation as long as they have not set a password yet; member area accounts get a new sign-in link. A link sent this way is valid for 7 days, one requested on the sign-in page for one hour; every new link invalidates the older ones, and at most three links per hour go to one address.

Below, **Terms of office** lists all roles per account with their period. There you resend the invitation to a single person, reset two-factor sign-in or change the period. Roles are assigned under Members › Offices.

You only see accounts with roles with role “read”. With the “Member accounts” area you see the member area accounts.
en.seiten/einstellungen-module.md:
---
key: page.settings_modules
titel: Settings › Modules
rechte: [settings.view]
routen: [/einstellungen/module]
stichworte: [Modul, Funktion, einschalten, ausschalten, Menü, Freigabe, Zusatzfunktion]
---

Here you switch on yourselves what your club uses. A switched-off module disappears from the menu; its data and the rights of roles are kept and come back when you switch it on again. Public parts go offline in the meantime.

You can only choose from the modules the platform administration has released; others do not appear here at all. A switched-on module the platform no longer releases stays visible, marked “not released by the platform”, so you can switch it off. If a module needs another one, that one is switched on as well; if you switch off a requirement, the dependent modules go too. Before every change a confirmation shows what changes.

Below a switched-on module you find its add-on features, such as the cash count in the cash book, SEPA direct debit for fees and invoices, or reserves for tax & charitable status. They are the same switches as in the module’s setup, which the link below them opens.

Anyone with the right to edit settings may change this.
en.seiten/einstellungen-nextcloud.md:
---
key: page.settings_nextcloud
titel: Settings › Nextcloud
rechte: [org.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/nextcloud]
stichworte: [Nextcloud, sign-in, file storage]
---

Here you connect your club's Nextcloud with HUBIplan so members can sign in there with their HUBIplan account.

With **Disable accounts automatically**, HUBIplan switches the Nextcloud account off as soon as someone no longer has access with you, for example because their role ends. Sessions and sync apps are signed out; the files are kept. If the person gets a role again, the account is switched back on. This needs a separate service account with an app password in Nextcloud. Use **Check connection** to test it.

Under “Accounts via HUBIplan” you see who has already signed in via HUBIplan and what the next synchronisation would do. If the synchronisation stops because too many accounts would be affected at once, check the roles and then confirm with **Synchronise now**.

Under **Adjust groups for individual roles** you choose which Nextcloud groups a role is put in, for example “1st treasurer” and “2nd treasurer” both in “Treasurer”. Separate several groups with commas. Without an entry, the group has the same name as the role. If you rename a role, the assignment stays.

Nextcloud itself decides how long a sign-in lasts: usually up to 24 hours without activity and up to 15 days with “stay logged in”; sync apps stay connected permanently. If access ends in HUBIplan without automatic disabling, only the next sign-in fails. Running sessions and sync apps only end when the account is disabled, automatically or by hand in Nextcloud.

“Only with PKCE (S256)” is switched on from the start and protects the login code. The Nextcloud app “user_oidc” uses PKCE by itself. You only need to switch it off for older applications that cannot do PKCE.
en.seiten/einstellungen-organisation.md:
---
key: page.settings_org
titel: Settings › Organisation
rechte: [org.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/organisation]
stichworte: [club, name, address, address supplement, c/o, contact, founding year, contacts]
---

Here you maintain the unit's name, short name, founding year, address and contact. The full name appears on invoices, cards, PDFs and in emails. The platform administration enables which modules you use. What the unit and its sub-units are called is under [Settings › Names and terms](/einstellungen/bezeichnungen); constitution, fee regulations and founding deed are under [Documents](/dokumente) at the top, under “Club documents”. While you scroll, the top of the page always shows whether everything is saved.

If the club is based at a company or in a building with its own name, enter that under “Address supplement”, for example “c/o Musterfirma GmbH”. It appears on its own line above street and house number: in the letterhead, the imprint, circulars and as the second address line of e-invoices.

At the bottom you set the contacts for questions about HUBIplan. They appear in the help under “Who helps us?”, also for sub-units without their own contacts. Like everything else on this page, HUBIplan saves them automatically as soon as a name is entered.

At the very bottom, “Setup of the areas” leads to the settings that only affect one area, such as Members › Setup or Finances › Setup. In a club they are listed under Settings › Modules, below each module’s switch. In the sidebar, settings are grouped into General, Legal, Roles and connections, and Data. Only items your role can read appear there; without any such item, “Settings” is not shown at all.

At platform level the first field is called “Name of this instance”. If you run HUBIplan yourself, give your installation its own name here, for example “Vereinsportal Musterkreis”. It then appears on the sign-in page, in the browser tab and in the emails HUBIplan sends (invitations, passwords, sender name). Below that, the sign-in page shows a small “powered by HUBIplan” linking to the licence and the source code.
en.seiten/einstellungen-orte.md:
---
key: page.settings_places
titel: Settings › Places
rechte: [settings.view, events.manage, competitions.manage, helpers.edit, meetings.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/orte]
stichworte: [place, places, address, directions, clubhouse, fairground, map point]
---

Here you save places that come up again and again, such as the clubhouse, fairground or shooting range. In events, competitions, volunteer duties and meetings you then choose them in the **Place** field instead of typing them every time.

- **New place**: name, address and **Directions and notes** (e.g. parking or entrance). Under **Exact map point (optional)** you enter latitude and longitude if the address is not enough.
- **Suggestions from earlier entries** shows places that were typed in several times in the last two years. **Apply** saves one of them.
- When you choose a saved place in a form, HUBIplan copies its name and address. Later changes here do not change earlier entries.
- If you type a new place in a form, **Save as place** saves it right away.
- A club also sees the places of its federation, a sub-unit those of its club. Only the owner can change or delete them.
- Places you no longer need are removed from the choice with **Edit** and the **Active (offered in forms)** box, without deleting them.
en.seiten/einstellungen-postausgang.md:
---
key: page.settings_outbox
titel: Settings › Outbox
rechte: [audit.view]
routen: [/einstellungen/postausgang]
stichworte: [email, sending, delivered, error]
---

The outbox shows the emails HUBIplan has sent or is about to send for your unit, with their status. Here you also see when an address could not be reached.

After 30 days, delivered emails keep only recipient, subject, type and date; text and attachments are removed. Undelivered emails stay complete for longer so you can resend them, but after 90 days they are emptied as well.

Platform support only sees recipients, subject and status of your emails in its outbox. With **Platform support may see text and attachments** you also share the content, for example when it should help with a delivery problem. Anyone allowed to edit the unit can change this.
en.seiten/einstellungen-protokoll.md:
---
key: page.settings_audit
titel: Settings › Log
rechte: [audit.view]
routen: [/einstellungen/protokoll]
stichworte: [log, changes, who, traceability]
---

The change log shows who changed what and when. The entries are chained, so later changes to the log can be detected.

Anyone allowed to audit the accounts without editing them (for example the auditors) receives a weekly email with the checksum of the latest entry. Please keep these emails: they let you prove later that bookings and the log have not been altered. Fixed bookings and sealed log entries are also protected against changes in the database itself.
en.seiten/einstellungen-rollen.md:
---
key: page.settings_roles
titel: Settings › Roles and permissions
rechte: [roles.view]
routen: [/einstellungen/rollen]
stichworte: [role, right, user, invite, access]
---

For each area, a role sets what its holders may do: **no access**, **read** or **edit**. Edit includes read. A “treasurer”, for example, gets cash book and dues “edit” and members “read”, an auditor only “read” for the cash book. Below are the additional rights to tick: export member lists, full data export and “view as role”. They only work together with the read right of their area.

In the role list, areas are grouped by level, for example “Edit: Cash book, Dues” and “Read: Members”. Areas without levels appear as single tags; “(partly)” means only some of their rights are granted. **Individual permissions** expands all rights of the role.

If someone has several roles, the highest level per area applies. Roles are assigned under Members › Offices with **Assign**; there the predecessor’s term can end in the same step. All accounts with their roles are listed under Settings › Accounts; without member management you assign a role there under **Terms of office**, optionally for a limited time. If the role has permissions and the person has no account yet, they receive an invitation by email. An account is a person's sign-in; a role without permissions needs none. Anyone who has not set a password yet is marked “Password not set yet”; **Resend invitation** sends a new link. With the “view as role” right you check under **My account** at the top right what a role sees. Anyone who may only read roles sees roles, rights and holders but changes nothing.

You set the order of the roles by grabbing a role at its handle and dragging it. The order applies wherever roles are listed: in the role list, on the website and for the authorised representatives in the imprint, privacy notice and letterhead. For example, put the chair before the deputy and the treasurer.

Organisation settings and role administration are separate areas. Editing settings is not enough to change roles, assign an effective role to a member or assign a head. These actions require role “edit”. Existing settings roles are not automatically promoted either: anyone who should continue managing sub-unit roles needs the role right explicitly granted.

Role administration only shows modules and permissions enabled for your club by the platform. When a module is withdrawn, its permissions disappear from the selection and immediately stop granting access. Existing settings are retained, including when you edit other permissions. Once the module is enabled again, they reappear and apply as before. This also applies to sub-unit roles.
en.seiten/einstellungen-verbund.md:
---
key: page.settings_peering
titel: Settings › Network
rechte: [peering.manage]
routen: [/einstellungen/verbund]
stichworte: [network, instance, partner, exchange]
---

In the network you connect your HUBIplan instance with that of an umbrella association or partner club to exchange member reports and invoices. You explicitly release what is transferred.

Peering shows the persistent reception reservation for each connection. Replaced states also count. Additional aggregate limits cover the partner, receiving unit and instance. Exhausted budgets reject data before storage; an administrator must check and approve capacity. Retained financial records are never deleted to recover quota.

Organisations as members (company, association, authority …) are included in the named report with name, name suffix and periods, without contact persons or contact details. If the umbrella association already has an organisation with the same name, it decides in a clarification case. If the other instance still runs an older version, organisations are left out and the connection shows “Other instance too old for organisation members”. After the other side updates, they are sent with the next daily reconciliation.
en.seiten/einstellungen-vereinsdokumente.md:
---
key: page.settings_documents
titel: Settings › Club documents
rechte: [org.edit]
routen: [/einstellungen/vereinsdokumente]
stichworte: [constitution, fee regulations, founding deed, version, PDF]
---

Here you store the constitution, fee regulations and founding deed, each with versions and dates. If you wish, the valid version appears on the website under “Documents”; older versions remain available for reference.

If you can see the document library, the club documents are under [Documents](/dokumente) at the top of the library; this settings item only appears without access to the library.
en.seiten/finanzen-abschluss.md:
---
key: page.finance_closing
titel: Finance › Evaluate & close
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen:
  [
    /finanzen/abschluss,
    /finanzen/auswertung,
    /finanzen/steuern,
    /finanzen/anlagen,
    /finanzen/pauschalen,
  ]
stichworte: [year-end closing, cash report, audit, DATEV, retention period, deletion hold, taxes]
---

In the Finance sidebar, “Book” also contains **Fixed assets** and **Allowances**, and “Evaluate & close” contains **Evaluation** (with net assets), **Development**, **Taxes** (with VAT, artists’ social security levy and use of funds), **Donation receipts** and **Year-end closing** (with cash audit).

Under year-end closing you produce the cash report for the general meeting and close a financial year. After closing, the bookings can no longer be changed. There are also exports, for example for DATEV or the cash audit.

Board members who can manage roles reopen a closing with a reason; the old state is kept. Clubs with an audit obligation switch on **Reopen a closing only with two people (treasurer requests, board confirms)**. The treasury then uses **Request reopening** with a reason, and another person who can manage roles reopens it with **Confirm and reopen**. A request expires after 14 days and can be withdrawn before that. Only board members who can manage roles can switch this on or off.

Once the retention period has ended (receipts 8 years, books 10 years after the end of the calendar year), receipts can be deleted and books anonymised. The periods are set by law and cannot be shortened. If an audit or a legal dispute is still ongoing, use **Set deletion hold** on the financial year and give a reason. While it applies, nothing is deleted. Board members who can manage roles may set and lift it; both are recorded in the log.

The **Taxes** item shows the tax report for a financial year. It belongs to the Tax & charitable status module. It also needs categories assigned to tax areas (Set up › Categories). You see:

- **Tax-free limit**: income from commercial operations including VAT compared with the tax-free limit (€50,000 since 2026, €45,000 before), plus the two previous years. From 80 % you get a note, above the limit a warning.
- **By tax area**: income, expenses and result per area. Cancellations are offset against the cancelled booking. A loss in the commercial operations shows a note.
- **Included cash books**: sub-units with their own cash book count towards the club unless their settings mark them as "separate for tax purposes". A sub-unit only sees its own figures in its own report.
- **Small-business limit**: turnover from purpose-related and commercial operations in the previous and the current year. If the club shows VAT on its invoices, this part is left out.
- **Tax return**: once the details of the exemption notice are entered, this shows for which years the next return is due.

The report is also available as PDF and Excel, for example for your tax adviser. It is a template, not tax advice.

The **VAT** tab under taxes (Tax & charitable status module) is a template for the advance VAT return. For the selected month, quarter or year it shows boxes 81 and 86 (taxable turnover at 19 % and 7 %, with the tax base in whole euros), 48 (tax-exempt turnover), 66 (input VAT) and 83 (amount payable or refund). Bookings with a tax rate are counted. Input VAT only counts for expenses outside the non-profit area, proportionally for mixed use; a cancellation reduces the cancelled booking. Sub-units that belong to the club for tax purposes are included. Under **Settings** you choose whether **The club is liable for VAT (not a small business)**, the **Advance return period** and whether input VAT is calculated as a flat rate under § 23a UStG: 7 % of taxable turnover instead of input VAT from invoices (box 63), only if this turnover did not exceed €50,000 in the previous year; the choice is binding for five years. HUBIplan does not transmit anything to ELSTER. In the DATEV export, bookings with a tax rate get the matching tax key.

The **Allowances** item under “Book” (also part of the Tax & charitable status module) adds up the trainer allowance (§ 3 no. 26 EStG, €3,300 since 2026) and the volunteer allowance (§ 3 no. 26a EStG, €960 since 2026) per person and calendar year. It counts expenses for which **Expense allowance to a person** is selected in the cash book; cancellations do not count. From 80 % there is a note, above the tax-free amount a warning: the payment is then taxable, usually as a mini-job.

The tax-free amounts apply across all payers together. Under **PDF** there is a declaration per person to sign, confirming they do not use the amount elsewhere. Once signed, it belongs with the receipts. If a board member receives an allowance, HUBIplan warns as long as **Our statutes allow the board to be paid** is not ticked (§ 27 (3) BGB).

Besides cash book expenses, the following also count:

- waiving the allowance as an expense donation: tick **Waiver of reimbursement of expenses** on the donation and choose the type under **Waiver of an allowance**. The amount uses up the tax-free allowance just like a payment,
- payments from the musician settlement: when an expense is assigned to an approved musician remuneration, HUBIplan sets the trainer allowance (artistic activity) and counts it for the musician,
- payments by sub-units with their own cash book that belong to the club for tax purposes. The same person then appears only once, with all payments in the expandable list below the name. The sub-unit itself only sees its own payments and a note where it is counted.

The **Fixed assets** item under “Book” is the fixed asset register: items from €250 net that are used for several years, such as tents, refrigerated trailers or furniture. With **Add fixed asset** you enter the date of acquisition, cost, tax area and type of depreciation: straight-line over the useful life (by month), at once as a low-value asset (up to €800 net), as a pool over five years (€250 to €1,000 net) or none. The register shows depreciation and book value for the selected financial year, also as Excel. Record a sale or scrapping as a disposal.

Depreciation only appears here and under **Taxes**, never in the cash book. There it replaces the purchase expense in the result, so that an expensive purchase in commercial operations does not show up as a loss.

The **Cash audit** tab in year-end closing guides you through auditing a financial year. The treasury creates the assignment with **Create audit assignment**: financial year, names of the auditors, deadline and number of samples. HUBIplan draws the five largest expenses plus further random entries and adds a row per account for reconciliation. The auditors get access under Settings › Roles and permissions with a role that may read the treasury but not keep it, ideally with an end date. The page shows who currently has auditor rights and until when.

Only the auditors can tick items off, not the treasury itself. They compare each sample with its document (in order, or a query with a remark), enter the balance per bank statement or cash count for each account, rate the checkpoints and record findings and the recommendation on discharge. **Draw 5 more** enlarges the sample. When nothing is open, they finish with **Complete audit**. The **Audit report (PDF)** is meant for the meeting; if the audit is reopened, the reason goes into the change log. The **Before closing the audit** checklist shows what is still open: checkpoints, account reconciliation, samples, findings, auditor names and the recommendation.

The **Net assets** tab in the evaluation shows what the club owns and owes at the end of a financial year: account balances, open invoices to members and business partners, fixed assets at book value from the asset register (Tax & charitable status module) and open incoming invoices. Anything paid only after the year end counts as open on the reporting date. If reserves are switched on, it also shows how much is set aside and how much is freely available. The overview is also part of the treasurer's report for the general meeting.

The **Artists' social security levy** tab under taxes (Tax & charitable status module) adds up the fees paid to self-employed artists and writers per calendar year, e.g. for a band, drum corps, DJ or graphic designer. It counts expenses ticked **Fee paid to artists (artists' social security levy)** in the cash book and all expenses of a category marked as **Artist fees** under Set up › Categories; cancellations do not count. The page shows the total per recipient, the levy at that year's rate (2026: 4.9 %) and the deadline for reporting to the Künstlersozialkasse (31 March of the following year), also as Excel.

The **Use of funds** tab under taxes (Tax & charitable status module) is a simplified statement on the use of funds. Non-profit funds must be used for the statutory purposes or placed in permitted reserves by the end of the second financial year after they were received. The page shows per year the amount carried over, the funds received (income of the non-profit area and surpluses of the other areas), their use (expenses of the non-profit area, losses of purpose-related operations), additions to and releases from reserves, and what is still to be used by year of origin. The oldest funds are used first. If a deadline has passed, a notice appears. From 100,000 € income per year the tax office usually expects such a statement.
en.seiten/finanzen-beitragslaeufe.md:
---
key: page.finance_fee_runs
titel: Finance › Fee runs
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen/beitragslaeufe]
stichworte: [fee run, annual fee, billing]
---

A fee run creates the fee invoices for all members for a period according to the fee rates. Before the run, a preview shows totals and a checklist; the invoices are only created when you confirm.

Good to know: an honour with a fixed fee never makes the fee higher; if the normal fee is lower, it applies. If a member who does not pay themselves belongs to several sub-units, the invoice goes to the one with the earliest start; the checklist shows how many. With monthly instalments HUBIplan puts remaining cents on the first instalments, so the total can differ by a few cents from a pro-rata annual invoice. A run can only be deleted while it contains drafts only; finalised invoices are also protected against deletion in the database.

Members with **Fee via the household** and a payer do not get their own invoice in the run; they appear together on one invoice to the payer of the household or company, with the family or company fee as a separate line. The preview lists these invoices with the reduction.
en.seiten/finanzen-beitragssaetze.md:
---
key: page.finance_rates
titel: Finance › Set up › Fee rates
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/einrichtung/beitraege]
stichworte: [fee, fee rate, membership type, reduction, size, bands]
---

Fee rates define who pays how much, usually per membership type and period. A fee run uses them to calculate the invoices.

With **Fees by size**, organisation members pay a fee based on their size, e.g. number of employees or inhabitants. Each band has a minimum and/or maximum size and an annual fee; a band for a specific membership type takes precedence over a general one. Enter the size in the member file. Organisations without a size pay the fee of their membership type.

![“Fees by size” card](bild:beitragsstaffel-groesse)

The **Family and company fee** applies to invoices to a household or company (see Members › Households and companies). For each kind you choose a type: **Maximum per invoice** (the sum of the individual fees is capped), **Flat rate** (exactly this amount, never more than the sum) or **Graduated (second person, from the third)** (the second person pays a percentage less, from the third a further one). Amounts are per year and are split across instalments like fees. With **from persons** and **only with at least one adult** you limit when the reduction applies. The invoice keeps the individual fees; the reduction is a separate line below them.
en.seiten/finanzen-dachverband.md:
---
key: page.finance_received
titel: Finance › Received invoices
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen/dachverband]
stichworte: [umbrella association, invoice, levy, association fee]
---

This lists invoices your unit has received from the umbrella association or another unit in HUBIplan, such as the association fee. You see what is open and record the payment.
en.seiten/finanzen-einrichtung.md:
---
key: page.finance_setup
titel: Finance › Set up
rechte: [finance.edit, billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/einrichtung]
stichworte: [setup, accounts, categories, fee rates]
---

In the **Set up** group you define the basics of finance: fee rates, reminder levels, invoice & payment, accounts, categories, details for donation receipts and business partners. Each part is its own entry in the sidebar; the Set up page itself lists all parts with a short description. You usually set this up once at the start of the year.
en.seiten/finanzen-entwicklung.md:
---
key: page.finance_development
titel: Finance › Development
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/entwicklung]
stichworte: [income, expenses, year comparison]
---

Development compares income and expenses over the years, by category and tax area. This lets you spot changes early.

After you change the selection, previous results are hidden until the new request finishes. If loading fails, **Reload** retries the same selection.
en.seiten/finanzen-erechnungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_einvoices
titel: Finances › Customer invoices
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.view]
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen/leistungen, /finanzen/geschaeftspartner]
stichworte: [E-invoice, XRechnung, business partner, customer invoice, EN16931]
---

Create a customer under **Business partners** first. Membership is not
required. Under **Invoices** → **Customer invoices**, enter the income category, service
period, addresses, buyer reference and payment IBAN. Enter net prices in EUR.

Choose the tax treatment explicitly. Exempt, zero-rated and outside the scope of VAT
are different categories. Exempt, reverse-charge and out-of-scope items require a
reason. XRechnung requires the supplier's contact name and phone number.
Without a VAT identifier, the supplier needs a unique business partner identifier,
such as the supplier number agreed with the customer.

**Validate e-invoice** displays errors and warnings. **Validate and issue** validates
again and assigns the final invoice number only on success. Issued invoices and
addresses cannot be changed. Download the XML, validation report and readable view.
Technical validation does not replace checking the service or tax treatment.

**Payments and delivery** opens the existing invoice view. Sending includes the XML
and readable view. A cancellation also creates a separate structured cancellation
document with the reason and a reference to the invoice number and date.
**Send cancellation invoice by email** attaches the XML and PDF.

Use **Invoice type** to choose an invoice, advance invoice or final invoice. A final
invoice includes the entire service and credits payments already received against
advance invoices for the same customer and event. This creates no duplicate income.
If payments change after drafting, save and validate the draft again. Credited advances
are marked “Settled”. Cancel the final invoice before removing their payments.

**Create and validate ZUGFeRD** generates a locally validated PDF/A file with embedded
XML from the original. Then **Download ZUGFeRD**, including cancellation documents.
Originals and validation reports remain available.

For Peppol, enter registered electronic addresses and EAS codes for the business
partner and supplier. The platform administrator configures the selected provider
for each club. **Transmit electronically** explicitly sends the original;
**Fetch delivery status** retrieves confirmation. Unconfirmed attempts are reconciled
with the provider before retrying. Send cancellations separately. Without a provider
connection, download the document and upload it manually to the recipient's portal.
Existing membership invoices remain available.
en.seiten/finanzen-gruppen.md:
---
key: page.finance_groups
titel: Finance › Group pages
rechte: [finance.view, billing.view]
routen: [/finanzen/buchen, /finanzen/abrechnen, /finanzen/zahlungen, /finanzen/abschliessen]
stichworte: [group, group page, payments, book, set up, to do]
---

Clicking the name of a group in the Finance sidebar (e.g. **Book**) opens its group page. It shows every entry of the group with a short description and, in red below it, what is currently to do there, such as entries without a receipt or reminders that are due. Clicking a card opens the entry.

At the top right is the main action of the group, if you may edit finance: **Write invoice** for Fees & invoices, **Import bank statement** for Payments, **Record income** and **Record expense** for Book, and **Close the year** for Evaluate & close. The group page of **Set up** is at [Finance › Set up](/finanzen/einrichtung).

With ▸ next to the group name you expand a group in the sidebar without changing the page. The finance overview also leads to the group pages under **Work steps**.
en.seiten/finanzen-haushaltsplan.md:
---
key: page.finance_budget
titel: Finance › Budget
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/haushaltsplan]
stichworte: [budget, plan, actual, forecast, annual general meeting]
---

In the budget you set out, for one financial year, what the club plans to receive and spend per category. Next to it you see the actual figures from the cash book, the variance and, in the current year, a forecast. This shows early whether the year is going to plan and gives you a template for the meeting.

Creating: Choose the financial year at the top, including the coming one. The quickest way is “Copy plan from …” or “Copy actual figures from …” (rounded to whole euros); **Start empty** starts without a template. With **Edit** you change amounts, add categories with **Add line** and remove lines. **Save** applies everything at once.

Sub-units: A line can apply to everyone or to one sub-unit (for example a platoon). A sub-unit's line counts only its bookings; the line for everyone counts the rest of the category. Bookings without a matching line are listed below as “not budgeted”; **Add to budget** takes them in.

Actual and forecast: Income and expenses of the financial year count, without transfers; a cancellation reduces the side it cancels. The forecast assumes that as much will still come in by year end as in the previous year from the same day, so a festival in summer does not distort it. Without figures from the previous year, the plan applies as long as the actual figure stays below it.

Adoption: Once the meeting has adopted the budget, record it with **Record as adopted** (date and, if you like, who adopted it). The budget is then locked. To change it, **Edit as draft again** sets it back; afterwards record it as adopted again.

For the meeting: **PDF** and **Excel** show plan and actual of the year next to plan and actual of the previous year. For a single festival, enter planned income and expenses directly on the event (Finance › Events).
en.seiten/finanzen-kassenbuch.md:
---
key: page.finance_cashbook
titel: Finance › Cash book
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/kassenbuch]
stichworte: [booking, receipt, income, expense, cash, split booking, split]
---

The cash book records every income and expense with date, account, category and receipt. Bookings in a closed period can no longer be changed, only corrected with a reversing entry. This keeps the cash book auditable.

Cancel bookings with receipts instead of deleting them. Imported bank statements are retained; ignore unwanted transactions. Archive used categories and create a new category for new assignments. Reminders retain their archived version.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.

After you change the selection, previous results are hidden until the new request finishes. If loading fails, **Reload** retries the same selection.

If loading accounts or categories fails, **Reload** retries locally. Booking details you have already entered are retained when a refresh fails.

**Split** (split booking): If one payment belongs to several categories or tax areas, for example the caterer's settlement with drinks, admission and advertising, open the booking and choose **Split**. Each part gets a category, an amount and optionally an event and a description. Together the parts must add up exactly to the amount. Each part becomes a booking of its own with its own number. Date, account and payee or payer apply to all parts; receipts and the bank transaction stay with the first part. Splitting works as long as the booking is not locked and does not belong to a cancellation, a signed receipt, an invoice payment or a donation.

**Business partners**: in the payee or payer field your business partners (Club › Business partners) come first. If you pick one, the booking is linked to it and an empty category gets its default category. You can still change the name freely. If the partner is marked as an artist, the expense counts for the artists' social insurance levy.

**Expense allowance to a person**: if the club pays a trainer or volunteer an allowance, choose trainer allowance or volunteer allowance on the expense and enter the member or recipient. The totals per person are under Finance › Allowances. The field is available with the Tax & charitable status module.

**VAT included in the amount**: if the club is liable for VAT, choose the tax rate for income and expenses (19 %, 7 %, tax-exempt or none). The amount stays gross; HUBIplan calculates net amount and tax. New bookings take the default of the category (Set up › Categories, column **VAT**). For expenses with mixed use, enter the business share under **Deductible input VAT (%)**. The totals are under Finance › Taxes › VAT.

**Record as fixed asset**: for an expense from €250, this button takes the amount, date and text into the fixed asset register (Finance › Fixed assets) and links the asset to the booking.
en.seiten/finanzen-kassenzaehlung.md:
---
key: page.finance_cash_count
titel: Finance › Cash count
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/kassenzaehlung]
stichworte: [count, cash, cash balance, festival]
---

In a cash count you enter notes and coins; HUBIplan calculates the total and compares it with the cash book. The record with signatures serves as proof, for example after a festival.
en.seiten/finanzen-kategorien.md:
---
key: page.finance_categories
titel: Finance › Set up › Categories
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/einrichtung/kategorien]
stichworte: [category, tax area, purpose-related business]
---

Categories group bookings, such as “fees”, “festival” or “uniforms”, and each category belongs to a tax area (non-profit area, asset management, purpose-related business, commercial business). The cash report and tax overview are built from them.

**Use a template** creates the usual categories of a shooting, sports or music club, each with a tax area and, where it fits, the donations or artist fees mark. Only missing categories are created; existing ones stay unchanged. The areas are a suggestion, and your tax adviser enters the DATEV accounts. For sponsorship: if the sponsor is only named, the money belongs to asset management; active advertising such as boards, ads or jerseys is a commercial operation.
en.seiten/finanzen-konten.md:
---
key: page.finance_accounts
titel: Finance › Set up › Accounts
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/einrichtung/konten]
stichworte: [account, bank account, petty cash, IBAN]
---

Here you create your bank accounts and cash boxes. With the IBAN, HUBIplan recognises the right account when reading a bank statement.
en.seiten/finanzen-kontoauszuege.md:
---
key: page.finance_statements
titel: Finance › Bank statements
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/kontoauszuege]
stichworte: [bank statement, CAMT, bank, matching]
---

Here you upload the bank statement from online banking in CAMT.053 format. For each transaction HUBIplan suggests what it belongs to, such as an invoice or a booking, and you confirm. HUBIplan detects if the same file is read twice. Imported statements are retained as originals. Ignore unwanted transactions or reopen incorrect assignments.

If the IBAN of a transaction belongs to a business partner (Club › Business partners, section Treasury), HUBIplan assigns the transaction to that partner. A booking created from it takes over the partner.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.
en.seiten/finanzen-lastschrift.md:
---
key: page.finance_debits
titel: Finance › Direct debits
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.view]
routen: [/finanzen/lastschrift]
stichworte: [SEPA, direct debit, collection, mandate, bank]
---

From open invoices with a valid SEPA mandate HUBIplan creates a direct debit file that you upload in online banking. A checklist first checks the creditor ID, deadlines and expiring mandates. HUBIplan does not connect to the bank itself.

For organisation members (and for clubs of an association) you can choose **Business direct debit (B2B)** as the **Scheme** when recording a paper mandate. This needs a signed mandate on the business form, and the payer must register it with their bank. The payer cannot reverse a business direct debit once it has been paid. In a direct debit run, core and business debits sit in separate blocks of the same file. For persons there is only the **Core direct debit**.

If loading fails, **Reload** retrieves proposals and runs again. A failed request is shown as an error rather than an empty selection.
en.seiten/finanzen-mahnstufen.md:
---
key: page.finance_dunning_levels
titel: Finance › Set up › Reminder levels
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/einrichtung/mahnstufen]
stichworte: [reminder level, deadline, reminder fee]
---

Reminder levels define after how many days a reminder is sent and with which text. A friendly first reminder is often enough.
en.seiten/finanzen-mahnungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_dunning
titel: Finance › Reminders
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen/mahnungen]
stichworte: [reminder, payment reminder, overdue]
---

Here you see overdue invoices and send payment reminders according to your reminder levels. Each reminder is noted on the invoice.
en.seiten/finanzen-quittungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_receipts
titel: Finance › Receipts
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/quittungen]
stichworte: [receipt, cash payment, voucher]
---

For cash payments you issue a receipt here, with your stored signature if you like. Each receipt gets a sequential number and is booked in the cash book.

The signature on the screen is a simple electronic signature: it shows that someone signed on the spot, but it does not verify who it was. If the app is used offline, date and time come from the phone. For the cash book this is as good a voucher as a paper receipt. If you need more certainty (for example for large amounts), also have the receipt confirmed in writing or by email.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.

The details of a new receipt are saved with **Continue to signature**. If you change details and cancel or leave the page, HUBIplan asks before discarding them. **Continue editing** retains your input. An automatically selected sole cash account does not trigger a warning on its own.

If the receipt list or the account and category choices fail to load, use **Reload**. A failed request for choices does not discard receipt details you have already entered.
en.seiten/finanzen-rechnung.md:
---
key: page.finance_invoice_settings
titel: Finance › Set up › Invoice & payment
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.edit]
routen: [/finanzen/einrichtung/rechnung]
stichworte: [invoice, payment term, creditor ID, e-invoice]
---

This holds the details that appear on every invoice: payment term, bank details, creditor ID for direct debits and the number range.

Under **E-invoices for public authorities** you can have invoices to members with a Leitweg-ID (e.g. a town or district as a member) created as XRechnung. Enter the Leitweg-ID in the member’s billing address. When finalising, HUBIplan validates the XRechnung; if something is missing, such as the club’s address, contact, phone or an account with IBAN, the invoice stays a draft and the message names what is missing. Membership fees appear in it as not subject to VAT. The invoice email carries the XRechnung as an attachment.

Cancel bookings with receipts instead of deleting them. Imported bank statements are retained; ignore unwanted transactions. Archive used categories and create a new category for new assignments. Reminders retain their archived version.
en.seiten/finanzen-rechnungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_invoices
titel: Finance › Invoices
modul: billing
rechte: [billing.view]
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen]
stichworte: [invoice, fee, open, paid, cancellation]
---

This lists all of the unit's invoices, such as membership fees or uniform costs, with their status: open, paid, reminded or cancelled. You create a single invoice here; a fee run creates many at once.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.

Enter a search term and choose **Search** or press Enter. Status and other filters apply immediately.

After you change the selection, previous results are hidden until the new request finishes. If loading fails, **Reload** retries the same selection.

Final invoices show credited advances and the remaining outstanding amount. A credited
advance invoice is marked “Settled”. Its receipts remain in the cashbook. Cancel the
associated final invoice before removing those payments. A final invoice fully covered
by advances can also be cancelled if it has no additional payments.

Cancelling: in the invoice, choose **Cancel invoice** and give a reason. HUBIplan then creates a separate cancellation invoice, for example R2026-0012-S. It has its own date and reason, refers to the number and date of the invoice and lists all items with negative amounts. The issued invoice stays unchanged. **View cancellation invoice** opens the document and **Send cancellation invoice by email** sends it to the recipient. Members also find it in the member area.

Paid invoices can be cancelled too. The payments then remain on the invoice as a credit. **Refund** reverses the payments in the cash book with today's date; then transfer the amount back. **Offset** moves the payments to an open invoice to the same recipient.

**Cancel and create again** cancels the invoice and opens a copy as a new draft, so you correct a wrong invoice in one step. Invoices from a fee run are recalculated in the fee run instead.
en.seiten/finanzen-rechnungseingang.md:
---
key: page.finance_incoming
titel: Finances › Incoming invoices
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/rechnungen/eingang]
stichworte: [E-invoice, ZUGFeRD, incoming, approval, XML]
---

Import XML invoices or ZUGFeRD/Factur-X PDFs. HUBIplan retains the original even when
validation fails. Importing the identical file again does not create another entry.
Check different files with the same invoice number for duplicates yourself.

**Invoice mailbox**: If an invoice mailbox is set up on the server, the address of your unit
is shown at the top, e.g. `rechnung+k7m2q9ab@example.org`. Give it to your suppliers. HUBIplan
collects the mailbox every minute and imports XML attachments and ZUGFeRD/Factur-X PDFs just
like an import. The entry then shows **By email from** with the sender. If the sender does not
match any business partner (email address under Club › Business partners), **Unknown sender**
appears; then check the issuer and bank details with particular care. Emails without
an e-invoice, such as an ordinary PDF invoice, spam or malware, are listed under **Notices from the mailbox**
until you choose **Done**. **Assign new address** invalidates the previous
address, for example if it receives spam.

**Business partners**: HUBIplan suggests a business partner for each invoice, recognised by
VAT ID, IBAN, the email sender (including the contact persons' email addresses) or name.
**Link suggestion** accepts it; **Create as business partner** creates a new supplier from the
name, VAT ID, IBAN and sender. **Unlink business partner** removes the link. When you later
link a cash book entry, it takes over the business partner.

**New IBAN**: If the invoice IBAN differs from the one stored for the business partner,
HUBIplan shows a clear warning. Call the issuer on a number you already know, not the one on
the invoice, and tick **New IBAN confirmed by phone** before approving. HUBIplan stores the
confirmed IBAN with the business partner. This protects you against fake invoices with
someone else's bank account.

Technical validation (KoSIT) runs in the background after the import. Until it finishes,
the entry shows **Checking**; this usually takes less than a minute and the page refreshes
by itself. HUBIplan deletes declined entries and files without a readable e-invoice after
90 days if no booking is linked.

Validation covers the XML data. It does not certify PDF/A properties or consistency
between an external PDF view and its embedded XML. Use the **Readable view** of the
structured data for review.

Check the recipient, service, amount and bank details before approval. Enter a review
note and choose **Approve business review** or **Decline**. Approval requires successful
technical validation. Revalidation preserves previous reports in the audit export.

Importing and approving do not send a payment. After actual payment, link a matching
cash book entry. Type, EUR amount and an open financial year are checked; partial
payments cannot be linked here yet. The original also becomes a cash book attachment.
en.seiten/finanzen-ruecklagen.md:
---
key: page.finance_reserves
titel: Finance › Reserves
modul: tax
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/ruecklagen]
stichworte: [reserve, non-profit status, use of funds]
---

Here you keep reserves, for example for a new flag or maintenance. Non-profit clubs must generally use funds promptly; reserves are only allowed for certain reasons (§ 62 AO).

At the bottom of the page, **Maximum for the free reserve** works out how much may be added to the free reserve in a financial year: one third of the surplus from asset management plus 10 % of the other funds to be used promptly (income of the non-profit area, surpluses from purpose-related and commercial operations). Any amount not used in the two previous years can be carried over. If additions are higher, a notice appears. The calculation uses the tax areas of the categories; entries without an area count as non-profit income.

If there are assets in the asset register, their depreciation for the year is shown as a guide for a replacement reserve. From 100,000 € income per year, the page points out that the tax office usually expects a statement on the use of funds.
en.seiten/finanzen-veranstaltungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_events
titel: Finance › Events
modul: finance
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/veranstaltungen]
stichworte: [festival, event, project, cash report]
---

For a festival or another project you group all related bookings here and produce a cash report at the end. This shows whether an event covered its costs.

Under **Planned income (optional)** and **Planned expenses (optional)** you enter what you expect. The evaluation then shows the plan next to income, expenses and result. The budget for the whole year is under Finance › Evaluate & close › Budget.
en.seiten/finanzen-zuwendungen.md:
---
key: page.finance_donations
titel: Finance › Donation receipts
modul: donations
rechte: [finance.view]
routen: [/finanzen/zuwendungen]
stichworte: [donation, donation receipt, tax office]
---

For donations and tax-deductible membership fees you create official donation receipts here, individually or as an annual statement. A checklist first shows missing details such as the tax exemption notice. You enter these details under Finance › Set up › Donations.

An issued donation receipt also protects its source cashbook entry: it cannot be edited, deleted or reverted with Undo. To make a correction, cancel the donation receipt first. You can then correct the entry under the usual cashbook rules; the cancelled receipt copy remains available.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.

For donations up to 300 €, the tax office accepts the bank statement together with a note from the club (simplified donation proof). Once the tax-privileged status details are complete, Finance › Set up › Donations offers this note under **Donations up to 300 €** as a PDF and as text for the website. It names the notice, the purposes, the donation account and whether it also covers membership fees.

In the **Earmarks** tab you create purposes that people donate to specifically, such as a new flag. Assign a donation to a purpose with the **Earmarked for** field, and the expenses for it in the cash book with **Earmarked donation used for**. The overview shows the donations per purpose, how much has been used and the remainder. Only money donations count; cancellations do not. If the first donation was more than two years ago and something is left, a notice reminds you of the prompt use of funds. A purpose with donations or expenses can only be archived, not deleted.

A donation taken from the cash book follows its booking: if you change the booking's amount or date, HUBIplan changes the not yet confirmed donation as well. If the booking is deleted or cancelled (also by cancelling a receipt), the unconfirmed donation is removed. Once it is confirmed, the booking and receipt can only be changed, deleted or cancelled after the confirmation has been cancelled. Before issuing, HUBIplan checks that booking and donation match; the checklist names mismatches from older data.

HUBIplan books payments on household and company invoices to the payer, not to the individual members. A donation receipt for them therefore goes to the payer: to the paying member or the company, or for a payer without membership with name and address as on the invoice.
en.seiten/finanzen.md:
---
key: page.finance
titel: Finance › Overview
rechte: [finance.view, billing.view]
routen: [/finanzen]
stichworte: [cash, balance, overview, open items]
---

The overview shows account balances, open invoices and upcoming tasks for the treasurer. On the left, the parts of finance are grouped along the financial year: **Fees & invoices**, **Payments**, **Book**, **Evaluate & close** and **Set up**. The group of the page you are on is open; ▸ expands another group for a look. Which groups and entries appear depends on the enabled modules and your rights; a group with only one entry is shown as a plain entry.
en.seiten/fristenkalender.md:
---
key: page.obligations
titel: Deadline calendar for club obligations
modul: obligations
rechte: [obligations.view, obligations.edit]
routen: [/fristenkalender]
stichworte:
  [
    Deadline,
    Obligation,
    Exemption notice,
    Tax return,
    Cash audit,
    Transparency register,
    Register court,
    Register of associations,
    Board election,
    Insurance,
    Reminder,
  ]
---

The **Deadline calendar** collects the obligations a club has to meet regularly, such as the tax
return for the exemption notice, the cash audit before the annual general meeting or the check of
the transparency register. HUBIplan reminds you in time and records when an obligation was
completed.

Adding an obligation: **New obligation** asks for a name, the next deadline, the repetition
(once, every year, every three years …) and how many days before the deadline HUBIplan sends a
reminder. In the note you can record, for example, the legal basis or where the documents are
kept.

Responsible: An obligation belongs to a role, not to a person, for example the treasurer. When
