the office changes hands, HUBIplan reminds the new holders automatically. Without a role, the
reminders go to everyone who may maintain the deadline calendar.

Suggestions: **Suggestions** lists common obligations of registered, non-profit associations in
Germany. **Apply** creates the obligation; you adjust deadline, repetition and responsibility as
you do so. Suggestions that only concern registered associations appear when “entered in the register” is ticked in the legal notice. The notes are no substitute for legal or tax advice.

Reminder: As soon as the reminder period starts, the responsible people receive one email, and
the obligation appears on the home page under **To do**. Overdue obligations are highlighted
there and in the deadline calendar.

Done: **Done** records the date and a short remark, such as “Notice of 12 March is in the tax
office folder”. A recurring obligation moves on to the next deadline, a one-off one then appears
under **Completed**. The **History** shows who completed which deadline and when. Everyone who
maintains the deadline calendar and the holders of the responsible role may mark it as done.

After a board election: When minutes are approved in [Meetings](/versammlungen) that contain an
accepted election to an office that represents the club, HUBIplan creates the task “Report the change of the board to the register court”. It names those elected, is due 14 days after the
meeting and is linked to the election in the resolution book. Representing roles are those marked
“represents the unit (§ 26 BGB)”; the office in the minutes must have the same name as the
role. If no role is marked, all board roles count. This happens for clubs that are entered in the
register according to their legal notice. If you adopt the suggestion, you can change the
deadline and the responsible role or switch the task off. If the Tasks module is switched off, a
one-off obligation appears in the deadline calendar instead.

You switch the module on under Settings › Modules.
en.seiten/geschaeftspartner.md:
---
key: page.partners
titel: Business partners
rechte: [partners.view, finance.view, billing.view]
routen: [/geschaeftspartner]
stichworte:
  [
    business partner,
    supplier,
    service provider,
    sponsor,
    sponsorship,
    thank-you letter,
    authority,
    contact person,
    customer,
    address book,
  ]
---

This lists all companies, authorities, associations and people outside the member list that you deal with: suppliers, service providers, sponsors, landlords, public offices or the press.

- **Create business partner** asks for the type (company, authority/office, association/federation, private person, other), address, contact and tax details. Only the name is required. Each entry gets a running number such as “GP-0001”.
- Under **Roles** you tick what the partner is for you, several if needed: for example supplier and sponsor. Customer and supplier also apply to invoices and incoming invoices.
- **Add contact** stores people at the partner with function, email and phone. A **Primary contact** is shown first in the list.
- Under **Contact with the club** you record when and how the first contact came about (**First contact on**, **First contact**) and which member looks after the partner (**Looked after by**).
- **Additional fields** creates your own fields for all business partners, such as sponsorship level, delivery time or customer since. The same kinds are available as for the members' additional fields, including repeatable fields with several entries. You enter the values in the partner's record in the **Additional fields** section; they save themselves. Fields without repetition appear as their own column in the Excel export and can be changed through the import. Anyone who may edit business partners may create fields.
- The **Treasury** section (bank account, **Default category**, payment term, artists' social security levy) only appears with cash or fee rights. Below it you see when the bank account was last changed and by whom.
- You can search the list and filter it by type and role. **Show inactive** brings back partners you no longer need.
- **Export to Excel** puts all details into a spreadsheet, with a second sheet “Contact person”. Bank account, payment term and default category are only included if you have cash or fee rights. Export, serial letter and mailing list require the “Business partners” right; anyone who only manages the cash book or fees sees the partners but cannot take the whole list.
- **Import from Excel** reads such a spreadsheet back in. The easiest way is to export, edit in Excel and import the file. A known number updates the partner; empty cells change nothing. Rows without a number are created, unless the name already exists. HUBIplan finds contact persons by partner number, name and first name. **Check file** shows beforehand what will be added and what will change. “Looked after by” is matched most reliably through the column with the member number.
- **Serial letter and mailing list** chooses a group by role and type, for example all sponsors. **Copy e-mail addresses** fetches the addresses of the contact persons who receive mail (otherwise the partner's e-mail) for your mail program. **Create serial letter** writes one letter per partner with an address as a PDF on your letterhead.
- **Merge duplicate entry** takes over a second entry of the same company: invoices, bookings, agreements, performances and contact persons move along.
- **Turnover in the treasury** shows income and expenses with the partner per year and the latest bookings. Cancelled bookings do not count.
- The card “Suggestions from the cash book” lists names that appear several times as payee or payer in the cash book. **Apply** creates a business partner from one and links the bookings with exactly this name. This needs the right to edit the cash book.
- **Add agreement** records sponsorship and other arrangements: period, amount or in-kind contribution, what you give in return (such as a logo on the website, a perimeter board, a commemorative booklet) and the tax classification. “Mention only” without advertising belongs to the non-profit area or asset management, active advertising to the commercial operations. With an end date, HUBIplan creates a task that reminds you of the renewal in good time (Tasks module); you set how many days before on the agreement.
- **Thank-you letter** creates a letter on your letterhead as a PDF, to the partner's address and the first contact person who receives mail. You can replace the suggestion with amount and in-kind contribution by your own text.
- For a **Contract** (type of agreement) you enter the **Notice period in days** and whether it renews automatically. The task then reminds you in good time before the last day to give notice, and the list shows “give notice by …”.
- Under **Documents** you keep contracts, offers, consents or correspondence on the record. The files count towards the storage of the document library and are checked for viruses as there.
- Under **Website** you record whether the partner may be named on your website as a partner or sponsor. Only these partners are taken over by the website section “Partners and sponsors” with **Take over from business partners**.
- You can only delete a partner as long as it is not used anywhere. Otherwise untick **Active**.
- If a partner is also a member, for example a company as a supporting member, please do not create it twice. Only store private persons as far as you need them for a contract.
en.seiten/helferdienste.md:
---
key: page.helpers
titel: Volunteer duties and shift rosters
modul: helpers
rechte: [helpers.view, helpers.edit]
routen: [/helferdienste]
stichworte: [Duty roster, Shift roster, Volunteers, Shift, Bar, Setup, Assignment]
---

Under **Volunteer duties** you plan who takes on which duty at a festival or event, such as the
bar, cash desk, setup or teardown. The overview shows each duty roster with its open places.

New duty roster: Choose **New duty roster**, enter a title and link the roster to an event if
needed.
From an event in the calendar, **Create duty roster for this event** leads straight here with
the event already selected. In the roster, the event name leads back to the calendar.

Duties and shifts: Use **Add duty** to create a duty with its place and, if needed, a minimum
age (such as serving alcohol from 18). Below it you create the shifts: day, times and people per
shift. Several shifts can be created at once, such as “14-18, 18-22, 22-02”; a shift past
midnight ends the next day.

Assigning: **Assign** on a shift adds a member or an external person with name and phone. If the
shift is already full, overlaps with another shift of the same person, or the person is younger
than the minimum age, HUBIplan asks first; **Assign anyway** goes ahead regardless. Phone numbers
are only visible to those who may edit duty rosters.

Requirement: If the “Qualifications” module is switched on, you choose a qualification under
**Requirement** at a duty, for example range officer for the shooting range. If the person lacks
it or it expires before the end of the shift, HUBIplan asks when assigning, and a note appears at
the person. Members who sign up themselves see the requirement and cannot sign up without a valid
certificate.

Printing: **Notice as PDF** creates one page per duty with the shifts and empty lines for
signing up. **List as Excel** contains all shifts with the people assigned.

Status: **Publish** marks the roster as final, **Close** ends it; after that it cannot be changed
until you reopen it. Only a published roster appears in the member area.

Roster settings: Under **Roster settings** you choose whether members sign up themselves or only
the administration assigns people, until how many days before a shift members can cancel
themselves, the maximum number of shifts per person and how many days before a shift HUBIplan
sends a reminder email (empty: no reminder). You also choose whether people who signed up see
who else is on their shift, and you can write a note for the helpers. After the cancellation
deadline, only the administration can cancel a shift.

Units: If a role of a unit (such as the platoon leadership) has the right, it plans its own
duties and only assigns members of that unit.

Quotas: In a club roster, **Quota** on a shift gives part of the places to a unit, for example
“the rifle platoon provides 4 people for the bar”. The unit's leadership sees its places in its
volunteer duties under **Quotas from the club** and assigns its own members there. Places of a
quota that are still open count as taken in the member area. Setting 0 places removes a quota;
people already assigned stay on the shift.

Copy roster: **Copy roster** creates a new roster in preparation, for example for next year's
festival. The copy takes over duties, shifts, quotas and settings, but no assignments. If you
enter the first day of the new roster, HUBIplan moves all shifts by the same distance.

Call-out: If a published roster still has free places, **Call-out as circular** creates a draft
to all members of the unit with the free shifts and the link to sign up. You check and send it
like any circular. You also need the right to send circulars.

Completed duties: Once a shift has started, tick **done** for each person. **Completed duties**
in the overview shows per year who took on how many shifts and hours, for example for a thank
you or required hours.
en.seiten/infrastruktur.md:
---
key: page.infrastructure
titel: Manage rooms and facilities
modul: infrastructure
rechte: [infrastructure.view]
routen: [/infrastruktur]
stichworte: [Shooting range, Clubhouse, Hall, Room, Area, Key, Shooting lanes]
---

Equipment & rooms › **Rooms and facilities** (Facilities module) lists the fixed premises of your active unit, for example a shooting range,
a clubhouse or a club hall. Each facility has its own number (INF-…), a type, a short
description and an address.

With editing permission, choose **Create facility**. Optionally enter the capacity,
ownership and use, and an **Access note** such as where the key box is. Only people with
viewing permission for facilities can see the access note.

For the type **Shooting range**, enter the number of lanes per discipline under
**Shooting lanes**, for example ten 10 m air rifle lanes. In the shooting facility settings
the club can choose **Take from facilities**. Target selection in competitions then
recommends targets that suit these lanes.

Add parts of a facility on its detail page with **Create area**, for example a hall, kitchen
or individual ranges. An area uses the address of its facility; areas cannot contain further
areas.

The detail page also shows **Equipment stored here** and **Associated equipment**. Equipment
is stored here when its location is **In a facility**. Associated equipment is linked under
**Belongs to** on the equipment item, for example a key kept by a member. Both are only
visible with equipment permission.

Photo, tasks, documents such as house rules or a lease, event links, history and the recycle
bin work as for equipment. A retired facility is hidden and can no longer be chosen as a
location.
en.seiten/material.md:
---
key: page.material
titel: Manage equipment
modul: material
rechte: [material.view]
routen: [/material]
stichworte: [Inventory, Equipment, Location, Photo, Image, Recurring events]
---

Equipment & rooms › **Equipment** lists the items belonging to your active unit. Search by name, description
or address. Use the filters to include retired items or open the recycle bin.

![Equipment list with locations and condition](bild:material-liste)

With editing permission, create an item with a name, short description, purpose or event,
and location. The default location type is **With a member**. Select an accessible member
or enter a complete address. Everyone with
equipment viewing permission in this unit can see manually entered addresses. Choose **Save**.

The form is divided into basic data, location and condition, with labels above the fields.
To select members, events, tasks or documents, enter at least two characters in **Search choices**.
A result menu opens below the field; choose the matching entry. There is no separate permanent menu.

![Equipment form with grouped input fields](bild:material-formular)

On the detail page, add, replace or remove an **Equipment photo**. JPEG, PNG and WebP
files up to 10 MB are accepted. Image metadata is removed. Viewing the image requires
equipment access.

Link multiple events, recurring series, tasks and documents. For a series, select the
whole series, one occurrence or an exclusion. An occurrence is identified by its original
start, even when rescheduled. If the recurrence rule changes, review and update its links.
Upcoming uses describe demand; they are not binding reservations.

Private tasks and inaccessible documents remain hidden. **Create a task for this item**
opens the task form and links the item when saved. Completing a transport task does not
change the location automatically: confirm the new location using **Edit**.

Under **History**, undo your most recent change if current permissions and linked objects
allow it. History and recycled items are retained for 30 days. Retiring an item preserves
its links; resolve open tasks and future uses first.

If the facilities module is enabled, the location can also be **In a facility**, for example
the clubhouse cellar. Use **Belongs to** to link an item to a facility, for example a key kept
by a member.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-ausweis.md:
---
key: page.portal_card
titel: My area › Card
routen: [/mein-bereich/ausweis]
stichworte: [card, QR code, membership card]
---

Your membership card with QR code. Show it on your phone or print it. If you lose your phone, the club can block the card and create a new one.

If your operator has configured Wallet and your club has switched it on, you can add
the card to Google Wallet or download an Apple Wallet pass (`.pkpass`). The pass shows
name, club, membership type, department and umbrella association in the club's colours
and with its logo, in German or English depending on the phone's language. Google
receives these details, but no photo. Apple passes do not update automatically; download them again
after changes. Scan the QR code to check current validity online. If the club creates
a new QR code, add the new pass to your wallet.

If you are the contact person of an organisation, the card shows the organisation with its logo instead of a photo, and the check page lists it as an organisation member. The card does not show who presents it.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-belegung.md:
---
key: page.portal_bookings
titel: My area › Bookings
routen: [/mein-bereich/belegung]
stichworte: [Booking, Request, Clubhouse, Hall, Range, Equipment, borrow]
---

Here you see when the clubhouse, a range or equipment that your club has opened for requests
from the members' area is booked. Other people's bookings only appear as "Booked".

Under **Make a request** you choose the item, the purpose and the time and send it with
**Send request**. The managers confirm or reject it; you then receive an email. Under
**My requests and bookings** you see the status and can cancel with **Cancel booking**.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-daten.md:
---
key: page.portal_data
titel: My area › My data
routen: [/mein-bereich/daten]
stichworte: [address, change, bank details, information]
---

Here you see what the club has stored about you. You send changes, such as a new address, as a notice to the club; they apply once someone there has accepted them.

If your club has switched it on, you can also cancel your membership here. The earliest leaving date follows the notice period in the statutes; the club confirms the leaving date by email.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-firma.md:
---
key: page.portal_company
titel: My area › Employees
routen: [/mein-bereich/firma]
stichworte: [Company, Employee, report, deregister, Company fee, Employer]
---

Contact persons of a company that is a club member and pays the fee for employees see this item. You only see who belongs to the company, since when, and whether the fee is paid via the company. Address, date of birth, events and offices stay with the club.

**Report employee**: enter first name, last name and email address and choose **Report**. The person receives an email with the link to the club's online application, completes their details and confirms the application themselves. The link is valid for 30 days. The link is only valid for the email address you entered: the person has to apply with exactly that address. Each address can receive one report per day, and a company can send 20 reports per day. Once the club admits them, they belong to the company with “Fee via the household”. If the club has not enabled an online application, report employees directly to the club.

Deregister: choose **End fee payment** for a person and enter the last day the company pays for. This is not a resignation: the membership continues, afterwards the member pays themselves. The club and the member receive an email.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-helferdienste.md:
---
key: page.portal_helpers
titel: My area › Volunteer duties
routen: [/mein-bereich/helferdienste]
stichworte: [Helper, Duty, Shift, Roster, sign up, cancel, Calendar]
---

Here you see the published duty rosters of your club and your sub-units, for example for the
festival. Each shift shows how many places are still free.

**Sign me up** takes a free shift. HUBIplan checks whether the shift is already full, whether it
overlaps with another of your duties and whether you meet the minimum age. Some rosters allow
only a certain number of shifts per person; in others only the administration assigns people.

**Cancel duty** removes you again while the cancellation deadline is open. After that the shift
shows “Cancellation only via the administration”; please contact the administration then.

**My duties** lists all shifts you are signed up for. **Add to calendar** downloads them as a
calendar file. HUBIplan sends you a reminder email before the duty if your club has set this up.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-rechnungen.md:
---
key: page.portal_invoices
titel: My area › Invoices
routen: [/mein-bereich/rechnungen]
stichworte: [invoice, fee, paid, open]
---

This lists your invoices from the club, such as the annual fee, with their status. The club's treasurer answers questions about an invoice.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-rundschreiben.md:
---
key: page.portal_circulars
titel: My area › Messages
routen: [/mein-bereich/rundschreiben]
stichworte: [messages, circular, unsubscribe, email]
---

Here you read the messages (circulars) your club has sent you. The app calls them “Messages” too. You can unsubscribe from circulars of the “information” type; you will still receive official notices such as invitations.
en.seiten/mein-bereich-versammlungen.md:
---
key: page.portal_meetings
titel: My area › Meetings
routen: [/mein-bereich/versammlungen]
stichworte: [Meeting, General meeting, Invitation, Agenda, Minutes]
---

**Invitations** lists the meetings of your club and your units to which you are invited as a
member entitled to vote, with time, place and agenda.

If your club accepts motions, the meeting shows the deadline for them. **Submit a motion** lets
you enter a title and a reason, and **Submit motion** sends it. You then see whether it was added
to the agenda or why not. Until a decision has been made, **Withdraw** takes it back.

**Minutes** contains the approved minutes of recent years that your club has made available to
everyone entitled to vote. Click a title to download the minutes as a PDF. Minutes of board
meetings do not appear here.
en.seiten/mein-bereich.md:
---
key: page.portal
titel: My area › Overview
routen: [/mein-bereich]
stichworte: [member, my details, overview]
---

This is your area as a member. Here you find your card, your invoices, messages and the data the club has stored about you. Your club decides which of these appear.

As the contact person of an organisation you see the organisation's data here and report changes for it; first name, date of birth and gender do not apply. If you are also a member yourself, **My account** lists both areas separately, the organisation's with the addition “as contact person”.

You can reach your card, events and invoices from any other view too: under **My account** at the top right, the **My area** section lists **My ID card**, **My events** and **My invoices**. If you are a member of several clubs, each club is listed by name. The unit picker at the top only shows the areas you help run.

Under **Competitions** you find your entries (“What am I entered for?”) and your results on one page.

When the music module is enabled, here and, as a musician, under the item **Music** you also find your performances, rehearsals, sheet music and absences also appear here. Individual events are separated; meeting details, uniform and response status are labelled. **Accept** and **Decline** mark your current response. Known availability conflicts are also shown in text.

Under **Messages**, read received circulars with paragraphs, emphasis, lists and links. Attachments are listed by filename with the open circular. A link from the Android app returns to this exact circular and membership access after browser sign-in if needed. **To the overview** closes it; browser Back also works. Retry is available if loading fails.

The information-email setting confirms successful changes. You still receive official notices. If a change fails, the last confirmed setting is retained.

![Received circular with formatted text and an attachment](bild:mitteilungen-lesen)
en.seiten/mein-konto-anmeldung.md:
---
key: page.account_login
titel: My account › Sign-in & security
routen: [/mein-konto/anmeldung]
stichworte: [password, two-factor, 2FA, authenticator]
---

This is where you change your password and switch **Two-factor authentication** on or off. With it,
signing in needs a code from your phone in addition to your password. Anyone who manages roles,
runs exports, posts in the cash book, may see all members or reads the change log and outbox has
to set it up; for platform administration this applies immediately. Before sensitive actions such
as a full export HUBIplan asks for a code again (guide “Set up two-factor authentication”).

A new address under **Change sign-in email** only takes effect once you have confirmed it with the link sent to the new
address. If you have no password of your own and only sign in with links, you also have to confirm
the change with the link sent to your previous address. After the change your other browsers are
signed out; the app stays connected.

If someone enters a wrong password for your account several times in a row, signing in with a
password is blocked for a few minutes, but only on unknown devices. On devices you have signed in
with before, and with a passkey, you can still get in. You will receive an email about it.
en.seiten/mein-konto-app.md:
---
key: page.account_app
titel: My account › App & other instances
routen: [/mein-konto/app]
stichworte: [app, phone, device, pair, instance, AI assistant, MCP]
---

This is where you connect the HUBIplan app on your phone to your account and see which devices are connected. You disconnect a device you no longer use here. Below, you link accounts on other HUBIplan instances so you can sign in there with this account.

Under “AI assistants” you find the address for connecting an AI assistant such as Claude or ChatGPT, and the list of connected assistants. You end a connection with **Disconnect** (see [Connect AI assistants to HUBIplan](/hilfe/ki-assistent-verbinden)).

If your app access or devices cannot be retrieved, the error offers **Reload**. Only a successfully loaded empty device list means that no device is connected.
en.seiten/mein-konto-benachrichtigungen.md:
---
key: page.account_notifications
titel: My account › Notifications
routen: [/mein-konto/benachrichtigungen]
stichworte: [Tasks, Reminders, Email, Push]
---

Set your task sharing notices and email and push reminders here. These defaults apply to your account across all units. Each task with a due date can have its own channels and reminder times. Due tasks remain highlighted even when messages are disabled.

You can hide task titles in push messages. You can also choose to move completed private one-off tasks to the trash after twelve months. This retention option starts disabled; recurring task history is retained.
en.seiten/mein-konto-briefvorlage.md:
---
key: page.account_letter
titel: My account › Letter template & signature
routen: [/mein-konto/briefvorlage, /briefvorlage]
stichworte: [letter, Word, template, signature, letterhead]
---

As a board member or with a role in a sub-unit, you create a Word template here with your unit's letterhead, your position and how to reach you. You can also store a signature that HUBIplan puts on receipts, for example.
en.seiten/mein-konto.md:
---
key: page.account
titel: My account › Profile
routen: [/mein-konto]
stichworte: [profile, name, language, appearance, dark mode, quick actions, learning aids]
---

This is where you set everything that only concerns you: your name, the **Display language** and
whether HUBIplan shows you learning aids. The settings apply in every unit you work in.

Under **Appearance** you choose **Same as device**, **Light** or **Dark**. In dark mode, HUBIplan shows sign-in, the start page, events, My account and My area in dark colours; administration (such as members or finances) stays light. With **Same as device**, HUBIplan follows the setting of your phone or computer. The choice applies on all devices where you are signed in. In the dark, HUBIplan adjusts the club colours so that links and buttons stay easy to read.

Under **Home**, **Show quick actions on the home page** decides whether the home page shows its buttons. You choose which actions appear, and in which order, on the home page under **Customise**. If you made a selection of your own there, **Show the suggestion everywhere** restores your roles' suggestion in all units.

Open the other sections through **My account** at the top right, for example **Sign-in & security**
for your password and two-factor authentication. The same menu shows your email address and lets you **Sign out**.
en.seiten/meldungen.md:
---
key: page.entries
titel: Entries
modul: entries
rechte: [entries.submit, entries.manage]
routen: [/meldungen]
stichworte: [entry, invitation to tender, team, organiser, registration]
---

Under Entries you register teams, people and details with an organiser, for example for a tournament or a parade. You can send the entry as a letter, email or spreadsheet, report changes later and pass a call for entries on to your own sub-units.

When creating a call for entries, your input is saved only when you choose **Create**. If you cancel or leave after changing something, HUBIplan asks for confirmation. **Continue editing** retains your input; **Discard** leaves the draft without saving.

If results from a linked competition cannot be loaded, **Reload** retries the request. When no competition is linked to a call for entries, the results section remains hidden.

With English selected, submission methods, validation hints, statuses and form actions are also shown in English. Your titles, club details and previously generated correspondence retain their content or the club language.
en.seiten/mitglieder-aemter.md:
---
key: page.members_offices
titel: Members › Offices
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/aemter]
stichworte: [office, board, position, term]
---

This lists the unit's offices, such as chair, treasurer or secretary, with their holders and terms. Offices are not rights: what someone may do in HUBIplan is set by the roles under Settings.

With **Assign** you give an office to a new person, for example after the annual general meeting. You pick the person from the member list and the date. The dialog says beforehand whether the role has permissions and where an invitation goes. If the office is held, it ends the predecessor’s term on the day before; the box is ticked by default. Afterwards it points to the imprint and letterhead if the role appears there.

At the top, pick the club or a sub-unit, such as a platoon, under **Unit**. Offices of a sub-unit are assigned the same way with **Assign**; no account is created and no email is sent. Current holders are ended there with **End**. The sub-unit’s page and its workspace show the same list under “Who has which role?”.
en.seiten/mitglieder-aenderungen.md:
---
key: page.members_changes
titel: Members › Data changes
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/anfragen/aenderungen]
stichworte: [change, address, member area, review]
---

Members report changed details in the member area, such as a new address or bank account. Here you review each notice and apply it to the record or decline it. Nothing changes in the record until you agree.
en.seiten/mitglieder-akte.md:
---
key: page.member_file
titel: Members › Member record
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/:id]
stichworte: [record, master data, periods, leaving, honours]
---

The tabs follow the order of work: **Personal data**, **Membership**, **Fees**, **Roles and account**, **Competitions**, **Music**, **Photo & website**, **Additional fields** and **History**. Tabs for modules that are switched off are hidden. **Photo & website** brings together the photo, photo requests, publication and the membership card. **Music** shows a short musician profile with the instruments; edit it via **Open in music area**. Issued equipment is listed under **Membership**. On a phone, choose the section from the **Area** list. The header shows the name, photo (otherwise the initials), status, membership number, membership type, units and current offices. **Call** and **Email** appear when a phone number or email address is recorded. **More actions** holds request photo, print membership card, record leaving, and access report and deletion.

![Member record with header, “At a glance” and tabs](bild:mitgliedsakte)

At the top, **At a glance** shows up to four tiles: **Member since** (with duration and next jubilee), **Fees** (open invoices and total, marked red when overdue), **Account** (member area, app, two-factor, last sign-in) and **Equipment** (items issued). A tile only appears if you may see the matching tab and there is something to show; clicking it opens the tab.

Next to gender is the **Title**: choose Dr., Dr. Dr., Prof. or Prof. Dr., or enter your own with **other title …** (e.g. Dipl.-Ing.). The title appears in the record header, in the addresses of letters and invoices (“Dr. Max Muster”) and in the formal salutation of circulars (“Sehr geehrter Herr Dr. Muster”); the informal salutation stays without a title. On the website it only appears if “Show titles before names” is switched on there. HUBIplan copies an additional field “Titel” into the fixed field once; the additional field remains.

For an organisation as a member (company, association, public body …), the master data show the name addition, legal form, register, VAT ID, website and size (e.g. employees or inhabitants) for fees by size instead of first name, date of birth and gender. In the member list, filter with **organisations only** or **persons only**.

In the **Contact persons** section you record who speaks for the organisation. Choose **Select member** if the person is a member themselves; name and contact details then come from their file. Otherwise enter name, function, email address and phone. Exactly one is the **Primary contact**. The settings **receives circulars**, **receives invoices**, **represents at meetings** define who is responsible for what. You set up a separate member area login for each contact person on the **Roles and account** tab; contacts who have one are marked **Member access**. If the contact person is a member themselves, they choose after signing in whether they act for themselves or for the organisation. Instead of a photo, an organisation has a **Logo**; it needs no consent and also appears on the membership card. When you remove a contact person, their contact details are deleted immediately.

For members under 18 the section is called **Legal guardians**. There you enter parents or a legal guardian, freely or as a linked member. With **receives circulars** they also get circulars to the child by email. You set up their login on the **Roles and account** tab, as for contact persons; parents with several children choose after signing in whom they act for. Four weeks before the 18th birthday the guardians get an email; on the birthday their access and entry end automatically.

If the person belongs to a household or a company, the Master data tab shows a section with its name, their role and the other members. You assign and remove them under [Members › Households and companies](/mitglieder/haushalte).

The **Fees** tab lists the member’s invoices with the outstanding amount and, if SEPA is switched on, their mandates (with the right to view fees and invoices). Open an invoice by its number.

In the **Fees** tab, under **Billing address**, you set where invoices and reminders go if not to the member's address, e.g. a company's accounts department, a town's treasury or a child's parents. It also holds the billing email, purchase order number and Leitweg-ID; the last two are printed on every invoice. Without a separate billing address, an invoice to an organisation is marked “attn.” of the contact person marked “receives invoices”, and the email goes to them.

The record shows everything about a person: master data, memberships with periods and membership types, honours, offices, contact details, SEPA mandate and photo. Changes are saved shortly after you type; you can undo them at the top right if needed. You record leaving as the end of the membership; the record is kept. Honours are in the **Membership** tab. In the **Roles and account** tab you see the person's roles and enable or block the member area. **Assign role** opens the same dialog as under Members › Offices.

In the **Membership** tab, use **Edit** next to a unit membership to correct its start and end dates, including past memberships. A blank end date means the membership continues. Apply the correction with **Save**. Overlaps with other unit memberships are checked. To add a past membership in one step, pick the unit, enter “from” and “until”, then click **Add**. Without “until”, the membership runs until today. Units that are no longer active are listed too, marked “(inactive)”; for them “until” is required. If HUBIplan reports an overlap, it names the affected membership with its exact dates; the check works by day even when the file shows only years.

Under **Privacy** you can download the access report as a ZIP. For former members, this is also where you delete their data on request. As after the deletion period, only the name, year of birth and membership periods then remain, for the club's history. If the person objects to that too, “Remove name from chronicle and honours” then removes their name from dignities, companions, honours and competition results. Photos of these dignities are deleted as well.
en.seiten/mitglieder-anfragen.md:
---
key: page.members_requests
titel: Members › Changes and transfers
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/anfragen]
stichworte: [requests, data change, change notice, transfer, transfer request, approval]
---

Transfer requests arise when a member is to move from one unit to another. The releasing side agrees or declines; only then is the transfer saved.
en.seiten/mitglieder-antraege.md:
---
key: page.members_applications
titel: Members › Membership applications
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/antraege]
stichworte:
  [membership application, joining, online application, admission, approval, become a member]
---

Membership applications from the online form and from booth mode arrive here. An application only appears once the applicant has confirmed it with the link in the email; HUBIplan deletes unconfirmed applications after 48 hours.

The list shows name, membership type, date received and status for each application. Clicking the number opens the review page with all details, possible matches among existing people, the approvals and the history.

What admission requires is set under [Members › Setup › Online application](/mitglieder/einrichtung/antrag): one person decides, several roles must approve, or the general meeting decides. Whoever is to approve also sees the application under “To do” on the home page.

On admission, HUBIplan creates the member and takes over a granted SEPA mandate, the consents and, for minors, the legal guardians as contact persons. Declined and withdrawn applications are deleted after the configured period.
en.seiten/mitglieder-ehrungen.md:
---
key: page.members_honours_setup
titel: Members › Setup › Honours
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/einrichtung/ehrungen]
stichworte: [honour, decoration, badge, award]
---

Here you define which honours exist, for example decorations or pins, and whether they come from the club or the umbrella association. An honour is then awarded in the member's record.
en.seiten/mitglieder-einrichtung-qualifikat:
---
key: page.members_qualifications_setup
titel: Members › Setup › Qualifications
modul: qualifications
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/einrichtung/qualifikationen]
stichworte:
  [qualification, certificate, validity, reminder, criminal record certificate, inspection note]
---

Here you define which certificates you keep track of, such as first aid, coach licence, youth
leader, firearms competence or range officer. Nothing is predefined; under **Suggestions** one
click adds a common type that you can then adjust.

Each type has a **Usual validity in months**: it suggests the expiry date when recording
(empty: unlimited). **Reminder days before expiry** sets when the member receives an email and
from when the certificate counts as “expires soon”.

**Inspection note only (e.g. criminal record certificate)**: HUBIplan only records that and when
the certificate was inspected. There is no remark field and no document; you never store the
content of the criminal record certificate.

A type that is recorded for members can only be **archived**; the entries are kept. Roles with
“Edit organisation data” may edit the types.
en.seiten/mitglieder-einrichtung.md:
---
key: page.members_setup
titel: Members › Setup
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/einrichtung]
stichworte: [setup, membership types, custom fields, honours, online application]
---

Under Setup you decide how member administration works for you: membership types, custom fields, honours, anniversaries, the online application and what members see in the member area. You usually set this up once at the start.
en.seiten/mitglieder-entwicklung.md:
---
key: page.members_development
titel: Members › Development
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/entwicklung]
stichworte: [statistics, development, age structure, joinings]
---

Development shows how membership numbers have changed over the years: joinings, leavings, age structure and membership types. The figures are based on the periods in the records.

After you change the selection, previous results are hidden until the new request finishes. If loading fails, **Reload** retries the same selection.

The average age uses completed years on the reference date. On average it is therefore about half a year below the exact age.
en.seiten/mitglieder-haushalte.md:
---
key: page.members_households
titel: Members › Households and companies
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/haushalte]
stichworte: [household, family, family letter, one letter, postage, company, employees]
---

Here you link members who belong together. **Families and households** lists members who live together, **Companies** lists members whose fees a company pays. A member belongs to at most one household and at most one company at the same time.

![Families and households with their members](bild:haushalte-liste)

With **Create household** you enter a name, e.g. “Muster family”. **Add member** lets you search for a member, choose the role (**Adult** or **Child**; HUBIplan suggests it from the age) and the date from which they belong. If the member already belongs to another household, HUBIplan asks whether to move them; the previous membership in it then ends the day before. **Remove** ends the membership in the household today; it stays visible as a past entry (**Show former members**). When a member leaves the club, their membership in the household ends on the exit date. You can delete a household without current members.

![Card of a household with role and date for each member](bild:haushalt-karte)

**Find suggestions** shows current members with the same address who are not yet together in a household. **Create as household** takes over a suggestion; members who already belong to another household stay there.

One letter instead of four: A circular to members combines the letters to a household at the same address into one letter, and likewise emails to the same address. It goes to the first adult; the address block reads e.g. “Familie Erika und Max Muster” and the salutation “Sehr geehrte Familie Muster” or “Liebe Familie Muster” (letters stay in the club language). Anyone who lives elsewhere or has their own email address gets their own copy. You can switch this off per circular under **Recipient**. Circulars for an event (with a reply link per person) and texts with {Mitgliedsjahre} or {Jubiläumsjahre} still go out individually.

In the member list, the **Household** filter shows members with or without a household. In the member file, the household appears on the Master data tab together with its other members.

![Companies with the members they pay for](bild:firmen-liste)

**Fee via the household**: With the Fees module, a household or company pays its members' fees with one invoice. Under **Payer and mandate** you enter who pays: a **Member** (usually a parent), a **Person without membership** with their own address, an **Organisation member** or a business partner. When adding a member, or later with **Fee via the household**, you decide per member that their fee goes on this invoice; for companies this is preselected, for families it is not. A fee goes via at most one household or company. Without a payer, fees are invoiced individually as before; the checklist before the fee run points this out. Direct debits use the paying member's mandate; if a person without membership or a business partner pays, you record the mandate here on the household. You set the family or company fee under Finance › Set up › Fee rates. The payer sees the invoice in the member area; the others see their line there.

Companies in the member area: if an organisation member pays for a company, its contact persons with access see the company's people under My area › Employees (only name, since when, and whether the fee is paid via the company). They can report new employees, who then get the online application and belong to the company with “Fee via the household” automatically once admitted, and end the payment for someone from a date. Then only the link to the company ends, and you receive an email at the club's contact address.
en.seiten/mitglieder-import.md:
---
key: page.members_import
titel: Members › Import
modul: members
rechte: [members.edit]
routen: [/mitglieder/import]
stichworte: [import, Excel, CSV, spreadsheet, migration]
---

With the import you take over an existing member list from a spreadsheet (Excel or CSV). HUBIplan first shows how it reads each column and which people already exist. Nothing is saved until you confirm. Rows without a membership number are given the next free numbers in turn when importing, counting the numbers in the file as well.

The import recognises organisations as members (company, association, authority …) by the column “Typ” with the value “Organisation”. For them there are the columns “Namenszusatz” (name suffix), “Rechtsform” (legal form) and “Ansprechpartner Name”, “Ansprechpartner Vorname”, “Ansprechpartner Funktion”, “Ansprechpartner E-Mail” and “Ansprechpartner Telefon” (contact person). Further contact persons go in further rows with the same membership number; the first becomes the primary contact. First name and date of birth stay empty for organisations. If a name without a type looks like an organisation (e.g. “… GmbH” or “… e. V.”), the check reports it instead of guessing.

A separate billing address (for people and organisations, e.g. a company’s accounts department or the parents of a child) goes in the columns “Rechnungsempfänger” (invoice recipient), “Rechnung z. Hd.” (attn.), “Rechnung Straße oder Postfach” (street or PO box), “Rechnung PLZ” (postcode), “Rechnung Ort” (town) and “Rechnung Land” (country), plus “Rechnungs-E-Mail” (billing email), “Bestellnummer” (purchase order number) and “Leitweg-ID”. These are the same columns as in the export. A separate address needs street (or PO box) and town; billing email, purchase order number and Leitweg-ID also work on their own.

You import households and companies with the columns “Haushalt” (household) and “Firma” (company) (same name = same household or company; existing ones with that name are extended), “Rolle im Haushalt” (role in the household) (Erwachsener or Kind) and “Beitrag über” (fee via) (Haushalt, Firma or empty). The export has the same columns. Undoing the import removes households it created that are then empty.

A few rules during the check: HUBIplan adds the leading 0 that Excel drops from numbers to a four-digit postcode (country Germany or empty) and shows this in the preview. Numbers such as “1.000” without a comma are ambiguous and are rejected; please write “1000” or use a decimal comma. If several rows for the same person contain different values in a custom field, or different details for a period with the same entry date, the check reports the contradiction. An invalid date in a date custom field is an error in that row.

Here you set which anniversaries HUBIplan shows (for example 25, 40 or 50 years) and how the length of membership is counted, for example whether periods in other units count.

Nothing changes in the record until you confirm the leaving date. The member receives a confirmation of receipt when sending and an email with the result after your decision.

Here you decide whether members get their own access and what they may see and change there, such as their card, invoices or their own details. You also set how photos for the card and record are collected.

Under **Cancellation by the member** you switch on that members can cancel in the member area. Set **Notice period** and **Leaving takes effect** as your statutes require, for example three months to the end of the financial year. HUBIplan calculates the earliest leaving date from this. You confirm cancellations under [Members › Cancellations](/mitglieder/anfragen/kuendigungen).

If the operator has configured Apple or Google Wallet, the **Membership card** switch appears:
it lets members save their card in Apple Wallet or Google Wallet (default: on). Switching it off
invalidates saved Google Wallet passes. A card is only valid anyway if the verification page shows
it as valid after scanning the QR code.

en.seiten/mitglieder-online-antrag.md:
---
key: page.members_application_setup
titel: Members › Setup › Online application
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder/einrichtung/antrag]
stichworte:
  [
    online application,
    membership application,
    joining form,
    QR code,
    booth mode,
    statutes,
    approval,
  ]
---

Here you set up the form people use to become members online. Each club has its own form with its own address.

- **Membership types in the form**: which types can be applied for, with name and short explanation. The form shows the annual fee if a fee rate for the type is set under Finances.
- **Fields**: phone, gender, date of birth, sub-unit, desired start date and message are required, optional or not asked. Custom fields can be added.
- **Fee and direct debit**: the SEPA mandate can be offered or required in the application once the creditor ID is entered.
- **Confirmations and consents**: statutes and fee regulations with their version, the privacy notice and voluntary consents such as photos.
- **Signature**: either the confirmed email address is enough, or a signature on the device or on the printed application is needed.
- **Minors**: whether minors may apply online with their legal guardians, and from what age. If someone gives no date of birth (field optional or not asked), the form asks whether the person is of age.
- Family application: adults can register further family members at the same address in the same application (first name, optionally their own last name, date of birth and membership type). On acceptance everyone is admitted and linked into a household “… family”; with the Fees module the applicant pays for everyone via their mandate, and minors get the applicant as their guardian. Please check yourselves whether a further person is already on record; duplicate entries can be merged.
- **Who decides?**: as your statutes require, also with several roles, a minimum number and the approval of the sub-unit.

**Share the form** shows the address and QR code, optionally with a preselected sub-unit, and the links for booth mode.

Retention: HUBIplan deletes unconfirmed applications after 48 hours, rejected and withdrawn ones after the period you set. After your decision, the link from the confirmation email only shows the status, no details and no PDF, and expires after 30 days. On acceptance HUBIplan files the application as a PDF; you still find it with the application. Twelve months after acceptance the individual details of the application are removed because they are in the member record. The number, decision, approvals and the PDF remain.

“Soon” means: within the days set as reminder for the type. Expired and soon-expiring
certificates are also listed on the home page under “To do”.

This lists the holders of your club's titles, such as kings and princes, year by year. This forms the chronicle, which can also appear on the website.

Name searches ignore letter case and normalize Unicode spelling variants; “ß” and “ss” are treated as equal. Other selected filters still apply.

Ordinals (“Hans II.”) count per first name, ignoring upper and lower case; hyphen and space count the same (“Hans-Peter” = “Hans Peter”, but not “Hans”). Set exceptions as a manual ordinal. When you link a name entered as text to a member, HUBIplan asks whether further entries with the same name should be linked too; otherwise the same person counts twice. The list is sorted by year or start date.

---
key: page.members
titel: Members
modul: members
rechte: [members.view]
routen: [/mitglieder]
stichworte: [member list, search, filter, export]
---

The list shows all members of the selected unit. At the top you search by name, email or
number; next to it you filter by status, membership type or gender. Clicking a name opens the
record with all periods, honours and contact details.

Each search word must match, but one may occur in the name and another in the email
address or number. Email addresses are found by the full address (`erika@example.org`) or
from the @ onwards (`@example.org` for everyone with that domain); parts without @ only
search names and numbers. Names are searched without regard to case, and `ß` and `ss` are
treated alike. Name sorting places umlauts with their base letter (`ä` with `a`).
Equal names have a fixed order so that moving between pages remains stable.

![The member list with search and filters](bild:mitglieder-liste)

On a phone, search stays visible. The Filters button opens status, membership type and other restrictions; the number indicates how many filters are set. **More actions** contains export and membership cards. For organisations, the Excel export contains type, name suffix, legal form and the primary contact; all contact persons are on the second sheet “Ansprechpartner”. The separate billing address with billing email, purchase order number and Leitweg-ID can be included as columns of their own. **Per page** lets you choose 10, 20 or 50 results; phones initially show 10. For multiple pages, navigation is available above and below the results. Your selection and page size are retained when you open a record and return. Small screens show name and membership type; open the record for other details.
en.seiten/musik.md:
---
key: page.music
titel: Music
modul: music
rechte: [music.view]
routen: [/musik]
stichworte: [Musik, Instrument, Auftritt, Besetzung]
---

# Music and performances

The music sub-items are in the sidebar, grouped as Performances (Overview, Performances, Availability), Musicians (Musicians, Rehearsals and sheet music checkout), Sheet music (Sheet music library) and Setup (Instrumentation templates). Each item has its own address, e.g. `/musik/noten`. Instruments and uniforms are under Equipment & rooms, batch payouts under Finance (Book) and the personal reminders under Tasks.

**Performance overview** combines staffing, pending responses, known conflicts,
sheet music requirements and permitted settlement issues. Select a period and choose
**Update overview** when needed. Each issue links to staffing, the programme or the
performance settlement. “Prepared” refers only to information you can access; it does not
confirm attendance. Missing planning details remain open. Finance issues require
cashbook read access. Cancelled performances are marked separately. Each page shows
twelve performances.

The platform enables Music per organization. Roles need music viewing or editing permission. Performances also require calendar viewing permission.

Section navigation remains visible on every music page: **Performances**, **Musicians**, **Sheet music library**, **Rehearsals and sheet music checkout**, **Availability** and **Instrumentation templates**. Under **Performances**, switch between performances, required instrumentation and assignments; under **Musicians**, switch between profiles and instrumental skills. The active section is marked. Navigation and form fields stack on smaller screens.

The search field is named after the view, for example **Search performances** or **Search musicians**, and filters it, for example by name, instrument or performance. Add new items with the matching button, such as **New performance**; an empty view explains what belongs there and offers the same button. **Search sheet music** filters the current library view. Empty lists and searches without matches show a message. Performance cards group programme, instrumentation, settlement, tasks and calendar links; detail pages show the associated performance above the heading. Totals and programme durations appear in labelled summaries. Responses and availability conflicts use consistent text badges, including in the member area.

Create a musician from an existing member or enter a guest name and contact details. Pick the member via the search: type at least two letters of the name and click a match. The member record shows a short profile with the instruments on its **Music** tab and leads here via **Open in music area**. Record instruments and sections or parts under **Instrumental skills**, marking the main instrument. Deactivate guests when no longer needed.

Create an individual event in your own calendar, then select it under **Performances**. Add customer, meeting time and place, setup, uniform, formation and notes. Performance times and location remain in the calendar. Use individual events for recurring performances. Open **Performance tasks** to manage tasks through the existing task workspace.

Record required player counts per instrument and part, then assign musicians with matching skills. Each musician can be assigned once per performance. The overview counts accepted and missing players per position.

Members can accept or decline their assignments under **My area**. Calendar cancellations remain visible. Calendar access restrictions also apply to performance administration.

For guests, open **Plan instrumentation** → **Manage guest invitation**, create a personal link and share it confidentially. Guests need no account and see only their own assignment, meeting details, setup, uniform, formation and programme. They can accept or decline; known conflicts prevent acceptance. Other musicians, contact information and settlements remain hidden. Links expire seven days after the performance, with a maximum lifetime of 180 days. **Revoke invitation link** blocks access immediately; **Create new invitation link** replaces the previous link. Changing the guest email address revokes existing links.

To send an invitation, enter the musician's **Email address for guest invitations** and explicitly choose **Send guest invitation**. This also enables change notices and reminders while access remains active. Creating or copying a link alone does not enable automatic email. Personal links are redacted in the outbox; reopen guest management to share them again. If delivery fails, retry or share the link confidentially.

Active members with enabled member access receive neutral outbox notices for new performance assignments, changes to dates, meeting details, instrumentation positions or programmes, and cancellations. The background service checks every five minutes and combines intermediate changes. Messages contain only the member-area link. Existing assignments do not generate another initial invitation when the feature is introduced. Guests receive automatic notices only after an explicit guest invitation is sent.

For each performance, **Reminder days before (0 = off)** sets the reminder window for pending responses (0 to 30 days, default 3). It uses the earliest meeting, setup or performance time. Each current information version receives at most one reminder, no earlier than one day after an invitation or change. Accepted or declined assignments and past or cancelled performances are not reminded. Failed deliveries are retried; failed attempts remain visible in the outbox.

## Fee templates and partial payouts

Under **Performance settlement** → **Musician remuneration**, finance editors can **Manage fee templates**. Templates contain fee and allowance amounts in EUR. Archiving prevents new use; existing remuneration retains its copied amounts.

For a batch settlement, select an active template and assignments without existing remuneration. **Select all without remuneration** selects assignments without confirming attendance. Confirm attendance separately for each musician. **Create remuneration drafts** creates drafts with expenses set to zero. Add actual expenses and check attendance individually, then approve after the performance as usual. Invalid selections are rejected together. Existing remuneration is never overwritten.

You can assign multiple recorded payouts from Finance to an approved remuneration claim. Each booking is used fully and only once and must not exceed the outstanding amount. **Partially paid**, **Paid** and **Outstanding remuneration** also show the current balance in the member's own area. An active partial payment prevents approval reversal. Reversing the booking in Finance increases the outstanding amount again. Assigning a booking does not initiate a bank transfer.

## Instrumentation templates and batch assignment

Under **Instrumentation templates**, use **Create template** to store instruments, parts and required player counts. Each part may appear only once. Clear **Active** to archive a template. Editing requires music editing permission; read-only users can view templates.

Open **Plan instrumentation** for a performance, select an active template and review its positions. **Apply template** adds missing parts and increases required counts if needed. Other positions and existing assignments and responses are preserved. Resolve ambiguous duplicate positions first. **Save performance instrumentation as template** copies the required positions into a new template without musicians or responses. Template changes affect performances only when applied again.

Under **Batch assignment**, select multiple matching active members or guests. Choose one position for multi-instrumentalists; each musician profile is assigned only once. Pending and accepted assignments reserve places. Already assigned musicians and existing declines are not offered again; edit their existing assignment individually.

**Request selected musicians** creates pending assignments. If the selection exceeds available places, contains invalid references, lacks skills or has known availability conflicts, nothing from the request is saved. Retries create no duplicate assignments. Existing calendar permissions apply to performances. General exports include templates.

## Availability and replacements

Under **Availability**, manage absences for active members and guests. Members can manage **My absences** in their own area. Only start and end are recorded, without reasons. Adjacent periods do not overlap. Other known performances including meeting and setup time, rehearsal series and accepted calendar events in the same association are considered. Individual declines and moved occurrences take effect immediately. Other associations and private calendars without an association response are not checked; plan travel and buffer time yourself.

Planning shows **Absent**, **Scheduling conflict**, **Declined this event** or **No known conflict**, without revealing private calendar content. Assignment and acceptance check again before saving. No known conflict does not constitute acceptance. Later changes highlight conflicts for existing assignments without automatically changing responses or remuneration. Decline the assignment separately if needed.

For a declined assignment, open **Find replacement** under **Plan instrumentation**. Conflict-free musicians with matching parts are offered, with matching primary instruments first. Select and request a replacement; the earlier decline remains. **Show all candidates** exits the filter; **Reset selection** discards an unsaved selection. General exports include absences.

## Performance settlement

Open **Performance settlement** from the performance. Music and calendar viewing permissions and the enabled cash book with finance viewing permission are required. Editing requires finance editing permission. Record the agreed fee, travel costs and additional services as gross amounts in EUR. With invoice editing permission, create a draft in the existing e-invoice editor. The customer and total gross amount must match the agreement. Enter net amounts, tax categories and invoice details explicitly, then validate, issue, send and manage receipts using the invoice workspace. Each performance links one customer invoice.

Record fees, allowances and documented expenses per assignment. Confirm attendance after the performance, then approve remuneration. Approved amounts are locked. Before payment, void approval and reopen the draft for corrections. Members see only their own approved remuneration in their personal area. Finance administrators handle guest remuneration.

Record payments with receipts as expenses in the cash book first. Search the booking text and link each matching booking in full. Each remuneration permits multiple partial payments up to the outstanding balance. Link other performance expenses in the same way. Each booking can be used once. Linking does not initiate a bank transfer.

Reverse incorrect payments in the cash book. The original link remains visible, while the outstanding balance increases and can be linked to a corrected payment. The overview distinguishes agreed and invoiced amounts, actual income and expenses and their cash result. Approved remuneration is shown separately and does not indicate a completed payment.

General exports and financial audit exports include agreements, remuneration and booking links. Financial retention and anonymization include settlement notes.

Use **Replace cancelled invoice** after fully cancelling the customer invoice. Then correct the agreement and create a replacement invoice. Previous invoices remain linked and traceable in the audit export.

## Sheet music and programmes

Use **Import sheet music catalogue** to select a UTF-8 CSV up to 2 MB with at most 1000 data rows. The **Download CSV template** lists all columns; `title` and `arrangement` are required. Use semicolons or commas as separators. Each row describes an arrangement and optionally stock for an instrumental part. Without an instrument, only the arrangement is created. **Preview import** shows new pieces, arrangements, stock and errors without saving anything. **Import reviewed sheet music catalogue** explicitly imports the reviewed data together. Identical entries are skipped; conflicting details, changed stock counts or ambiguous existing entries must be resolved first. Existing details and archived arrangements are not overwritten or reactivated. Create a new preview if the file or catalogue changes; previews expire after 30 minutes. Add digital sheet music through the existing document library.

For each performance, **Programme list as PDF** and **Parts list as PDF** complement the existing CSV exports. Printouts include performance, location, creation timestamp and page numbers. The programme lists order, breaks, encores and durations; the parts list shows format, available and missing copies, copies held by assigned musicians, missing musicians, storage locations and licence notes. Check current stock and usage rights before printing.

Open **Music** → **Sheet music library**. Create pieces with composers, then editions/arrangements with arrangers, publishers, duration in seconds, difficulty, instrumentation and licence notes. Archive unused arrangements. Record required musicians, copy counts, storage locations and concert or march book format for each instrument and part. Record full scores separately. Stocks at multiple locations are added together for the same part; the highest player requirement applies.

With **In the repertoire on the website** a piece appears with title and composer in the “Repertoire” section of the club website. Switch the section on under **Website** → **Menu and sections**.

Upload digital files in the existing document library, then link them to an arrangement and optionally a part under **Sheet music documents**. Document viewing permission is also required to link and open files. Access changes and deletions apply immediately. Music permissions do not extend document access. Record licence and usage notes; a stock count or file does not grant copying or performance rights.

Open **Musical programme** on a performance. Add pieces and encores with an arrangement, and breaks with their own duration. A blank duration uses the arrangement duration; an explicit value overrides it. Edit, remove and move items up/down. Regular duration includes breaks; encore and total durations are shown separately. Zero indicates an unknown duration and is highlighted.

Preparation compares required instruments and parts against planned instrumentation and active musicians who accepted assignments. Names are compared without case sensitivity or surrounding whitespace; different instrument names remain distinct. Missing musicians, planned counts and missing copies in the chosen format are visible. Copies in the other format do not count. Repeated pieces need one set per format. Missing instrumentation is highlighted. Changes to stock and arrangement duration affect existing programmes.

Download programme and part lists as CSV. Use **Sheet music preparation tasks** to create preparation tasks linked to the event in the existing task workspace. Programmes require music and calendar viewing permissions; editing requires music editing permission. General exports include the catalogue and programmes. Digital files remain in the existing document export.

## Instruments and uniforms

When the inventory module and inventory viewing permission are also enabled, the item **Instruments and uniforms** appears under Equipment & rooms. Editing requires both music and inventory editing permissions. **Link inventory item as music equipment** selects an existing inventory item; create items and maintain photos, documents and tasks in inventory management. Inventory number and condition remain shared. Use **Edit equipment details** for type, instrument, size/specification and the next maintenance date.

**Issue equipment** assigns an item to an active musician with a return deadline and handover note. Issuing equipment to members also requires member viewing permission. The inventory location changes to that member. For guests, the location is marked for review with a reference to the music issue; the guest assignment appears in Music. Items already issued, defective or retired cannot be issued again. Overdue returns are marked.

**Record equipment return** confirms condition and destination: explicitly restore the previous storage location or enter a complete new address. Inaccessible member locations must be replaced with a valid destination. **Record maintenance** saves completed maintenance with date, condition, note and next due date. Schedule planned maintenance in equipment details. The last 100 issues and maintenance entries are displayed; general exports retain all records. Correct issues and returns through these workflows rather than Undo in inventory history. An outstanding issue prevents deletion. The inventory record links back to music equipment when music viewing permission is available.

## Rehearsals and personal sheet music

Open **Rehearsals and sheet music checkout** and link events or series from your own calendar. Dates, location, recurrence and cancellations remain in the existing calendar. Rehearsal focus and pieces form the shared series template. Assign musicians and deactivate assignments no longer required. Administrators record guest responses.

Under **Upcoming rehearsals**, open **Edit rehearsal programme** for an occurrence. **This occurrence only** saves its own focus and pieces, including an empty programme. **Entire series** loads and changes the shared template; occurrences with their own programmes keep their contents. **Use series programme** removes the override and inherits the current template again. Rehearsal planning and rehearsal pieces continue to edit the template. Moved occurrences keep their programmes. After a recurrence rule change, programmes without a matching original start need to be planned again. Programme changes preserve attendance responses.

The overview covers the past 14 days and next 90 days. Each response belongs to the original occurrence start from the calendar rule, including moved occurrences. Changing the series rule requires new responses. Cancelled or started rehearsals cannot be answered. Missing responses are visible.

Current members with an active musician profile see their own rehearsals and performances with their effective programmes and focus under **My area**. **Sheet music for this rehearsal** shows matching permitted files. Downloads still require the document library’s member permissions and a matching part or skill. Removed pieces no longer grant access unless another own event needs them. Rehearsals use the displayed past 14 and next 90 days; cancelled rehearsals and declined invitations grant no sheet music access. Restricted, deleted and unrelated files remain inaccessible.

Record musician, part, quantity and return date for checkouts. Each checkout reduces available stock. Partial returns are recorded with timestamps. Outstanding checkouts prevent reducing or repurposing stock. Overdue returns are highlighted; members see their own outstanding quantities. Preparation distinguishes available copies from copies already held by assigned musicians.

New rehearsal assignments and upcoming pending responses generate neutral notices through the existing outbox. The hourly job reminds once per occurrence within the configured number of days; 0 disables reminders. Notices link to the member area and contain no sheet music attachments or confidential event details. Guests without member access do not receive these notices. Preparation tasks and other calendar communication remain in the existing task/calendar workspace.

General exports include rehearsal, response and checkout data. The additive migration includes tables, RLS and quantity constraints; export the new history before rolling back.

After an inventory item with closed issues is deleted, the existing 30-day trash period applies; its music links are then removed. Items with an outstanding issue are excluded from permanent cleanup.

## Batch payouts

In **Batch payouts** (Finance, Book), select approved outstanding remuneration, a bank account
and an execution date. Check each holder, IBAN and optional BIC. Saving a run for
review reserves claims and freezes amounts and recipient details.
Download the SEPA file (pain.001.001.09, EUR), check it and approve it at your bank.
Repeated downloads contain the same instruction; do not submit the file twice.
Export does not execute transfers or mark claims paid. The file requests individual
bank entries. Assign each actual expense in the performance settlement; bank account
and amount must match. Reversed bookings reopen reconciliation.
Cancelling a run releases claims; submitted transfers must also be stopped at the bank.
Finance read access permits inspection; edit access is required to prepare, export or cancel.

## Rehearsal guests and explicit sheet music sharing

In the rehearsal overview, **Guest invitation** creates a personal link for exactly
one occurrence. Series occurrences can have separate links. Share links confidentially.
Guests can only accept or decline their own assigned occurrence. Links can be rotated
or revoked and expire within 180 days. Changing a guest email revokes rehearsal and
performance links.
Document managers with edit rights may explicitly share matching sheet music from the
current programme. Check usage rights first. A grant covers the selected file version;
later uploads are not shared automatically. Downloads stop when the guest declines,
the event is cancelled, the piece leaves the programme, the document is deleted or moved,
or the grantor loses permission. Performance invitations support the same sharing.
Department documents and documents from other organisations cannot be shared this way.

## Offers and confirmations

Open **Offers and confirmations** from a performance settlement. First complete the
customer address and gross amounts. Check expiry date and agreements before issuing
the offer PDF. Issued PDFs and checksums preserve their original content. A new offer
supersedes a pending offer. Invoice numbering is separate. Issuing does not send mail.
Record the customer's actual acceptance with evidence, then issue an order confirmation.
Repeated issuance returns the same confirmation. Firm confirmation locks agreed amounts
and performance details. Record cancellation with a reason before making changes and
issuing a new offer. Original PDFs remain as evidence after cancellation. Calendar changes
do not alter archived documents. These documents are not invoices. Finance readers can
inspect documents; issuance and status changes require finance and music edit rights.
PDFs use the existing letterhead.

## Personal return and maintenance reminders

In Tasks › **Personal music reminders**, enable private tasks for your own sheet music returns and equipment
returns and maintenance. Choose zero to 30 days ahead; overdue records are included.
Tasks are reconciled on save and hourly. Equipment still requires inventory read access;
department equipment is excluded. Enabling requires task read and edit permission.
You cannot select another recipient. Each task links directly to its source record.
Notifications use your existing task settings. Unchanged tasks are completed after a
recorded return or changed/completed maintenance. Your edits, completions and deletions
are preserved; only a new due date creates another task. Disabling completes unchanged
automatically created tasks. A review task does not itself record return or maintenance.
en.seiten/noten.md:
---
key: page.scores
titel: Sheet music
modul: scores
rechte: [scores.view]
routen: [/noten]
stichworte: [Noten, Notenarchiv, Notenbestand, Chor, Arrangement, Stimme]
---

# Sheet music

The sheet music archive manages pieces, arrangements, parts and digital scores. Without the Music module, for example in a choir without performance planning, it appears as its own **Sheet music** entry in the sidebar; with Music you find it under Music › Sheet music library.

Anyone with the right “Maintain sheet music library” may edit it. Roles with music rights can read the inventory so that programmes and rehearsals can pick arrangements.

**Import sheet music catalogue** takes over an existing catalogue from a CSV file. Upload digital scores in the document storage and link them to an arrangement under **Sheet music documents**.
