## Music folders for the app

Under **Music folders** you create fixed folders such as a **March book** or the **Repertoire**. Each folder holds arrangements in a fixed order, optionally with a number (“No. 27”). Use ↑ and ↓ to change the order.

Musicians find the folders in the “HUBIplan” app under **Sheet music** and can search by title, composer or number there. Everyone only sees the parts for their own voice, and only files that the document storage shares with members. Without a selection under **Visible to**, all musicians see the folder; otherwise only members of the chosen sub-units.

If a piece has several files for one voice (for example page 1 and 2 as images), **Order when there are several files** under **Sheet music documents** sets the order in which they are shown.

## Music files: PDF, images, MusicXML and MIDI

Upload sheet music in the document storage. Besides PDF, JPEG and PNG, HUBIplan understands MusicXML (`.musicxml`, `.mxl`, `.xml`) and the open formats MEI and ABC. MuseScore, Capella, Sibelius and Finale export MusicXML (usually under “Export” or “Save as”).

- From a MusicXML score, each musician only gets their own part. HUBIplan picks the part by the instrument and register of the link. If that is not unambiguous, enter the part’s name as it appears in the file under **Sheet music documents** in **Part in the MusicXML score (empty: by instrument)**.
- In the browser, MusicXML music opens as a PDF. In the app it is engraved to fit the screen and can be transposed.
- Link MIDI files (`.mid`) as listening examples. For MusicXML music, HUBIplan creates the listening example itself.

## Leading in the app

The conductor, bandleader or drum major can send the next piece to all musicians in the app; the devices then jump to each musician’s own part. Anyone allowed to edit music can do this, as well as anyone entered under **Leading in the app**: for a music folder (under **Show pieces**), for a performance under **Plan instrumentation**, or for a rehearsal.
en.seiten/plattform.md:
---
key: page.platform
titel: Platform
modul: platform
rechte: [platform.manage]
routen: [/plattform]
stichworte: [platform, create club, umbrella association, enable modules, self-update]
---

Platform administration creates clubs and umbrella associations on this HUBIplan instance and enables modules. When creating one, a person receives the “board” role with all rights and then manages roles and users themselves.

In the list of units, each unit shows the number of enabled modules (“12 modules”); click it to see them one by one.

Under settings you set the deletion period after leaving. A shorter period only applies 30 days after the change. Until then, data is still deleted after the longer one, so that a typo does not immediately delete the data of former members.

## Deactivating or deleting units

Under **Units** → **Edit**, clear “is active” and save to deactivate a unit. Its data is retained and the unit can be activated again later.

Deletion happens in two stages:

1. **Deactivate and schedule deletion**: in the edit form, enter the full name under “Delete unit”. The unit and all subunits below it are deactivated immediately; nobody can access them any more and the data is retained. While deletion is scheduled the unit cannot be activated again; **Withdraw scheduling** cancels it.
2. **Delete permanently**: at the earliest 30 days after scheduling and only once the statutory retention periods for books and vouchers of all financial years have expired (§ 147 AO: vouchers 8, books 10 years). The form shows until when the periods run. A deletion hold on a financial year prevents deletion. To confirm, enter the name; HUBIplan also asks for a current two-factor code. If the unit has financial data, state who confirmed the retention periods (e.g. auditor or tax advisor).

Permanent deletion removes the members, roles, financial records and stored files of the unit and its subunits. User accounts are retained. Clubs belonging to a federation must be deleted or moved first. If references from other units prevent deletion, an error is shown and the data is retained. The deletion is recorded in the platform audit log and on the deletion list: if an older backup is restored later, HUBIplan deletes the unit again.

## New versions

Once a day HUBIplan asks GitHub whether a newer release is available. If so, you see the notice “A newer version of HUBIplan is available” at the top, with a link to the changes. None of your data goes to GitHub; GitHub only sees the server's IP address, and the platform's privacy policy mentions this. Whoever runs the server can switch the check off with `HUBIPLAN_UPDATE_CHECK=0` in the `.env`. Once the new release is running, the changes are listed under [News](/hilfe/neuigkeiten).

## Updating from HUBIplan (self-update)

Platform › Version shows which version is running and whether a newer release is available. If the operator has turned on self-update (`HUBIPLAN_SELBSTUPDATE=1`, see `docs/betrieb.md`), you can install the new release there with “Update to …”. This needs two-factor sign-in, and you enter your password again.

If no virus scanning is set up on the server, or it is switched off for sharing, a notice appears there: circular attachments and public documents then go out unscanned. With virus scanning (ClamAV) set up, HUBIplan shares such files only after scanning them.

If the virus scanner is briefly unreachable, HUBIplan still accepts uploaded documents, attachments and receipts, but locks them until the scanner has checked them (quarantine). Platform › Version shows how many files are waiting and whether malware was found in any of them; such files stay locked for good.

HUBIplan only leaves an order. A service on the server first backs up the database, checks the release signature and that it is newer than the running version, and then installs it. HUBIplan is unavailable for a few minutes meanwhile; the page checks back on its own and then shows the result. If anything fails, the previous version keeps running. Every order is recorded in the change log, and the operator receives a security email.

## Addresses per unit

In the **Addresses per unit** section of the platform settings you assign further addresses to a unit, for example `mitglieder.sv-musterstadt.example` to Schützenverein Musterstadt. Anyone opening HUBIplan via that address sees the unit's name, colours, coat of arms and icon on the sign-in page; after signing in, the unit is preselected. Unknown addresses and the main address show the instance. Links in the unit's emails (invitation, sign-in link, events, volunteer shifts, tasks, membership card, photo link, circulars) lead to its address, otherwise to that of the next higher unit with its own address; “Forgot password” sends the link for the address on which it was requested. The unit uploads its own icon under Settings › Appearance; without one, HUBIplan uses its coat of arms. Sign-in applies per address. The address must point to the server via DNS. If the server has `HUBIPLAN_ADRESSEN_AUS_LISTE=1` set, it accepts listed addresses without further configuration and obtains the certificate on first access; otherwise the operator must allow them (`DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, certificate). Nextcloud, the app connection and federation stay on the main address.
en.seiten/rundschreiben.md:
---
key: page.circulars
titel: Circulars
modul: circulars
routen: [/rundschreiben]
stichworte: [mailing, letter, newsletter, distribution list, invitation]
---

Circulars go by email, letter or to the app to members, boards or holders of certain roles. You choose the type: everyone receives official notices such as invitations, while members can unsubscribe from “information”. Sent circulars remain available to read.

For organisations as members, the circular goes to every contact person marked “receives circulars”. Without such an address it goes to the organisation's email address or as a letter marked “attn.” of the primary contact. The placeholder {Organisation} inserts the organisation's name; the salutation addresses the contact person.

If members belong to a household at the same address, they get one joint letter, and emails to the same address become one email. The preview shows the others as “im gemeinsamen Schreiben an den Haushalt” (in the joint letter to the household). Under **Recipient** you switch this off with **Combine letters per household**. The placeholder {Haushalt} inserts the household name. You create households under [Members › Households and companies](/mitglieder/haushalte).

For a single letter, Circulars › Letter creates a Word template with the club letterhead and your sender details. The board designs the letterhead under Settings › Letterhead; you store your signature under My account.

A mailing list turns a mail sent to a club address into a circular. Anyone may write to an open mailing list. So that outsiders cannot reach many members unchecked, their mails go out directly only up to an adjustable number of recipients (50 by default) and up to a number per day. Anything beyond that is kept as a draft. Those allowed to write to the list are notified and release or delete the mail.

Name lists use a fixed alphabetical order: accented letters are placed with their base letter. Identical names keep their relative order when paging through the list.

You create a circular about an event in the event under **For this event**. It goes to those invited to the event, optionally only to those with a certain reply.

If the club belongs to an umbrella association, the **Received** tab shows its circulars to the boards. Without an umbrella association this tab does not exist.

Received circulars and their attachments are also available in the member area under **Circulars**. The Android app calls this shared inbox “Messages”. Changes to information emails are confirmed and keyboard focus is kept while saving. Further changes are blocked during the request; official notices are unaffected.
en.seiten/start.md:
---
key: page.start
titel: Home page
routen: [/]
stichworte:
  [tasks, quick actions, notices, anniversaries, birthdays, accept, customise, layout, drag]
---

The home page is your workplace in the selected unit. Without a layout of your own it has the same order for every role: **To do**, **Quick actions**, **Upcoming events**, **Anniversaries**, **Birthdays** and **Notices**. What you see depends on your rights; anything you may not do is simply left out. At the top right you switch units if you work in more than one.

The navigation on the left starts with **Home**, **Tasks** and **Events**. Club activities follow, then organisation and finally administration. Spacing separates the visible groups; **Help** stays separate at the bottom.

At the top, **Help on this page** opens help for the current page; on narrow screens only the “?” sign is shown. **Help** in the sidebar opens the overview of all guides. **My account** contains your email address, personal settings and **Sign out**.

Buttons have their own opaque background, including subtle actions, disabled buttons and file pickers. Selected views also use a distinct fill. Very light club colours are darkened for action buttons to keep them recognisable; the club logo and the remaining brand colour are preserved.

The **To do** tile comes first and collects tasks, approvals, requests, overdue invoices, open booking requests, held contact form messages, your own circular drafts untouched for a week, meeting invitations from two weeks before the invitation deadline, received motions and open minutes, open helper places in the next two weeks, queries and close entry deadlines, received invoices to review, invoice drafts, due reminders and direct debits, expired account invitations, bookings without a receipt in the current financial year, bank accounts whose statement for the previous month is still missing from the 5th, and missing required items of the [setup](/einstellungen/einrichtung); each entry only appears with the matching permission. Finance › Overview shows the same entries where they concern finance. The count is shown beside its heading. **New task** at the bottom of the tile opens the task dialog. **All tasks** beside it opens the overview. Each row separates its type, title and details; tasks that are due also show a due-date notice. Use the checkbox to complete a task if you have permission. Its title opens the details.

**Quick actions** are buttons for what you do most often; the first one is highlighted. Without a selection of your own, HUBIplan suggests at most four actions for your role: the treasurer gets **Record a booking**, **Import bank statement**, **Issue receipt** and **Prepare reminders**, the board **New event**, **Admit member** and **Write a circular**, the secretary **Create a meeting** and **Write minutes**. The treasurer's actions are only suggested if you hold a treasurer role (a role with finance rights that may not assign roles); if you have several roles, they come first. Under **Customise** you choose up to six actions yourself from everything your rights allow, grouped by area: finance (such as **Record income**, **Write invoice**, **Prepare fee run**), events and planning (**Create task**, **Create helper shift**, **Enter booking**), members, club (**Add to chronicle**, **Create competition**, **Enter results**, **Upload sheet music**) and writing and filing (**File a document**, **Edit website**, **Write a letter**). You set the order by grabbing an action anywhere and dragging it; with the keyboard, use the handle and the arrow keys. The selection applies to each unit and sub-unit separately; **Restore suggestion** goes back to the suggestion. In the workspace of a sub-unit you can choose **Event for the unit**, **View members**, **Letterhead** and, if allowed, **Create task**. **Hide quick actions completely** removes the whole block; you can turn it back on under My account › Profile › Home.

In **Upcoming events**, **New event** opens the event dialog when you have permission to create events, and **Calendar** opens the overview.

The **Anniversaries** card shows the anniversaries of the current year, from October also those of the next year, each under its own heading such as “Anniversaries 2026”. Anniversaries count for a calendar year; a date is only shown if the club counts to the day or month. **All anniversaries** leads to the full list. The **Birthdays** card shows the birthdays in the next 30 days. Names lead to the member record.

The **Notices** card collects what is not urgent: missing details in the legal notice and letter template notices (with **Later**). The number next to the heading is the number of these notices. Without a notice there is no card.

**Customise home page** at the top right lets you put the home page together the way you like. Each block then gets a dashed frame and a bar with **Show**, **Width** and **Height to fit content**. Grab a block anywhere and drag it to its new place; with the keyboard, use the handle and the arrow keys. Drag the corner at the bottom right to change width and height; with the keyboard, the left and right arrow keys there change the width and up and down the height. The home page uses a grid of twelve columns and fine rows: a block moves up into the next gap that is wide enough, including below a shorter block next to it. You choose the width as ¼, ⅓, ½, ⅔, ¾ or full, and at the corner also in twelfths. If a block has a fixed height, its content scrolls inside the card; **Height to fit content** makes it as tall as needed again. Hidden blocks stay faintly visible while customising so you can switch them back on. A block without content, such as birthdays when there are none in the next 30 days, does not appear on the home page. Every change is saved straight away; **Done** ends customising. The layout is yours alone and kept separately for each unit and sub-unit; **Restore default** returns to the order above, and under My account › Profile › Home page you can do this for all areas at once. On narrow screens all blocks are stacked; on a phone the page scrolls over the content, and you drag by the bar with the name.

![Board home page with To do, quick actions, anniversaries and notices](bild:startseite-vorstand)

As a member the next event is at the very top, on a phone too. If a response is possible, you accept or decline right there with **Accept** or **Decline**; the following events come below. Under **My area** at most four tiles are shown, **Show ID card** first; **Everything in My area** leads to the rest.

![Member home page with the next event at the top](bild:startseite-mitglied)

If two-factor sign-in is required for your permissions, every page shows the same short notice with **Set up now**; **Learn more** shows which permissions are affected. If the connection drops, the “No connection” band appears straight away. Automatically saved changes are sent as soon as the connection is back; after about ten seconds at the latest the form shows that nothing has been saved yet.
en.seiten/termine.md:
---
key: page.events
titel: Events
modul: events
routen: [/termine]
stichworte: [calendar, event, accept, decline, subscription]
---

The calendar shows the unit's events. With the right to do so, you create events, including recurring ones, and invite members who accept or decline. With the calendar subscription the events appear in your own calendar on phone or PC. Under Events › Setup you manage categories, external calendars, sharing with other units and the website link. Under “External calendars” the calendar imports other calendars’ events every hour, e.g. the federation’s from Vereinsplaner.

Each entry names its unit and, where applicable, its external calendar, so you can distinguish events with the same title before opening them. In the month view, a multi-day event starts with its start time; subsequent days show “Continued”, and the last day shows, for example, “Continued until 01:05”. An end exactly at midnight is shown on the preceding day as 24:00, without an extra entry on the new day. All-day events remain labelled as such. The list and accessible names include the complete date and time range; the list is the default view on small screens.

You can tell an event’s category not only by its colour: every event has a light background and a stripe on the left in its category colour, and the category name appears below the title. On small screens the month view shows a short code instead of the name (e.g. “Mee” for Meeting). The legend above the month explains the colours and codes of all categories in that month. Screen readers announce the category too.

![Calendar with units and continuation past midnight](bild:kalender-kontext)

In an open event, the block **For this event** shows what belongs to it: the meeting, volunteer duty rosters, booked rooms and equipment, tasks and the music performance. From there you also create a duty roster or a booking for the event. You only see areas whose module is switched on and for which you have the right. Events, meetings, volunteer duties and tasks are grouped together in the sidebar under “Planning”.

**Write a circular about it** creates a draft to those invited. It contains title, time, place, description and the reply deadline, and the event's PDF attachments go along as attachments. In the circular you can pick only those invited with **no reply yet**, **accepted** or **declined**, for example for a reminder. All circulars for the event are then listed in the block. **Reminder to everyone without a reply** creates such a draft right away to everyone who has not replied yet (and, if “Maybe” is allowed, to those as well). You see the replies in the event's participant list.

The event dialog first asks for title, time and place, then category and **Who sees the event?**. Rarely used options are folded under **More settings**: **Pass on upwards**, **Pass on downwards** and **Hide end time on the website**. If one of them is set, the section is open. The header and the save bar stay in place while you scroll in the dialog.

Under **Directions** you enter notes such as parking or the entrance. Without further details the links **Route in OpenStreetMap** and **Route in Google Maps** lead to the address. If the address is not enough (marquee, shooting range in the woods), enter **Latitude** and **Longitude** or paste a link from OpenStreetMap or Google Maps under **Take point from map link**. Directions and route links appear in the event, in the emails, on the reply page and in the calendar subscription; no map is embedded. If you pick a saved place, the event copies its address, directions and point.

When creating or editing an event, enable **Hide end time on the website** to show only the start time publicly. The internal calendar and calendar subscription keep the end time. For recurring events, the setting applies to all occurrences.

After successfully accepting, declining or withdrawing your response, a confirmation is provided as a status message for screen readers. Focus stays at the action when accepting or declining; after withdrawal it moves to **Accept**. An error produces no success confirmation; you can retry your response.

For replies to an event you can switch on **Allow “Maybe” as an answer**. “Maybe” does not count against the maximum number, but the reminder before the event also goes to these members. **Allow a comment** is on by default; with **Own question for the comment (optional)** (e.g. “Meal preference?”) it appears above the field instead of “Comment”. The participant list and the export show “Maybe” and the comments.

Every email about the event (invitation, reminder, circular about the event) contains a personal link “Accept or decline (without login)” for each member. It opens a page with time, place, description and attachments; there the member chooses “I am coming”, “Maybe” or “I am not coming” and saves. Just opening the link saves nothing. The same link lets them change the answer until the deadline, as do the member area and the app. The invitation carries the event's attachments directly as email attachments (up to 5 files, 10 MB each); larger ones are on the page behind the link.

Create a personal calendar-subscription link for your own calendar app. Keep it private. Creating a new link invalidates the previous link. A status confirms when your link is ready.

![Create a personal calendar subscription](bild:kalender-abo)
en.seiten/untereinheiten.md:
---
key: page.units
titel: Sub-units
routen: [/untereinheiten]
stichworte: [platoon, department, sub-unit, manager]
---

This lists the sub-units of your unit, which can be nested freely. Each sub-unit can have its own roles, its own cash book, events and a website. With “Assign head” a person from the sub-unit gets an account with all permissions for their area.

For each sub-unit you upload a coat of arms or logo and, if you like, a second one for dark mode. Without a dark one, the normal one is used in the dark.

Unit settings and roles have separate rights. Settings “read” shows administrative data; role “read” shows roles. Without settings read access, a limited sub-unit selection remains available for this purpose. Changing and assigning roles requires role “edit”; “Assign head” additionally requires settings edit access.

“Who has which role?” lists the current holders per role. With **Assign** you give a role to a member, without an account and without email; the predecessor’s term can end in the same step. Earlier terms are under Members › Offices with the Unit filter.

With its own workspace you choose under “Modules for this unit” which of the club’s modules the sub-unit also uses there, such as tax & charitable status for its own cash book or social media for its own website. By default: all.
en.seiten/versammlungen.md:
---
key: page.meetings
titel: Meetings
modul: meetings
rechte: [meetings.view, meetings.edit]
routen: [/versammlungen]
stichworte: [AGM, General meeting, Board meeting, Agenda, Item, Notice period, Minutes]
---

Under **Meetings** you prepare general meetings, board meetings and meetings of a unit. The
overview shows upcoming and past meetings with their status.

New meeting: Choose **New meeting**, then the type, start, end and place. HUBIplan creates an
event in the calendar for it. All members see general meetings in the calendar; only the board
sees board meetings. If **Copy the agenda of the last meeting of this type** is ticked, HUBIplan
copies its items; for the first meeting of a type it suggests a typical agenda.
**Event in the calendar** in the meeting leads to its event; there the block “For this event”
shows duty rosters and bookings for the meeting.

Agenda: Each agenda item has a title, a type (report, resolution, election or other) and an
explanation. Use the arrows to change the order; the numbers follow from it. **Save agenda**
saves all changes at once.

Notice period: Below the heading you see the date by which the invitation has to go out. Once
that day has passed, HUBIplan points it out. Set the notice period for each type under **Types and notice periods**, in line with your statutes.

Cancelling and deleting: **Cancel** keeps the event in the calendar and shows it as cancelled.
You can only delete a meeting before invitations have gone out. The event of a meeting cannot
be deleted in the calendar, only here.

Types and notice periods: HUBIplan starts with the usual types, such as the annual general
meeting and the board meeting. You can rename them, add more or switch them off. For each type
you set the notice period, how invitations are sent, the quorum and who will see the minutes.

Invitation: **Prepare invitation** creates a draft circular with the agenda. For general meetings it goes to the members entitled to vote under the type (member types and minimum age), for board meetings to the board, and for leadership meetings of a unit to its role holders. Use **Open circular** to check the recipients and text and to send the invitation. After that the meeting counts as invited; if it went out after the last day of the notice period, HUBIplan points this out. You also need the right to send circulars. If the agenda changes after the draft has been created, adjust the text in the circular. Until the invitation has gone out, the **Before the invitation** checklist shows whether the notice period can still be met, whether the agenda has items and whether every resolution and election item has an explanation. It never blocks anything.

Attendance: If you also have read access to members, **Attendance** lists everyone entitled to vote at the meeting. For each person choose **Present**, **Excused** or, if the type allows proxies, **Represented** and then who holds the proxy. Only a present member with voting rights can act as proxy. Enter guests under **Guest without a vote**. The figures at the top show whether the meeting has a quorum under the rule of its type.

Organisations as members have one vote and attend **By representative**: choose a contact person marked “represents at meetings” or enter a name. This is not a proxy and also works if the type does not allow proxies. The minimum age of the type does not apply to organisations. If the representative is a member themselves, they keep their own vote; the list then shows “also represents”. The minutes name the organisation and its representative.

Minutes: After the meeting choose **Mark as held**. The agenda is then fixed and the minutes appear in its place. For each agenda item write down what was discussed. Use **Add resolution** to record a resolution with its text and result, and **Add election** to record an election with the office and the person elected. Enter the vote as yes, no and abstentions or tick **unanimous**. **Save minutes** stores all changes.

Approval: Under **Approval of the minutes** the chair and the minute taker confirm the minutes with **Confirm as chair** and **Confirm as minute taker**. Both must first be entered in the meeting details. **Preview as PDF** shows the minutes as a draft beforehand. Any change to the minutes or the attendance cancels the confirmations. With the second confirmation the minutes are approved: the resolutions receive a consecutive number per year (such as 2027/03), and the PDF is stored with a checksum and can no longer be changed. If document storage is switched on, HUBIplan files the PDF in the folder “Minutes”, which only the board sees at first. **Minutes as PDF** downloads the approved minutes.

Resolution book: The **Resolution book** tab lists all resolutions and elections from approved minutes with number, date and result. Search by text, office or number and filter by year, type of meeting, resolution or election and implementation status. With editing rights you set the status to open, implemented or repealed. If the tasks module is switched on and you may create tasks, **Create as task** turns an open resolution into a task for you so its implementation is not forgotten. **List as Excel** downloads the filtered list.

Taking elections into office: For an accepted election whose elected person was picked from the member list, **Take into office** opens the **Assign role** dialog in the club. The role named like the office is preselected, the term starts on the day of the meeting, and if you wish the predecessor's term ends the day before. The election then counts as implemented. You need the right to manage roles. Offices of units are still filled under Members › Offices.

Member area: Members entitled to vote see meetings they are invited to there, with the agenda. They see approved minutes only if the meeting type makes them available to everyone entitled to vote; board minutes stay with the roles that have read access.

Motions: For each type, **Types and notice periods** sets until how many days before the meeting members can submit motions; an empty field switches motions off. Invited members entitled to vote submit their motions in the member area. They appear in the meeting under **Motions**. **Add to agenda** turns a motion into a new agenda item; **Decline** gives the member a reason. This works while the meeting is in preparation or invited. If the invitation has already been sent, inform the members about the changed agenda.
en.seiten/webseite-aufbau.md:
---
key: page.website_structure
titel: Website › Menu and sections
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/aufbau]
stichworte:
  [
    menu,
    section,
    order,
    chronicle,
    member list,
    memorial,
    heading,
    search,
    instrument,
    link,
    button,
    home page,
  ]
---

Here you decide which sections the website has, such as events, sub-units, chronicle or contact, what they are called in the menu and in which order they appear.

Unpublished changes: When there is a draft, the bar “Unpublished changes” with **Publish** and **Discard** is shown at the very top. It stays visible below the top bar while you scroll.

Members: The heading “Members” has one list per member type, for example “Active” and “Passive”. You switch each list on separately and give it a name with the pencil. The lists show today’s members by surname, with the year they joined and, if you like, their main instrument (settings under “People”). Only members who consented appear: in the member record on the “Photo & website” tab under “Publication on the website”, item “Member list”. Anyone who objected to publishing their name is still left out. “In memoriam” shows members whose reason for leaving is “death”, with the year of death, but only if the board has approved each of them in their member record under “In memoriam”; a text page with the address `in-gedenken` appears above it as an introduction.

Custom headings: “Add heading” creates a menu item without its own page, for example “Band”. Drag sections onto it and they become its sub-items. Without sub-items the heading does not appear. If you leave the name empty, it is removed when saved.

External links: “Add external link” creates a menu item that leads to another website, for example your federation. Use the pencil to enter the name and the address (with https://). The link opens in a new window and can be moved or made a sub-item like any other item. If you leave the name empty, it is removed when saved.

Button: Under “Highlight a menu item as a button” you choose one main item that appears in the menu as a coloured button, such as “Contact” or a link “Become a member”. There is at most one button; headings and items with sub-items are not possible.

Menu items in the footer: if the menu bar gets too full, “Menu items in the footer” lets you set for each main item whether it appears “in the menu”, “footer only” or “menu and footer”. In the footer it appears next to the legal notice and privacy policy, for example “Contact”. The page stays reachable and its block stays switched on. Headings and items with sub-items are not possible. “Home” and the search are set under Website › Design › Fine-tuning › Header and menu.

Draft: order, names, links, button and footer place of the menu go into the draft, like design and home page. The preview under Website › Design shows the new menu; it becomes public with **Publish**. The check boxes that switch a section on or off, however, apply immediately.

Home page: You put together the home page sections under Website › Design, with the preview next to them.

Repertoire and press: “Repertoire” shows the pieces from the sheet music library that are ticked “In the repertoire on the website”. “Press” shows the press clippings from Website › Documents.

Bookings: “Bookings” shows facilities and material whose booking calendar is not set to “do not show” under “On the website”, as a week view with a calendar subscription. Depending on the setting it shows only “Booked” or, for public bookings, also the purpose; names never appear.

Search: With the “Search” section a magnifying glass appears in the menu. It searches text pages, albums, documents and events, not people.

People: “Show titles before names” puts the title from the member record before the name (e.g. “Dr. Max Muster”) for the board, lists and results; when off, names appear without a title. “Show main instrument below the name” takes the main instrument from Music › Musicians. “Show postal address for the board” only applies to people with the consent “Postal address” in their member record.

Events: If there are sub-units, a check box adds their public events to the website calendar; if there are parent units with events (e.g. the umbrella association), a second one adds their events that are shared downwards. If there are neither, the “Events” block is not shown.
en.seiten/webseite-beitraege.md:
---
key: page.website_social
titel: Website › Social media
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/beitraege]
stichworte: [Instagram, Facebook, post, social media]
---

Here you connect Instagram or Facebook and show selected posts on the website. HUBIplan stores the posts so the website works without third-party services.

Drafts for posts: if an AI assistant has prepared a post, it appears here with text and images. **Copy text** puts the text on the clipboard; clicking an image opens it for saving. You post in your own Instagram or Facebook account, then **Mark as done**. HUBIplan never publishes drafts itself.

At the top you manage the club’s social media channels, i.e. the profile links shown in the website header and in letter templates. They used to be under Settings › Organisation.

**Fetch now** schedules a background fetch. Repeated requests are coalesced; manual and periodic fetches of the same channel never run concurrently. Reload later to see the results. The web process does not wait for Meta or image downloads.
en.seiten/webseite-bilder.md:
---
key: page.website_images
titel: Website › Images
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/bilder]
stichworte: [image, photo, gallery, consent, author, clipboard]
---

You upload and crop images for the website here. Instead of a file you can also use a copied image, such as a screenshot or an image from the browser: just press Ctrl+V, here or in the image picker. JPEG (including iPhone photos), PNG and WebP up to 15 MB are allowed; save HEIC images from an iPhone as JPEG first. Mind the rights: for photos you need the photographer's permission and, for recognisable people, their consent. Each image needs a short alternative text.
en.seiten/webseite-dokumente.md:
---
key: page.website_documents
titel: Website › Documents
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/dokumente]
stichworte: [documents, press, press clippings, newspaper article, PDF]
---

Here you upload files for the website, as PDF or image (JPEG, PNG, WebP). Each file belongs to a section:

- Press: press clippings, for example newspaper articles with source and date. They appear in the “Press” section, newest first.
- Documents: further files. They appear in the “Documents” section next to the statutes, fee regulations and founding deed.

You switch both sections on under “Menu and sections”. Images are rewritten when uploaded, which removes camera and location data. PDFs stay unchanged and get a preview image of the first page. With “Show on the website” you take a file off the website temporarily without deleting it.

Newspaper articles are protected by copyright. Only show them if the newspaper has agreed.
en.seiten/webseite-domain.md:
---
key: page.website_domain
titel: Website › Web address
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/domain]
stichworte: [domain, address, DNS]
---

This shows the web address where the website can be reached and how to set up your own domain.

Images for AI assistants: under “Allowed servers” you enter host names from which a connected AI assistant may fetch images by address, such as `cloud.example.org` for the club’s Nextcloud. HUBIplan downloads the image itself, only via https and only JPG, PNG or WebP, and checks it like any upload. If the field stays empty, images only arrive via an upload link that the assistant offers in the chat.
en.seiten/webseite-galerie.md:
---
key: page.website_gallery
titel: Website › Gallery
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/galerie]
stichworte: [gallery, photo album, album, sub-album, photos, cover image, sorting]
---

In the gallery you create photo albums for the website. An album can have sub-albums, for example “2024” with “Schützenfest” and “Königsball”; it does not go any deeper.

Create an album: enter a title and choose “New album”. The address on the website (e.g. /galerie/schuetzenfest-2024/) is made from the title and can be changed. With a date the website shows the year and can sort the albums by it. For a sub-album, choose the parent album under “Belongs to album”.

Photos: “Upload photos” takes many photos at once; you can also drag them onto the page. The photos are also added to the image library. Cropping is off while uploading to keep it quick; you can crop single photos later with “Edit image”. “Choose from the image library” adds existing images to the album. “Remove from album” does not delete the image.

Sorting: by default the gallery sorts images by date taken and albums by date (newest first). Choose “custom order” to sort by dragging. The cover is the chosen image, otherwise the first one.

Visibility: an album appears on the website only with “Show on the website”; a sub-album only if its parent album is shown as well. The “Gallery” section must also be switched on under “Menu and sections”. Only show photos of recognisable people with their consent.
en.seiten/webseite-gestaltung.md:
---
key: page.website_design
titel: Website › Design
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/gestaltung]
stichworte:
  [
    draft,
    home page,
    sections,
    tiles,
    quote,
    contact persons,
    frequently asked questions,
    partners,
    sponsors,
    directions,
    video,
    divider,
    countdown,
    preview,
    publish,
    versions,
    design,
    colours,
    logo,
    header image,
    banner,
    font,
    fine-tuning,
    style settings,
    corners,
    width,
    menu,
    footer,
    design package,
    export,
    import,
  ]
---

Under Design you choose the look, colours and logo of the website. The colours usually come from the unit's appearance and can be adjusted here.

When assigning colours you choose a palette colour, white or dark for each place of the design (header, menu, decorative lines, footer, colour bands, date box). The header, footer, colour bands and decorative lines can also get a gradient from the appearance settings instead of a colour; the menu, buttons and date box stay single-coloured, and rounded edges show the first colour of the gradient. Below, under **Text, surfaces and background**, you set the colour of body text, secondary text, surfaces (cards, table rows) and the page background. “Default” takes the colour ticked under **Used for** in Settings › Appearance, otherwise the design stays as it is; table rows then alternate with the surface colour; a chosen page background takes precedence over the “Background” control of the fine-tuning. If text on surfaces or background becomes hard to read (below 4.5 : 1), a notice appears.

Changes to design, colours, **Fine-tuning**, header image and home page are a draft first: visitors keep seeing the previous version. At the top you then see “Unpublished changes”. **Publish** makes the draft public, **Discard** undoes all changes. On a wide screen, a preview on the right shows the real website with the draft; it reloads after every change. At the top you choose **Phone**, **Tablet** or **Desktop**, **Reload** reconnects the preview, **In a new window** opens it full size. On narrow screens the **Preview** button opens the website in a new window. Anyone you gave a preview link can see the draft as well.

Under **Home** you build the home page from sections and see every change straight away in the preview. The existing sections (such as welcome text, upcoming events, majesties) exist once each; you switch them on and off. **Add section** adds your own sections, which you can use as often as you like: **Text**, **Text with image**, **Banner**, **Button bar**, **Tiles**, **Featured event** (with “N days to go”, disappears after the event), **Album preview**, **Quote**, **Contact persons** (only roles shown on the website, and people who have given their consent, as on the board page), **Frequently asked questions** (questions with answers to expand), **Partners and sponsors** (logos with a link; **Take over from business partners** fetches name and link of the business partners who have consented), **Directions** (address of a saved place with “Plan route”), **Events of one category** (the next public events of one category), **Document to download** (a published file from Website › Documents as a button), **Video as a link** (preview image linking to the video at the provider; the website embeds nothing), **Excerpt from the chronicle** (the latest timeline entries with a link to the chronicle), **Facts at a glance** (two to six numbers with a short text) and **Divider** (line or space). Events and chronicle only appear when their area is switched on. Drag the sections by the handle into the order you want. **Edit** opens a section's content and appearance, **Apply** saves it to the draft, **Delete** removes one of your own sections. For each section you choose the **Background** (**None**, **Light**, a palette colour or a gradient, each with a matching text colour) and the **Section width** (**Text width**, **Content width** or **Full width**). In the “Newspaper” design, **Column** sets whether a section is in the **Main column** or the **Side column**. Buttons and tiles lead to a page of the website, the contact form, an event or, as an **External link**, to a new window. People who may only “Edit content” change the content of the existing sections under Website › Home.

Under **Area display** you choose how the fixed areas look: the board as cards with photo or a compact list, events as a list by month or a monthly calendar (on a phone only the days with events appear), sub-units as large or small tiles or a list, and the gallery as tiles or masonry with pictures at their own height. A sketch shows each option. Like everything here, your choice goes into the draft first. You write an introduction at the top of an area under Website › Texts.

Under **Earlier versions** you find the last five published designs. **Restore** turns one of them into a draft; it only goes live with **Publish**.

Under **Fine-tuning** you adjust the chosen design without any programming. The settings are in six collapsible groups: font, page, cards/images/buttons, header and menu, home page and footer. Each setting has two to four fixed levels, for example corners “square”, “slight” or “round”; yes/no questions are switches. If no field is chosen, the website shows what the design provides. A second click on the chosen field resets the setting, **Reset** resets all of them. Whatever a design sets itself (such as the position of the coat of arms in the sidebar design) is greyed out. The coat of arms and the club name cannot both be hidden. The fonts are stored on the website itself (free licences); nothing is loaded from other servers.

Under **Page**, **Dark mode** › “follow device” shows the website in dark colours when the visitor's phone or computer is set to dark; header, menu and footer keep their club colours, design packages with their own CSS stay light. **Increased contrast** makes text darker and lines stronger, and the **“Back to top” button on long pages** appears at the bottom right once someone has scrolled far down. **Font** › **Size** also offers “very large”. **Image format in tiles** sets home page tiles, gallery albums and posts to 3:2, 4:3 or square. **Menu on phones** shows the menu on small screens “collapsible” behind the “Menu” button or as a **swipeable bar** below the header. Under **Home**, **Cover image** has the “medium” level like the header height, and **Image carousel advances** sets whether carousels change “only by hand”, “slowly” (each image twice as long) or “normal”.

With **Header and menu** › **Background** › **Header image** you choose an image from the image library that appears at the top of the website instead of the coat of arms and club name, for example a banner with lettering. It should contain the club name and be wide, about 1200 × 300 pixels. Without a header image, or with the background “white” or “coloured”, the coat of arms and name stay. **Header height** sets how tall the header image can get: “low”, “medium”, “normal” or “high”. “Medium” suits, for example, a wide logo with a subtitle that becomes too small at “low”. On a phone a wide header image quickly becomes too small to read next to the menu button. Below the header image you can therefore choose an optional **Header image for phones**: a more compact version, for example with the lettering on two lines. The website shows it on narrow screens below 600 pixels wide and the header image everywhere else. Without a header image for phones the header image is used everywhere.

Also under **Header and menu**, **“Home” in the menu** hides the first menu item on larger screens; the coat of arms, club name or header image then lead to the home page, and the mobile menu keeps “Home”. **Search** sets where the magnifying glass appears: “in the menu” at the end of the menu bar, “top right” in the header next to social media, or “in the footer” as a small search field. To hide the search completely, switch off the “Search” block under Website › Menu and sections › Building blocks. This keeps room in a full menu bar, for example when one item is highlighted as a button.

In the browser tab and on the phone home screen the website shows the unit's own icon, otherwise its coat of arms (square, with a transparent border). You set both under Settings › Appearance. Without an icon or coat of arms the website shows no icon of its own. Browsers often keep an old icon for a while; reloading the page helps.

Under **Design as a file**, **Save design** saves the design, colour assignment, **Fine-tuning** and **Area display** as a small file. For another unit or on another server, **Load design** loads it into the draft again; it is checked like a change made by hand. If the design does not exist there, the other values still apply. Coat of arms, texts, images and the home page are not included; the colours follow the palette of the unit that loads the file. Unlike a design package the file contains no CSS, so anyone who manages the website may load it.

Under **Share design** you save a design as a ZIP file with **Save as package**. The package contains the styling, the layout of header, footer and home page and the colour defaults, but no coat of arms, texts or images.

Platform administrators can import a package under **Load design from package**. With a new **Short name** and **Name** it becomes an own design, for example a styling variant for your club only. **Check** lets HUBIplan check the package: no JavaScript, no content from other addresses, no imported HTML/Django templates. **Import** releases the design for this website; under **Imported designs** the release can be switched on and off for each website.

Design packages use maintained built-in layouts with custom CSS and colours. Imported HTML/Django templates are rejected. Legacy packages with such templates are quarantined and display Classic until replaced by a package without templates. Layout markup follows maintained components rather than freezing historic HTML.
en.seiten/webseite-inhalte.md:
---
key: page.website_texts
titel: Website › Texts
modul: website
rechte: [website.manage, website.content]
routen: [/webseite/inhalte]
stichworte: [text, page, home page, blocks, sections, banner, tiles, chronicle, timeline, chapter]
---

Here you write the website texts and put together the blocks of the home page. Changes are saved as you type; the latest versions of each text are kept.

Text pages from sections: Under **Page sections** you build a text page from sections, like the home page. The existing text with the image at the top is the fixed section “Page text”; without further sections the page stays as before. **Add section** adds, for example, a **Banner**, a **Button bar**, **Tiles**, a **Quote**, **Frequently asked questions**, **Directions** or a **Document to download** above or below it; drag them by the handle into order. **Edit** opens content, background and width, **Apply** saves the section to the draft. Everything becomes visible with **Publish**; earlier versions bring back their sections too. A **Cover image** is a narrow image at the very top above the heading; each page has at most one, and it always appears at the top, wherever it is in the list.

Area introductions: **Introduction for an area** lets you write a short text, with an image if you like, that appears at the top of the board, events, sub-units or gallery, as on the memorial page. Each area has one introduction; it appears once you choose **Publish**.

Image captions: For each text, **Show image captions on the website** decides whether the website shows the caption below the image at the top and in the image carousel. Without the tick (the default) the images appear without a caption; the description for screen readers stays.

Chronicle as a timeline: The “Chronik” text has a short introduction at the top and the timeline below it (box **Timeline**). Each event has a year or a period (e.g. 1939 to 1948), a heading, at most 400 characters of text and, if you like, up to six pictures, such as posters from several years. On the website they appear small side by side; in the large view you can page through them. Under “Picture position” you choose for each event whether the pictures appear on the left, on the right or large below the text; automatic alternates the side from entry to entry. On a phone they always appear below the text. Chapters (marked **Chapter**) such as “Founding years 1920–1938” are subheadings: below them the website shows all events from their year until the next chapter begins. **Add from Excel** brings a list with the columns Jahr (year), Überschrift (heading) and optionally bis (until), Text and Art (type, “Kapitel” for a chapter) into the draft. With **Newest entries at the top** the website shows the timeline backwards, from the present to the founding; chapters still stay above their events and the jump links follow. Without the tick the order stays from old to new. The timeline is published together with the chronicle. The timeline belongs to the “Chronicle” module. When it is switched on, you maintain the introduction and timeline only under its own menu item **Chronicle**, even without rights on the website; here the chronicle then only shows the address, “show in menu” and delete.

**Edit** opens a section, **Apply** saves the change to the draft. Visitors keep seeing the previous version until you choose **Publish**. On a wide screen the **Preview** on the right shows the website with the draft.

If the draft also changes the design, for example a different design, only the website managers can publish it. Your content changes stay in the draft and go online with it.

key: page.website

modul: website

The overview shows the status of your club website and what is still missing before publishing, such as the legal notice or privacy notice. The website only reads what you release here; names and photos only appear with consent.

Under **Notice bar** a short notice appears at the top of every page, for example “Fair 22–25 Aug: programme”. With **Target** it leads to a page of the website, to an event or to an outside address. **Show from** and **Show until** set the period (both days included); afterwards the bar disappears by itself. Without dates it applies right away and without end; without **Notice bar text** there is none. The notice bar goes online immediately, not with the design draft.

---

en.seiten/wettbewerbe-titel.md:
---
key: page.competitions_titles

modul: competitions

---

Titles and dignities such as “king” or “club champion” are set up here and awarded from a competition. The holders then appear in the chronicle. Kings and other honours of past years are added under Members › Title holders, where all honours are kept in one place.
en.seiten/wettbewerbe-urkunden.md:
---
key: page.competitions_certificates
titel: Competitions › Certificate templates
modul: competitions

en.seiten/wettbewerbe.md:
---
key: page.competitions
titel: Competitions
modul: competitions
rechte: [competitions.manage, competitions.results]
routen: [/wettbewerbe, /wettbewerbe/statistik]
stichworte: [shooting, bird shooting, ranking, shoot-off, result]
---

## Statistics

Open **Competitions** › **Statistics** for participation, achievements and performance across
all members. Select a member for their personal statistics. The same view is available in
the member file under **Competitions**. Your own entries and results are under My area › Competitions.

Filter by year, competition type and scoring conditions. Average rings, rings per counted
shot and best results refer to the same recorded conditions. Different conditions have
separate averages; select a row to see the corresponding progress. Averages include the
number of valid results. The overall view also shows the equally weighted average of
personal member averages.

Only final results count. Missing values are not zero. Each person counts once per
competition. Guests, non-competing entries and absent starters do not count as
participations; **Participations** shows how many were not counted. This is why the number
of starters in the competition list can be higher. Wins and podium finishes count per individual standing. Team achievements
are not counted as personal wins. Chart values are also available as a table. Expand
**All starts and awards** to see ongoing competitions as well.

Here you set up your own shooting competitions with individual and team scoring, record results and decide ties in a shoot-off. Bird shooting with prizes and external competitions where you only enter your places also belong here. Provisional results only become fixed when marked final.

Stand mode stores private data for the verified account or complete stand credential, for at most twelve hours and never beyond the credential's expiry. Without reception, the same stand remains available in the same browser tab. An explicit server access denial ends offline access. Signing out or switching accounts removes this browser's stand cache. Send outstanding entries before signing out; signing out asks before discarding them. Revoked or expired access also removes unsent entries. The old cache without account binding is removed on first opening this version; a notice appears if it contained unsent entries. Browser storage does not replace a backup.

In the live camera, the dashed circle shows where the outermost ring of the target should be; if the target has a black aiming area, a solid circle also shows where the black should be. On the card with five target faces (four corners and centre), the camera looks for all five and draws the circles around the ones it finds; it takes the picture once all five are straight, steady and fully in view. It does not need fixed card dimensions for this. This works the same in the browser and in the app.

### Setup

**Set up** separates **Basic data**, **Shooting conditions**, **Rankings** and **Output & sharing**. A target is selected by its image once per shooting round. Individual and centre-distance rankings can share the same recorded hits; unit rankings derive from an individual ranking. Facilities configured under [Competitions › Setup](/wettbewerbe/einrichtung) filter the target catalogue without removing existing selections. Targets with hit pattern, photo evaluation and bird shooting belong to the “Shooting sports” module; without it you enter results as values.

Under **Basic data** › **Event in the calendar** you link the competition to an event. The competition then takes the event's date, and empty place and description fields as well. If the event is moved later, the competition moves with it; competitions that are already final keep their date. If the dates still differ, a notice offers **Use the event's date**.

Changes to conditions or calculations require confirmation when results exist. Calculated results are recalculated, while manual totals remain and must be reviewed. After conditions change, stand mode requires the current setup and discards old offline entries. Finalising and reopening are available under **Evaluation** → **Competition and finalisation**.

### Names on the website

Under **Set up** → **Output & sharing** → **Publicly visible**, **prize places with names** publishes
individual places up to the number of **prize places** configured for each scoring.
Two prize places show places 1 and 2; five prize places show places 1 to 5.
This also applies to the results block on the home page and to external competitions.
The results page shows the latest published competition directly;
older competitions can be opened through links.
Zero prize places show no individual places. Tied prize places are shown in full;
existing consent and objections still apply. Unit and team rankings also show only their prize places, likewise
with **only the scoring of subunits and teams**. All places appear only with **full ranking**.

### Personal results for connected clubs

Under **Evaluation** → **Result approval for connected clubs**, administrators with both
competition and peering management rights may explicitly assign otherwise unassigned
guest starters to an active downstream connection. Changes are audited and also
possible after completion; scores and places stay unchanged. An empty selection
revokes the local assignment. A starter already assigned to a unit uses that stable
assignment. Club names alone never authorize personal result sharing. The connection
must also allow the own-starters packet. Changes propagate on the next peering sync;
already received copies cannot reliably be recalled remotely.

Name lists use a fixed alphabetical order: accented letters are placed with their base letter. Identical names keep their relative order when paging through the list.

On wide screens the live tables of the scorings (for example individual and unit ranking) appear side by side, on narrow screens one below the other. Live tables show an error and **Reload** even when the first request fails. Previously loaded rankings remain visible with a notice identifying the earlier state until updating succeeds.

de.name: aktiv / passiv
de.text: Kennzeichen einer Mitgliedsart: aktive Mitglieder nehmen voll am Vereinsleben teil, passive unterstützen vor allem mit ihrem Beitrag. Was das für Rechte und Beitrag bedeutet, regelt die Satzung (§ 25 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: 112 aktive und 38 passive Mitglieder: Der Dachverband berechnet seinen Beitrag für beide Gruppen getrennt.

de.name: Anzahlungsrechnung
de.text: Rechnung über einen Teil des Entgelts vor der Leistung; die Umsatzsteuer entsteht schon mit der Zahlung (§ 13 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 Buchstabe a Satz 4 UStG). Die Schlussrechnung zieht die Anzahlungen mit ihrer Steuer ab (§ 14 Abs. 5 UStG).
de.example: Beispiel: Für das Zeltfest zahlt die Brauerei 1.190 € an; die Schlussrechnung über 4.760 € zieht sie ab, offen bleiben 3.570 €.

de.name: Altersstufen oder eigene Mitgliedsart?
de.text: Altersstufen setzen den Beitrag automatisch nach dem Alter zu Beginn des Geschäftsjahrs, ohne dass du die Mitgliedsart wechseln musst. Eine eigene Mitgliedsart wie „Jugend“ ist besser, wenn sich mit dem Alter auch Rechte oder die Meldung ändern. Unterschiedliche Beiträge brauchen eine Grundlage in Satzung oder Beitragsordnung (§ 58 Nr. 2 BGB).

de.name: Welche Ausgaben als Künstlerhonorar kennzeichnen?
de.text: Abgabepflichtig sind Honorare an selbständige Künstler und Publizisten, etwa Kapelle, DJ, Fotograf oder Grafiker, auch wenn sie selbst nicht in der Künstlersozialkasse sind (§ 25 KSVG). Nicht dazu gehören Zahlungen an eine GmbH, gesondert ausgewiesene Umsatzsteuer und steuerfreie Reisekosten (§ 25 Abs. 2 KSVG). Ob der Verein überhaupt abgabepflichtig ist, hängt davon ab, wie oft er Künstler beauftragt (§ 24 KSVG).

de.name: Künstlersozialabgabe
de.text: Abgabe an die Künstlersozialkasse auf Honorare an selbständige Künstler und Publizisten (§§ 24, 25 KSVG). Die Summe eines Jahres meldet der Verein bis 31. März des Folgejahres (§ 27 KSVG).
de.example: Beispiel: 2.400 € für die Kapelle beim Schützenfest; bei einem Abgabesatz von 5 % wären das 120,00 €.

de.name: Vermögensverwaltung
de.text: Einnahmen aus dem Vermögen des Vereins, etwa Zinsen oder langfristige Vermietung, ohne eigenen Geschäftsbetrieb. Bei gemeinnützigen Vereinen bleibt sie steuerfrei (§ 14 Satz 3 AO, § 5 Abs. 1 Nr. 9 KStG).
de.example: Beispiel: 1.200,00 € Pacht im Jahr für die verpachtete Vereinsgaststätte.

de.name: Sofort abschreiben, Sammelposten oder über die Nutzungsdauer?
de.text: Bis 800 € netto darf ein Gegenstand im Jahr der Anschaffung voll abgeschrieben werden (§ 6 Abs. 2 EStG), von 250 bis 1.000 € wahlweise als Sammelposten über 5 Jahre (§ 6 Abs. 2a EStG). Teurere Anlagen verteilen sich linear über die Nutzungsdauer laut AfA-Tabelle (§ 7 Abs. 1 EStG). Steuerlich zählt das nur im wirtschaftlichen Geschäftsbetrieb, und die Wahl für den Sammelposten gilt dann für alle Anschaffungen des Jahres.

de.name: Welche Empfehlung zur Entlastung?
de.text: „Entlastung empfohlen“ passt, wenn die Prüfung nichts Wesentliches ergab, „mit Anmerkungen“ bei Mängeln, die das Ergebnis nicht in Frage stellen. „Nicht empfohlen“ ist richtig bei ungeklärten Differenzen oder fehlenden Belegen; die Versammlung entscheidet trotzdem selbst. Die Prüfer berichten nur, Grundlage ist die Rechenschaftspflicht des Vorstands (§ 27 Abs. 3, § 666 BGB).

de.name: Warum der Kontenabgleich?
de.text: Nur wenn der Bestand laut Kassenbuch mit Kontoauszug und gezählter Barkasse übereinstimmt, ist die Buchführung vollständig und richtig (GoBD). Eine Differenz heißt: Es fehlt eine Buchung oder ein Betrag ist falsch erfasst. Klärt jede Differenz und schreibt die Ursache in die Anmerkung.

de.name: Warum Stichproben und welche?
de.text: Kassenprüfer müssen nicht jeden Beleg sehen, aber nachvollziehen können, dass jede Buchung belegt und richtig ist (GoBD, Nachprüfbarkeit). Die größten Ausgaben tragen das größte Risiko; zufällig gezogene Buchungen verhindern, dass nur ausgesuchte Belege geprüft werden. Bei Auffälligkeiten zieht weitere Stichproben, bis das Bild klar ist.

de.name: Kassenprüfer
de.text: Von der Mitgliederversammlung gewählte Mitglieder, die die Kasse prüfen und darüber berichten; ihre Aufgaben bestimmt die Satzung. Sie gehören nicht zum Vorstand, den sie prüfen (§ 25 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: zwei Kassenprüfer prüfen 312 Buchungen stichprobenartig und empfehlen die Entlastung.

de.name: B2B – Firmenlastschrift
de.text: SEPA-Lastschrift nur für Zahler, die keine Verbraucher sind, ohne Rückgaberecht nach der Belastung (EPC B2B Rulebook). Der Zahler muss das Mandat vorher seiner Bank bestätigen.
de.example: Beispiel: Die Sparkasse als Fördermitglied zahlt 250 € Jahresbeitrag per B2B; ohne Bestätigung bei ihrer Bank wird der Einzug abgewiesen.

de.name: Basislastschrift oder Firmenlastschrift?
de.text: Die Firmenlastschrift (B2B) gibt es nur für Zahler, die keine Verbraucher sind, etwa Firmen oder Vereine als Mitglied. Der Zahler kann eine autorisierte Belastung nicht zurückgeben, muss das Mandat aber vorher seiner Bank melden, sonst wird der Einzug abgewiesen (EPC B2B Rulebook). Nimm B2B für Organisationen mit eigener Buchhaltung, sonst die Basislastschrift mit 8 Wochen Widerspruchsfrist.

de.name: Saldo
de.text: Differenz von Einnahmen und Ausgaben, etwa je Kategorie. Positiv heißt: mehr eingenommen als ausgegeben (§ 259 Abs. 1 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Kategorie Schützenfest: Einnahmen 3.100,00 €, Ausgaben 2.700,00 €, Saldo 400,00 €.

de.name: pain.008 – Datei für die Bank
de.text: Die XML-Datei mit allen Lastschriften eines Laufs, die du im Online-Banking hochlädst. Ihr Format legt das SEPA-Regelwerk fest; die Bank zieht danach die Beträge ein (EPC016-06).
de.example: Beispiel: eine Datei mit 104 Lastschriften über 7.488,00 €: einmal hochladen statt 104 Einzelaufträge.

de.name: Jährlich oder öfter abrechnen?
de.text: Jährlich abrechnen spart Arbeit, Porto und Bankgebühren je Lastschrift. Halb- oder vierteljährlich verteilt hohe Beiträge auf kleinere Beträge, vervielfacht aber Läufe und Mahnungen. Was gilt, legen Satzung oder Beitragsordnung fest (§ 58 Nr. 2 BGB).

de.name: § 26 BGB – Vorstand nach § 26 BGB
de.text: Die Personen, die den Verein gerichtlich und außergerichtlich vertreten; wer dazugehört, bestimmt die Satzung. Sie stehen im Vereinsregister (§§ 26, 64 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Laut Satzung vertreten 2 von 3 Vorstandsmitgliedern gemeinsam; die 7 Beisitzer des erweiterten Vorstands nicht.

de.name: Vorstand mit Pauschale vergüten?
de.text: Ohne Regel in der Satzung arbeitet der Vorstand unentgeltlich und bekommt nur seine Auslagen ersetzt (§ 27 Abs. 3 BGB). Eine Vergütung ohne Grundlage in der Satzung kann die Gemeinnützigkeit gefährden, weil Mittel satzungswidrig fließen (§ 55 Abs. 1 Nr. 1 AO). Kreuze das nur an, wenn eure Satzung eine Vergütung des Vorstands ausdrücklich erlaubt.

de.name: Buchwert
de.text: Anschaffungskosten abzüglich aller bisherigen Abschreibungen (§ 7 Abs. 1 EStG). Er sagt, mit welchem Wert ein Gegenstand noch im Verzeichnis steht, nicht, was er beim Verkauf brächte.
de.example: Beispiel: Festzelt für 6.000 €, nach 3 Jahren mit je 600 € Abschreibung: Buchwert 4.200 €.

de.name: Warum nur noch Storno statt Ändern oder Löschen?
de.text: Der ursprüngliche Inhalt einer Buchung muss feststellbar bleiben (§ 146 Abs. 4 AO), deshalb ist sie nach Ablauf des Folgemonats festgeschrieben (GoBD) und nur am Tag der Erfassung löschbar. Danach korrigierst du mit einem Storno: Eine Gegenbuchung hebt die falsche Buchung auf, beide bleiben sichtbar, und die richtige legst du neu an. Das ist umständlicher, macht aber jede Korrektur für Kassenprüfer und Finanzamt nachvollziehbar.

de.name: CAMT.053 – Elektronischer Kontoauszug
de.text: Kontoauszug als Datei im Format camt.053 nach ISO 20022, den fast jedes Online-Banking anbietet; anders als eine CSV-Datei enthält er eindeutige Angaben wie IBAN, Verwendungszweck und Endsaldo.
de.example: Beispiel: Auszug Oktober mit 37 Umsätzen und Endsaldo 4.812,55 € als XML-Datei.

de.name: Was prüfen die Kassenprüfer?
de.text: Kassenprüfer sieht das Gesetz nicht vor; ihre Aufgaben bestimmt die Satzung. Sie prüfen meist, ob jede Buchung belegt ist, die Bestände zu Kontoauszügen und Barkasse passen und Ausgaben durch Beschlüsse gedeckt sind. Ihr Bericht hilft der Mitgliederversammlung, über die Entlastung des Vorstands zu entscheiden, der Rechenschaft schuldet (§ 27 Abs. 3, §§ 666, 259 BGB).

de.name: Warum die Barkasse regelmäßig zählen, und zu zweit?
de.text: Die Barkasse muss jederzeit nachprüfbar sein: Gezähltes Geld und Kassenbuch sollen übereinstimmen (Kassensturzfähigkeit, § 146 Abs. 1 AO). Ein Zählprotokoll mit Stückelung belegt den Stand und macht eine Differenz mit Grund nachvollziehbar; eine zweite Person schützt den Kassierer vor Verdacht, kostet aber einen Termin mehr. Zähle mindestens zum Monats- und Jahresende und immer, wenn die Kasse übergeben wird.

de.name: Kassensturz
de.text: Zählen des Bargelds und Vergleich mit dem Bestand laut Kassenbuch. Die Kasse muss jederzeit so prüfbar sein (§ 146 Abs. 1 AO).
de.example: Beispiel: Gezählt 412,30 €, laut Kassenbuch 415,00 €: Die Differenz von 2,70 € wird mit Grund gebucht.

de.name: Quittung
de.text: Schriftliche Bestätigung, dass Geld empfangen wurde; wer Geld bekommt, muss sie auf Verlangen ausstellen (§ 368 BGB). Für die Kasse ist sie zugleich der Beleg zur Buchung.
de.example: Beispiel: Ein Mitglied zahlt 40 € Beitrag bar beim Schützenfest und bekommt Quittung Q-2026-0012.

de.name: Kassenbericht
de.text: Zusammenstellung von Anfangs- und Endbestand je Konto sowie Einnahmen und Ausgaben nach Kategorie für ein Geschäftsjahr. Mit ihm legt der Vorstand Rechenschaft gegenüber der Mitgliederversammlung ab (§ 27 Abs. 3, §§ 666, 259 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Kassenbericht 2026 auf vier Seiten, unterschrieben von beiden Kassenprüfern, liegt der Jahreshauptversammlung vor.

de.name: verkettetes Protokoll
de.text: Jeder Eintrag im Änderungsprotokoll enthält eine Prüfsumme seines Vorgängers; wird einer geändert oder gelöscht, passt die Kette nicht mehr. So bleibt nachweisbar, dass Änderungen nicht unterdrückt wurden (§ 146 Abs. 4 AO, GoBD).
de.example: Beispiel: Eintrag Nr. 1205 verweist auf die Prüfsumme von Nr. 1204; fehlt Nr. 1204, meldet die tägliche Prüfung „Nr. 1204 bis 1204 fehlen“.

de.name: Endbestand
de.text: Geld auf einem Konto am Ende des Zeitraums: Anfangsbestand plus Einnahmen minus Ausgaben, plus oder minus Umbuchungen. Er muss zum Kontoauszug passen (§ 259 Abs. 1 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: 4.250,00 € + 9.800,00 € − 8.900,00 € = 5.150,00 €: Der Kontoauszug zum 31. Dezember zeigt denselben Betrag.

de.name: Abgeschlossenes Jahr sperren, statt es zu ändern?
de.text: Nach dem Abschluss ist das Jahr gesperrt, damit der geprüfte Kassenbericht gilt und spätere Änderungen sichtbar bleiben (§ 146 Abs. 4 AO). Das schützt vor stillen Korrekturen, kostet aber Beweglichkeit: Fehler korrigierst du dann mit einer Gegenbuchung im laufenden Jahr. Schließe erst ab, wenn die Kassenprüfer fertig sind.

de.name: Welches Einzugsdatum wählen?
de.text: Das Einzugsdatum muss ein Bankarbeitstag sein und nach Ablauf der Vorabankündigung liegen (EPC016-06). Ein frühes Datum bringt das Geld schneller; ein Datum kurz nach dem Monatsanfang trifft oft gedeckte Konten und kann Rücklastschriften sparen. Zieh nicht vor der Fälligkeit der Rechnungen ein.

de.name: Sammelrechnung
de.text: Eine Rechnung an eine Untereinheit, die die Beiträge ihrer Mitglieder gesammelt zahlt, statt jedem Mitglied einzeln. Die Untereinheit zieht die Beiträge dann selbst ein (§ 58 Nr. 2 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Sammelrechnung Jägerzug: 18 Mitglieder, 1.296,00 €: Der Zug überweist einen Betrag für alle.

de.name: wGB – wirtschaftlicher Geschäftsbetrieb
de.text: Eine selbstständige, nachhaltige Tätigkeit, mit der der Verein Einnahmen erzielt und die über Vermögensverwaltung hinausgeht (§ 14 AO). Steuer fällt erst an, wenn diese Einnahmen einschließlich Umsatzsteuer 50.000 € im Jahr übersteigen (§ 64 Abs. 3 AO).
de.example: Beispiel: Getränkeverkauf am Schützenfest, 14.000,00 €: steuerpflichtiger Bereich, aber unter der Freigrenze.

de.name: Ausscheiden und feste Reihenfolge?
de.text: Scheidet aus, wer ein Pfand errungen hat, kommen mehr Schützen zu einem Preis. In fester Reihenfolge wird Pfand für Pfand geschossen, und HUBIplan bietet nach jedem Treffer gleich das nächste an. Welche Regel gilt, steht in der Schießordnung des Vereins (§ 25 BGB).

de.name: gewertete Schüsse
de.text: Die Schüsse, deren Ringe in den Wert eingehen; die übrigen sind Probe- oder Streichschüsse. Wie viele zählen, legt die Schießordnung des Vereins oder die DSB-Sportordnung fest.
de.example: Beispiel: 5 Schuss, davon 3 gewertet: Wer 9, 10, 8, 10, 7 schießt, hat mit den besten drei 29 Ringe, wenn die Ordnung die besten zählt.

de.name: Zehntelwertung
de.text: Jeder Schuss zählt mit einer Nachkommastelle, je näher an der Mitte, desto höher, auf dem Luftgewehr höchstens 10,9 (DSB-Sportordnung). Damit gibt es viel seltener einen Gleichstand als mit ganzen Ringen.
de.example: Beispiel: Ein Treffer 0,8 mm neben der Mitte der DSB-Luftgewehrscheibe zählt 10,6, einer 3 mm daneben 9,8.

de.name: Was bedeutet endgültig abschließen?
de.text: Danach sind Eingaben gesperrt, und nur endgültige Ergebnisse sind für Webseite und Ehrungen gedacht. Offene Stechen sperren den Abschluss, weil sonst Plätze ungeklärt blieben. Veröffentlichte Ergebnisse müssen sachlich richtig sein (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. d DSGVO), „Wieder öffnen“ bleibt für Korrekturen.

de.name: endgültig
de.text: Zustand nach dem Abschluss: Eingaben sind gesperrt, die Ergebnisse gelten. Nur endgültige Ergebnisse sind für Webseite und Ehrungen gedacht (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. d DSGVO).
de.example: Beispiel: Nach dem 2. Stechen schließt der Schießmeister ab, danach lässt sich kein Wert mehr ändern.

de.name: Gast
de.text: Teilnehmer, der nicht Mitglied ist; von ihm speichert HUBIplan nur Name und Verein (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. c DSGVO). Ob Gäste um Preise schießen dürfen, regelt die Ausschreibung.
de.example: Beispiel: „Gerd Gast, SV Nachbarort“ schießt 26 Ringe mit; für die Zugwertung kann er einer Untereinheit zugeordnet werden.

de.name: Loch in Loch
de.text: Mehrere Schüsse liegen so dicht, dass ihre Löcher ineinander übergehen; dann lässt sich aus dem Umriss nicht sicher ablesen, wo jedes Loch sitzt. Gewertet wird trotzdem jeder Schuss nach seinem Lochrand (DSB-Sportordnung), deshalb heißt es bei der Fotoerkennung „bitte prüfen“.
de.example: Beispiel: 5 Schuss in einen Spiegel ergeben ein einziges, gezacktes Loch etwa so groß wie 2 einzelne Löcher.

de.name: Innenzehner
de.text: Besonders guter Zehner: Auf der DSB-Luftgewehrscheibe ist es einer, der den weißen Zehnerpunkt ganz wegschießt (DSB-Sportordnung). Mehr Innenzehner entscheiden oft einen Gleichstand.
de.example: Beispiel: Ein Treffer 0,8 mm neben der Mitte ist ein Innenzehner, einer 2 mm daneben nur ein Zehner.

de.name: Losnummer
de.text: Nummer aus dem Hut, die beim Vogelschießen die Reihenfolge der Schützen bestimmt. Nachzügler ziehen eine noch freie Nummer; das Verfahren regelt die Schießordnung (§ 25 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Wer Los 7 zieht, schießt nach Nummer 6 und vor Nummer 8.

de.name: Wozu „Lose im Hut“?
de.text: Ohne diese Angabe zieht „Nummer ziehen“ nur bis zur Zahl der bisherigen Schützen, und ein Nachzügler bekommt meist die nächste Nummer. Mit der Zahl der Lose im Hut zieht HUBIplan wie aus einem echten Hut; wer lieber alle zugleich auslost, nimmt „Alle ohne Nummer auslosen“. Wie die Reihenfolge bestimmt wird, regelt die Schießordnung (§ 25 BGB).

de.name: außer Konkurrenz
de.text: Der Schütze schießt mit und erscheint in der Liste, bekommt aber keinen Platz und keinen Preis. Üblich etwa für Schießleiter oder Gäste aus Nachbarvereinen (§ 25 BGB, Schießordnung).
de.example: Beispiel: Der Schießleiter schießt 30 Ringe außer Konkurrenz; Platz 1 geht an die Beste mit 28.

de.name: Ausrichter
de.text: Verein oder Verband, der einen fremden Wettbewerb veranstaltet und wertet. Er legt Regeln und Preise fest (§ 25 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Beim Bezirksschießen 2027 ist der Bezirksverband der Ausrichter; ihr tragt nur eure Plätze ein, etwa Platz 3 mit 287 Ringen.

de.name: Eigener oder fremder Wettbewerb?
de.text: Beim eigenen Wettbewerb erfasst ihr Schützen und Werte selbst, und HUBIplan rechnet Plätze, Zugwertung und Stechen. Beim fremden tragt ihr nur ein, was der Ausrichter bekannt gegeben hat: Platz und Wert eurer Teilnehmer. Wie dort gewertet wird, regelt die Schießordnung des Ausrichters (§ 25 BGB).

de.name: Warum ist das Foto nur ein Vorschlag?
de.text: Bei mehreren Löchern ineinander, auf dunkler Unterlage oder knapp an einer Ringlinie kann die Erkennung irren; maßgeblich ist die Auswertung der Scheibe nach der DSB-Sportordnung bzw. eurer Schießordnung. Deshalb setzt das Foto die Treffer nur ins Antipp-Bild, und erst „Speichern“ übernimmt sie. Das Foto selbst wird nur ausgewertet und nie gespeichert, so entsteht kein Bild mit Bezug zum Schützen (Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. c DSGVO).

de.name: Spiegelausschnitte sammeln?
de.text: Echte, bestätigte Scheiben sind der einzige Weg zu prüfen, wie gut die Fotoerkennung wirklich ist; ohne sie wird nur an künstlichen Fotos gemessen. Gespeichert wird nur der Ausschnitt des Spiegels mit der Trefferlage, ohne Namen, Wettbewerb oder Uhrzeit, also ohne Bezug zu einer Person (Art. 4 Nr. 1 DSGVO). Schalte es ein, wenn ihr die Erkennung oft nutzt; ausschalten und alles löschen geht jederzeit.

de.name: Summe und Foto weichen ab, was gilt?
de.text: Gespeichert wird die eingegebene Summe; das Foto ist nur eine zweite Meinung, die Tippfehler und verzählte Ringe auffallen lässt. Bei einer Abweichung die Scheibe noch einmal ansehen, im Zweifel entscheidet die Aufsicht bzw. der Auswerter nach der DSB-Sportordnung oder eurer Schießordnung. „Treffer ansehen“ zeigt, wo die Erkennung die Löcher sieht.
de.section: Standmodus → Nur die Summe eingeben → Foto der Scheibe

de.name: Pfand
de.text: Teil des Vogels, für dessen Abschuss es einen Preis gibt, etwa Kopf, Flügel oder Schweif. Wer es herunterholt, hat das Pfand errungen; Pfänder und Preise legt die Schießordnung fest (§ 25 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Paul holt mit Schuss 54 den linken Flügel herunter und erhält den Flügelorden.

de.name: Preisplatz
de.text: Platz, für den es laut Ausschreibung einen Preis gibt, etwa die ersten drei. Nur hier braucht ein Gleichstand ein Stechen (§ 661 BGB).
de.example: Beispiel: Bei 3 Preisplätzen muss ein Gleichstand auf Platz 3 gestochen werden, einer auf Platz 4 nicht.

de.name: Wozu Preisplätze?
