en.text: If the club mainly promotes sport, local heritage, customs or leisure culture, membership fees are not deductible as donations (§ 10b(1) sentence 8 EStG); this usually applies to marksmen's, sports and carnival clubs. A receipt for them would be incorrect, and the club is liable for the lost tax (§ 10b(4) EStG). Only switch it on if the notice names other purposes, such as youth welfare or monument protection.

en.name: What must be documented for a donation in kind?
en.text: The value of the item is confirmed: for used items the market value (gemeiner Wert), for items from a business the withdrawal value (§ 10b(3) sentences 2 and 3 EStG). Describe the item precisely and keep documents on its value, such as a purchase receipt or expert opinion; without them the amount cannot be upheld in an audit. HUBIplan always issues donations in kind individually, never in a collective receipt.

en.name: Who is liable for an incorrect receipt?
en.text: Whoever issues an incorrect receipt intentionally or through gross negligence is liable for the lost tax, a flat 30% of the confirmed amount (§ 10b(4) EStG). The club keeps a duplicate of every receipt (§ 50(7) EStDV); HUBIplan stores the PDF for this. You correct errors by cancelling and issuing anew, not by changing.

en.name: How long does the tax office's notice last?
en.text: The club may only issue donation receipts as long as the exemption notice is at most 5 years old or the determination under § 60a AO at most 3 calendar years old (§ 63(5) AO). After that HUBIplan issues nothing until the new notice is entered. File the tax return in good time so that no donor has to wait for their receipt.

en.name: Donation receipt (Zuwendungsbestätigung)
en.text: Certificate from the club for a donation or a deductible fee, following the official template; only with it can the donor deduct the amount from tax (§ 10b(1) EStG, § 50(1) EStDV). Colloquially called Spendenquittung.
en.example: Example: Ms Muster donates 3 × €50 during the year: in January she receives a collective receipt for €150.

en.name: When is waiving expenses a donation?
en.text: Only if a claim to reimbursement existed beforehand by contract or constitution and was then waived; the claim must not already have been granted on condition of the waiver (§ 10b(3) sentences 5 and 6 EStG). Travel costs under a club travel expense rule are typical. Without such a rule, the waiver is not a deductible donation.

en.name: Confirm individually or once at year end?
en.text: The collective receipt combines all monetary donations of a donor in a calendar year and saves work and postage; the individual receipt comes immediately; both follow the official template (§ 50(1) EStDV). Up to €300 the bank statement together with a document from the club is often enough for the donor (§ 50(4) sentence 1 no. 2 EStDV). Common practice: large donations individually at once, everything else collectively in January.

en.name: Do we need a data protection officer?
en.text: It is mandatory if as a rule at least 20 people are constantly engaged in the automated processing of personal data (§ 38(1) BDSG) or the core activity requires it (Art. 37 GDPR). In small clubs this is rarely the case. Appointed voluntarily, a contact person still helps but takes time and expertise.

en.name: due (fällig)
en.text: From the due date the club may demand payment; it results from invoice date and payment term. At the latest 30 days later a member is in default if the invoice points this out (§§ 271, 286(3) BGB).
en.example: Example: invoice dated 1 March, payment term 14 days, so due on 15 March.

en.name: How long should the payment term be?
en.text: The payment term is the period from the invoice date to the due date. Without a reminder, a member is in default at the latest 30 days after the due date and receipt of the invoice, but consumers only if the invoice points this out (§ 286(3) BGB). A short term brings the money in sooner but means more reminders; a long term the opposite.

en.name: Reminder level (Mahnstufe)
en.text: Step in the reminder process reached a certain number of days after the due date, with its own text and possibly a charge. With the first reminder after the due date the member is in default (§ 286(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: payment reminder after 14 days without charge, 1st reminder after 28 days with €2.50 postage.

en.name: How many reminder levels and what charge?
en.text: More levels give late payers more opportunity but take time and delay expulsion or a court payment order. Charges beyond actual costs such as postage need a basis in the constitution or fee regulations (§§ 280(2), 286, 58 no. 2 BGB). Start with a friendly reminder without a charge and add levels if a lot is still open afterwards.

en.name: Reminder by email or letter?
en.text: By email the reminder is quick and free; by letter, receipt is easier to prove. A reminder only takes effect once it is received (§ 130(1), § 286(1) BGB). Email is usually enough for a first reminder; before expulsion or a court payment order a letter is safer.

en.name: E-invoice (E-Rechnung)
en.text: Invoice in a structured data format (XRechnung or ZUGFeRD) that a program can read; a PDF alone is not an e-invoice (§ 14(1) UStG). Since 2025 every business must be able to receive them, including a club with a commercial operation.
en.example: Example: the brewery sends invoice RE-2026-0815 for €1,190.00 as an XML file; HUBIplan reads amount and date and keeps the file as a document.

en.name: Why start and end of service?
en.text: Every invoice must state when the goods or services were supplied (§ 14(4) sentence 1 no. 6 UStG). For longer services such as a season’s rent the period states exactly that; for a single day start and end are the same. Without it the recipient cannot deduct input VAT.

en.name: Why work out the festival's day's takings backwards?
en.text: Without a cash register, not every sale is recorded individually; the takings result from closing balance minus float plus expenses paid in cash and withdrawals (open till, § 146(1) AO). This is simple but requires a complete count record at the end, because without it the takings cannot be proven. An electronic till would be more precise but needs a certified security device (§ 146a AO).
en.section: Finance → cash count → festival cash report

en.name: Event public or members only?
en.text: Public events reach guests and the press and can be subscribed to as a calendar. Internal events protect place, time and participants, for example for board meetings or youth gatherings (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Make public what should be known anyway, and keep everything else internal.

en.name: Exemption notice (Freistellungsbescheid)
en.text: Notice from the tax office that the club is exempt from corporation tax because of its non-profit status, usually as an annex to the corporation tax notice (§ 5(1) no. 9 KStG). It comes after the tax return, usually every three years.
en.example: Example: notice of 14 March 2024 for the years 2021 to 2023: receipts are possible until 14 March 2029.

en.name: Donation by waiver of expenses (Aufwandsspende)
en.text: Someone waives reimbursement of expenses that the club owes them; the waiver then counts as a monetary donation (§ 10b(3) sentences 5 and 6 EStG).
en.example: Example: 120 km trip to the association conference at €0.30 under the travel expense rule, so €36, and the treasurer confirms €36 as a donation.

en.name: Verbandsnr. – Association number (Verbandsnummer)
en.text: Number under which the umbrella association lists a member, so that reports and honours are assigned unambiguously. It is part of the data that goes to the umbrella association (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR).
en.example: Example: association no. 1920-0457: the same member, even if they change platoon.

en.name: Fee run (Beitragslauf)
en.text: Creates the fee invoices for a period all at once, according to each member's fee rules. The basis is the obligation to pay fees under the constitution or fee regulations (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).
en.example: Example: fee run 2026 with 142 invoices totalling €9,360.00: one click instead of 142 separate invoices.

en.name: Calendar year or different financial year?
en.text: The calendar year suits tax, because corporation tax is assessed by calendar year (§ 7(3) KStG). A different financial year suits clubs whose year follows a season or festival, but may require additional statements for the tax office. What the constitution says is decisive (§ 25 BGB).

en.name: Financial year (Geschäftsjahr)
en.text: The period for which the club accounts and presents a treasurer's report, usually the calendar year. The constitution can set a different year (§ 25 BGB).
en.example: Example: financial year 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026: the marksmen's festival in June falls at the end of the same year.

en.name: QR code on the invoice?
en.text: The QR code contains recipient, IBAN, amount and reference, so members scan it with their banking app instead of typing (EPC069-12). That avoids typos and wrong references; not every banking app reads it. It is worthwhile as soon as members pay by transfer rather than direct debit.

en.name: Should volunteers see the other names?
en.text: Anyone who can see who else is on duty can coordinate or share lifts. At the same time the club passes names on to other members, which should be limited to what is necessary (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Switch it on if coordination within the shift matters, otherwise leave it off.

en.name: IBAN / BIC – Account number and bank code (IBAN/BIC)
en.text: The IBAN is the international account number, 22 characters in Germany; the BIC identifies the bank and is no longer needed for payments within the SEPA area. A check digit in the IBAN catches most typing errors (EPC016-06).
en.example: Example: DE02 1203 0000 0000 2020 51: “DE” for Germany, “02” is the check digit.

en.name: Non-profit sphere (ideeller Bereich)
en.text: The actual club work for the statutory purpose, financed mainly by fees and donations. For non-profit clubs this area is tax-free (§ 52 AO, § 5(1) no. 9 KStG).
en.example: Example: membership fees €9,360.00 and donations €800.00 belong to the non-profit sphere.

en.name: Legal notice (Impressum)
en.text: Mandatory information about the provider of a website: name, address, authorised representatives, contact and, if registered, register and number (§ 5 DDG). It must be easy to reach from every page.
en.example: Example: an “Impressum” link in the footer of every page, no more than 2 clicks away.

en.name: Why approve an incoming invoice on the merits?
en.text: Whoever ordered or received the service confirms that it was delivered as invoiced; only then does the treasurer pay. Two people check what one would otherwise decide alone, and errors or duplicate invoices are caught earlier (GoBD, internal control system). In small clubs where one person does everything, the chair can give the approval.

en.name: Which invoice date for the fee run?
en.text: The payment term, and with it the period until default, runs from the invoice date (§ 286(3) BGB). A date shortly before sending is right; a backdated one shortens the members' term, a late one delays the money coming in.

en.name: Routing ID (Leitweg-ID)
en.text: Identifier that routes an e-invoice to the right office of a public authority; invoices to federal authorities must contain it (§ 5(1) ERechV). The authority states it with the order or the grant notice.
en.example: Example: the town gives routing ID 05162000-0001-12 for the hall rental; it goes in the “buyer reference” field.

en.name: Lending (Ausleihe)
en.text: Handing over an item for use free of charge, legally a loan for use (§ 598 BGB). The borrower returns it on time and is liable for damage, but not for normal wear (§§ 602, 604 BGB).
en.example: Example: the Jäger platoon borrows 20 beer table sets from 3 to 5 July; 2 come back with a broken leg, which is noted on return.

en.name: SEPA mandate (SEPA-Mandat)
en.text: The payer's permission for the club to collect amounts from their account, and at the same time the instruction to their bank to honour the direct debit (EPC016-06). Without a valid mandate the club may not collect (§ 675j(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: 104 of 142 members have granted a mandate: their fee arrives without a transfer.

en.name: Expired mandate (Mandat verfallen)
en.text: A mandate expires if no direct debit has been collected on it for 36 months. After that a new mandate is needed (EPC016-06).
en.example: Example: last collection in May 2023, then expired in May 2026: the member must sign again for the next fee.

en.name: Mandate reference (Mandatsreferenz)
en.text: Unique identifier of a mandate at the club, up to 35 characters. It appears on every direct debit and pre-notification so that the payer can match it (EPC016-06).
en.example: Example: mandate reference M-0042: on the bank statement the member recognises which mandate the collection belongs to.

en.name: Which notice period and form for the invitation?
en.text: The constitution sets the form and notice period of the invitation (§ 58 no. 4 BGB); enter exactly those values here. Every matter to be decided must already be named in the invitation, otherwise the resolution is invalid (§ 32(1) sentence 2 BGB). An invitation sent too late makes every resolution of the meeting open to challenge.

en.name: Who approves the minutes?
en.text: The constitution sets how resolutions are recorded and who signs the minutes (§ 58 no. 4 BGB), usually the chair and the minute-taker. The register court requires a copy after a board election or a change to the constitution (§§ 67, 71 BGB). Once approved, the minutes can no longer be changed, so check them together beforehand.

en.name: Motions from members before the meeting?
en.text: The meeting can only safely decide on a motion that was announced with the invitation (§ 32(1) sentence 2 BGB). A deadline for motions gives the board time to announce motions it has received but rules out spontaneous ones. Take the deadline from the constitution; if it says nothing, the board decides.

en.name: Allow voting by proxy?
en.text: By law the right to vote is personal and cannot be handed to anyone else (§ 38 sentence 2 BGB). The constitution may allow proxies (§ 40 BGB); this helps members who cannot attend but risks a few people collecting many votes. Only switch it on if your constitution provides for proxies.

en.name: Minimum attendance for a quorum?
en.text: The law sets no minimum: a properly convened meeting can pass resolutions however many attend (§ 32 BGB). A minimum protects against decisions by small groups but can paralyse the meeting if too few turn up. Only enter a value if your constitution requires one (§ 40 BGB).

en.name: Membership type (Mitgliedsart)
en.text: Group of members with the same rules, such as “active”, “passive” or “youth”. It determines the fee, reporting to the umbrella association and whether the time counts towards length of membership (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).
en.example: Example: “Passive” with an annual fee of €36.00 instead of €72.00 for “Active”: whoever no longer takes an active part pays half.

en.name: When is a membership type “active”?
en.text: Active members are counted separately, for example for the association fee per active member and in the development figures; passive members often pay less and take less part in club life. A fine-grained division helps with reporting and fees but takes upkeep if members change often. Follow the constitution or fee regulations, which set out which groups exist and what they pay (§§ 25, 58 no. 2 BGB).

en.name: Which periods count towards length of membership?
en.text: If a type counts towards duration, its periods feed into anniversaries and honours. In favour: loyalty is also recognised as a passive member; against: if your honours regulations only count active years. Adopt the rule from the constitution or honours regulations so that honours are calculated the same for everyone (§ 25 BGB).

en.name: Which members to report to the umbrella association?
en.text: The club passes reported members with their data to the umbrella association, which then calculates its fees. Every transfer needs a legal basis and should be limited to what is necessary (Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 6(1) GDPR). Report the types that the umbrella association's constitution requires, and no more.

en.name: Length of membership (Mitgliedsdauer)
en.text: Total of the periods in which someone was a member, without gaps between leaving and rejoining. Only membership types marked “counts towards duration” count (§ 25 BGB).
en.example: Example: 1998 to 2010 and again from 2014 gives 24 years in total in 2026; the 25-year anniversary follows in 2027.

en.name: Statement of assets (Vermögensübersicht)
en.text: List of accounts, fixed assets, receivables and liabilities at the end of the year. It is part of the board’s accounting to the general meeting (§ 27(3), § 666 BGB).
en.example: Example: €8,000 accounts + €4,200 assets + €300 unpaid fees − €1,190 unpaid invoices = €11,310.

en.name: Open till (offene Ladenkasse)
en.text: Cash box without a cash register, for example at the drinks stand; the day's takings are worked back at the end from the counted balance (§ 146(1) AO). This requires a count record.
en.example: Example: closing balance €1,850.00, float €200.00, ice cream paid in cash €50.00: day's takings €1,700.00.

en.name: Opening balance with cut-off date?
en.text: The opening balance is the account balance on the cut-off date from which you book in HUBIplan, usually the start of the financial year. Take it from the bank statement or the last treasurer's report; an estimated value is quicker but carries through every later report as a difference. The board's duty to account requires a complete statement of income and expenses (§ 259(1) BGB).

en.name: Opening balance (Anfangsbestand)
en.text: Money in an account or the cash box at the start of the period, usually the previous year's closing balance. It is the starting point of every cash calculation (§ 259(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: opening balance €4,250.00 on 1 January: this much was in the current account before the year began.

en.name: Objection (Widerspruch)
en.text: A member can unsubscribe from information emails such as circulars; HUBIplan then no longer sends them by email. An objection to advertising by email is possible at any time (Art. 21(2) and (3) GDPR).
en.example: Example: 6 of 120 members have unsubscribed: the circular goes to 114 addresses.

en.name: open (offen)
en.text: The part of an invoice not yet paid: invoice amount minus all recorded payments. The member still owes this remainder (§ 362(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: invoice €72.00, paid €36.00, open €36.00: half is still missing.

en.name: overdue (überfällig)
en.text: An invoice whose due date has passed and on which something is still open. Whether the member is already in default also depends on a reminder or a note on the invoice (§ 286 BGB).
en.example: Example: 9 of 142 invoices overdue, together €648.00: time for the reminder.

en.name: What belongs in a written mandate?
en.text: A mandate states, among other things, payer, IBAN, creditor ID, mandate reference, date and signature (EPC016-06). Keep the original as long as you collect on it, and afterwards as long as queries are possible; without proof, the club must refund a disputed direct debit up to 13 months later (§§ 675u, 676b(2) BGB). HUBIplan stores mandates from the member area itself.
en.section: Direct debit → mandates → record written mandate

en.name: Report by name or only numbers?
en.text: Numbers are enough for fees and statistics; the association needs reports by name, for example for honours or eligibility to compete. Names may only be passed on if the constitution or membership of the association provides for it (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and no more than necessary (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Also name the association as a recipient in the privacy notice.

en.name: Personal data shared or per unit?
en.text: Maintained jointly, an address changes everywhere at once, so data stays correct (Art. 5(1)(d) GDPR). In return several units see and change the same data, which requires clear agreements on responsibility (Art. 26 GDPR). Separate copies per unit separate responsibility but lead to diverging versions.

en.name: Photos only with consent?
en.text: A photo makes recognition on the ID card easier but shows a person recognisably; for this the club usually relies on their consent (§ 22 KUG, Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). Consent is voluntary and can be withdrawn at any time, after which the photo must go (Art. 7(3) GDPR). The ID card also works without a photo, so only ask if it really helps.

en.name: How many days of pre-notification?
en.text: Before each collection you announce amount and date, under the SEPA rulebook 14 calendar days in advance unless otherwise agreed (EPC016-06). A shorter period speeds up the run but only applies if it is stated in the mandate or the fee terms. Without such an agreement, use 14 days.

en.name: Pre-notification (Vorabankündigung)
en.text: Notice to the payer of the amount and date of a collection, 14 calendar days in advance unless otherwise agreed (EPC016-06). It can also be on the invoice or apply once for several identical collections.
en.example: Example: collection on 15 March, notice by 1 March at the latest: the member can make sure the account is in funds.

en.name: Pro rata fee when joining during the period?
en.text: Pro rata means: whoever joins during the period pays per started month. That seems fair and makes joining in autumn easier, but gives odd amounts that need explaining. If the constitution or fee regulations say nothing, the board should decide on a rule and apply it equally to all (§ 58 no. 2 BGB).

en.name: Create events and series?
en.text: If you assign bookings to an event, you see its result and can compare it over the years in a series. This shows which festival pays for itself and provides figures for the limit in the commercial operation (§ 64(3) AO). It is worth the effort for festivals with many bookings; for small occasions the category is enough.

en.name: Special-purpose operation (Zweckbetrieb)
en.text: A business operation that directly fulfils the statutory purpose and cannot be achieved otherwise. It remains tax-privileged like the non-profit sphere (§§ 64(1), 65 AO).
en.example: Example: entry fees for the club competition, €650.00: the event itself serves the club's purpose.

en.name: Document (Beleg)
en.text: Evidence for an entry, e.g. invoice, receipt or bank statement. Accounting documents must be kept for eight years (§ 147(1) no. 4, (3) AO).
en.example: Example: entry 2026-0117 “Festival drinks” €412.30 with the scanned invoice from the drinks supplier.

en.name: Show VAT on the receipt?
en.text: Only if the payment belongs to a VAT-liable area and the club is not a small business (§ 19 UStG). Whoever shows tax without being entitled to owes it to the tax office anyway (§ 14c(2) UStG). Up to €250 a small-amount invoice with the tax rate instead of the tax amount is enough (§ 33 UStDV).

en.name: A document for every entry?
en.text: Without a document an entry cannot be proven at the cash audit or to the tax office; the principle is “no entry without a document” (GoBD). Accounting documents must be kept for eight years (§ 147(1) no. 4, (3) AO). Uploading the document straight away with the entry takes a moment but saves searching before the closing.

en.name: Register court and register number (Registergericht, Registernummer)
en.text: A registered association is entered in the register of associations at the local court, under a number with “VR”. Both belong in the legal notice (§ 21 BGB, § 5(1) no. 4 DDG).
en.example: Example: Amtsgericht Neuss, VR 1234.

en.name: Why does reopening a closing need a reason?
en.text: A closed year is the basis for the cash audit and discharge; if it is reopened, it must remain visible what applied before (§ 146(4) AO, GoBD). That is why the old state is kept with reason, person and time, and when closing again you see the differences. Only reopen a closing for real errors, such as a forgotten document, and inform the cash auditors.

en.name: Reserve (Rücklage)
en.text: Part of the funds that the club sets aside for a purpose without moving money (§ 62 AO). It is then no longer freely available.
en.example: Example: €3,000.00 of €8,000.00 in the accounts are tied up as “Reserve marquee”; €5,000.00 is freely available.

en.name: When does the club need a reserve?
en.text: A tax-privileged club must in principle use its funds by the end of the year after next (§ 55(1) no. 5 AO); whoever saves for a project, such as a tent or an anniversary festival, creates a reserve for it (§ 62(1) AO). Reserves make saving traceable but tie up money and need a decision with a purpose. Small clubs below the income limit in § 55(1) no. 5 AO do not have to use funds promptly, but a reserve still helps with planning.

en.name: Responsible for the content (Verantwortlich für den Inhalt)
en.text: Person who takes responsibility for journalistic and editorial content such as reports and news, with name and address (§ 18(2) MStV). Usually the chair or the press officer.
en.example: Example: “Responsible under § 18(2) MStV: Erika Muster, Hauptstraße 1, 41468 Neuss”.

en.name: Result (Ergebnis)
en.text: All income minus all expenses of a period or event, without transfers. A negative result means the club paid in from reserves or balances (§ 259(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: result 2026: +€900.00: the club took in €900.00 more than it spent during the year.

en.name: When may old treasury data go?
en.text: Documents must be kept for 8 years, books and closings for 10 years, counted from the end of the calendar year (§ 147(3) and (4) AO); after that data protection requires deleting personal data (Art. 5(1)(e) GDPR). Cleaning up protects former members and donors but is final. Do not clean up while taxes for those years can still be assessed, for example during a tax audit, because the period does not expire until then (§ 147(3) AO).

en.name: Retention period (Aufbewahrungsfrist)
en.text: Time for which treasury records must be kept: documents 8 years, books and closings 10 years, each from the end of the calendar year (§ 147(3) and (4) AO).
en.example: Example: documents from 2025 may be deleted from 1 Jan 2034, the 2025 entries anonymised from 1 Jan 2036.

en.name: Returned direct debit (Rücklastschrift)
en.text: A direct debit that comes back, for example because the account has insufficient funds or the member objects; a member can object to an authorised direct debit up to eight weeks after the debit (§ 675x(2) and (4) BGB, EPC rulebook). Bank charges are often added.
en.example: Example: €60 fee collected on 1 March, returned on 6 March with reason “AM04” (insufficient funds) and a €3 charge.

en.name: Grant only the necessary permissions?
en.text: Every permission opens up personal data; grant only what a role needs for its task (Art. 5(1)(f), Art. 25(2) GDPR). Broad rights are convenient when few people do everything, but increase mistakes and damage if sign-in details are lost. Better create one more role, such as “Treasury” without member management, than one catch-all role for everyone.

en.name: Who represents the unit under § 26 BGB?
en.text: Whoever represents the unit under § 26 BGB concludes contracts for it and appears in the register of associations and in the legal notice (§ 5 DDG). Tick this only for roles that the constitution names as the board within the meaning of § 26 BGB, not for the extended board. Many authorised representatives make the club flexible but increase the risk of unwanted obligations.

en.name: Direct debit or bank transfer?
en.text: With direct debit the fee arrives on time and without reminders; for this you need a creditor ID, mandates and a pre-notification. Payers can return a direct debit within eight weeks without giving a reason, which can cost the club bank charges (§ 675x BGB, EPC016-06). The more members pay, the more work direct debit saves; with few, bank transfer is often enough.

en.name: Simple majority (einfache Mehrheit)
en.text: A motion is carried if it has more yes than no votes; abstentions do not count (§ 32(1) sentence 3 BGB). The constitution may provide otherwise.
en.example: Example: 23 yes, 20 no, 9 abstentions: the motion is carried although only 23 of the 52 present agreed.

en.name: Simplified proof of donation (vereinfachter Zuwendungsnachweis)
en.text: Up to €300 the bank statement is enough for the donor instead of a donation receipt, if they also keep a document from the club with the purpose and details of the tax exemption (§ 50(4) sentence 1 no. 2(b) EStDV). The club may still issue a receipt.
en.example: Example: €50 donation by transfer: the bank statement and the donation slip from the club booklet are enough.

en.name: Small business (VAT exemption)
en.text: Anyone with at most €25,000 turnover in the previous year and at most €100,000 in the current year does not charge or pay VAT, but cannot deduct input tax either (§ 19 UStG, limits since 2025). Membership fees and donations do not count; income from purpose-related and commercial operations does.
en.example: Example: €18,000 from festival sales and advertising in the previous year: the club remains a small business.

en.name: When to split a booking?
en.text: One payment can concern several categories, for example the takings of a festival with admission and drinks sales. Only the income of the commercial operation counts towards the €50,000 limit (§ 64(3) AO), so each part belongs in its own category and thus its own tax area. Split when the categories differ; otherwise one booking is enough.

en.name: Amendment to the constitution (Satzungsänderung)
en.text: Needs three quarters of the votes cast, and a change of the club’s purpose the consent of all members, unless the constitution says otherwise (§§ 33, 40 BGB). For a registered club it only takes effect once entered in the register of associations (§ 71 BGB).
en.example: Example: 40 yes, 12 no, 5 abstentions: 40 of 52 votes cast is 77 %, more than three quarters, so carried.

en.name: Determination under § 60a AO (Feststellung nach § 60a AO)
en.text: Notice that the constitution meets the requirements for non-profit status (§ 60a AO). Newly founded clubs receive it before there is a first exemption notice.
en.example: Example: determination of 2 May 2025: HUBIplan issues receipts until 2 May 2028.

en.name: Assign categories to tax areas?
en.text: Non-profit clubs separate the non-profit sphere, asset management, special-purpose operations and commercial operations, because only the last can be taxable (§§ 14, 64, 65 AO). The assignment makes the tax return easier but requires clean categories. Switch it on as soon as the club has income from sales, festivals or advertising; if this stays at or below €50,000 a year including VAT, no corporation or trade tax is due on it (§ 64(3) AO, since 2026; previously €45,000).

en.name: Trainer allowance (Übungsleiterfreibetrag)
en.text: Tax-free up to €3,300 a year (from 2026) for part-time teaching, coaching or artistic work, for example as a trainer or conductor, in the non-profit area (§ 3 no. 26 EStG). The amount applies per person across all payers together.
en.example: Example: the youth coach receives 12 × €250 = €3,000 a year; that is below €3,300 and stays tax-free.

en.name: Transfer (Umbuchung)
en.text: Money moves between two of your own accounts, for example from the cash box to the current account. It is neither income nor expense and does not change the result (§ 259(1) BGB).
en.example: Example: €600.00 cash takings from the festival paid into the current account: cash box −€600.00, current account +€600.00, result unchanged.

en.name: Should the sub-unit manage itself?
en.text: Self-managed, the sub-unit's role holders work with their own accounts and relieve the board above. But every additional account means more people see member data, and someone has to maintain the permissions (Art. 5(1)(f), Art. 32 GDPR). Switch it on if the sub-unit really has its own tasks, such as looking after members or planning events.

en.name: Sub-unit separate for tax purposes?
en.text: Departments, platoons or groups with their own cash book are almost always part of the club for tax purposes. Their income is added up there, including for the tax-free limit of the commercial operation; a club may not split itself into departments to stay below it (§ 64 (4) AO). Only switch this on if the unit is a club of its own with its own tax number and its own exemption notice.

en.name: USt – VAT (Umsatzsteuer)
en.text: Tax on supplies and services in return for payment, normally 19%, reduced 7% (§ 12 UStG). Genuine membership fees are not covered (UStAE 1.4).
en.example: Example: advertising board for €500.00 net, with 19% VAT €595.00 gross.

en.name: USt-IdNr. – Tax number and VAT ID (Steuernummer, USt-IdNr.)
en.text: The tax number is issued by the tax office, the VAT ID by the Federal Central Tax Office. One of them belongs on every invoice with VAT (§ 14(4) sentence 1 no. 2 UStG).
en.example: Example: VAT ID DE123456789: “DE” and nine digits.

en.name: Show VAT on invoices?
en.text: Genuine membership fees that everyone pays for the club's purpose are not a taxable supply; no VAT belongs on them (UStAE 1.4). You only show tax for services in return for payment, such as sales or advertising, and only if the club is not a small business (§ 19 UStG: previous year up to €25,000, current year up to €100,000). Whoever shows tax without owing it owes it anyway (§ 14c UStG); if in doubt, ask the tax office or a tax adviser.

en.name: Volunteer allowance (Ehrenamtspauschale)
en.text: Tax-free up to €960 a year (from 2026) for part-time work in the non-profit area, for example as treasurer or groundskeeper (§ 3 no. 26a EStG). It cannot be claimed on top of the trainer allowance for the same activity.
en.example: Example: the groundskeeper receives €80 a month, €960 a year; anything more would be taxable.

en.name: What is alternative text for?
en.text: Screen readers read it out to blind visitors, and it appears if an image does not load (WCAG 2.2, criterion 1.1.1). Describe in one sentence what can be seen and what of it is important. Pure decoration such as a pattern needs no text.

en.name: What does the website show without consent?
en.text: Names of members on a public page need a legal basis, usually their consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). “Omit” is safest; a placeholder keeps lists such as the list of kings complete. You maintain consents and objections in the member record under “Publication”.

en.name: Should search engines index the website?
en.text: With indexing, interested people find the club via search engines; without it the site can only be reached via its address. In return, names on the site then also appear in search results (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). Switch it on once the legal notice, privacy policy and name format are right.

en.name: How much of the name does the website show?
en.text: The full name makes board members and title holders clearly identifiable; “First name L.” protects more because search engines find less (Art. 5(1)(c) GDPR). For roles with an external function such as the board, the full name is usual. For the chronicle and titles the short form is often enough.

en.name: Which photos may go on the website?
en.text: Pictures of identifiable people need their consent (§ 22 KUG, Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). Exceptions apply, for example, to pictures of gatherings and parades where the crowd is in the foreground (§ 23(1) no. 3 KUG). If in doubt, use group pictures of public appearances and ask for close-ups.

en.name: Why does HUBIplan fetch the posts itself?
en.text: An embedded Instagram or Facebook post sends data to Meta when the page is opened; for this the page would need consent (§ 25 TDDDG), and the club would be jointly responsible (CJEU, C-40/17). HUBIplan therefore fetches the posts itself every 30 minutes and shows them without a connection to Meta. The price: new posts appear with some delay, and each unit needs its own Meta app.
